entries.name: BlockRun US Stock Spot Price
entries.description: Real-time spot price for a US-listed equity by ticker symbol, sourced from Pyth. Returns the latest price with a confidence interval and publish time. Symbol is a path segment.

usage.callShape: GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/usstock/price/{SYMBOL} — symbol is a PATH segment (e.g. /usstock/price/AAPL). Optional query param session=regular|extended. No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key.
usage.outputShape: symbol, category, price, confidence, publishTime (epoch seconds), timestamp (ISO), assetType, feedId, source ('pyth')
quirks: Symbol is a PATH segment, not a query param (/usstock/price/AAPL).
Two equivalent path aliases on the same origin: /usstock/price/{SYM} and /stocks/us/price/{SYM}; the *.a.run.app host is the same Cloud Run backend behind blockrun.ai.
Pyth-sourced: includes a `confidence` band (price uncertainty), not a bid/ask.
publishTime is Unix epoch SECONDS; timestamp is the ISO equivalent.
No mandatory params — calling with just the symbol returns 200.
usage.guide: Real-time spot price for a US-listed equity by ticker symbol, sourced from Pyth. Returns the latest price with a confidence interval and publish time. Symbol is a path segment. entries.name: BlockRun US Stock OHLC History
entries.description: Historical daily (or intraday) OHLC bars for a US-listed equity over a time range, sourced from Pyth. Symbol is a path segment; the time window is set via from/to query params.

usage.callShape: GET https://blockrun.ai/api/v1/usstock/history/{SYMBOL}?from={epochSeconds}&to={epochSeconds}&resolution=D — symbol is a PATH segment; from/to/resolution are query params. No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key.
usage.outputShape: symbol, resolution, from, to, source ('pyth'), category, bars[] each {t (epoch seconds), o, h, l, c, v}
quirks: ALWAYS pass `from` (Unix epoch SECONDS) before paying. OpenAPI marks it optional, but historically calling /history/{SYM} with no query params returns HTTP 400 {error:'Missing or invalid `from`'} AND STILL CHARGES $0.001. Verified call included from+to.
Also pass `to` (epoch seconds) to bound the range; defaults to now if omitted.
Symbol is a PATH segment, not a query param.
resolution defaults to 'D' (daily); other values: 1,5,15,60,240,D,W.
Volume field `v` is ALWAYS 0 (Pyth feed carries no volume).
Two equivalent path aliases: /usstock/history/{SYM} and /stocks/us/history/{SYM}.
Optional session=regular|extended query param.

entries.name: Stock Trends Weekly
entries.description: Stock Trends historical weekly price series and trend indicators for equities. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.stocktrends.com/v1/prices/history?symbol=AAPL&exchange=Q (query params: either symbol_exchange OR symbol+exchange; exchange is a single-letter code)
usage.outputShape: Body is JSON. Weekly price history series returned on a successful 200 (not reached within attempt cap). On error, body.detail holds {error, message} or a string explaining the param problem.
quirks: Registry inputSchema was null — required query params discovered via error hints.
MUST provide query params: either ?symbol_exchange=... OR ?symbol=AAPL&exchange=Q. With no params it returns 400 missing_required_param.
exchange is a SINGLE-LETTER code, not a name. Valid: ['A','B','I','N','Q','T']. Q=NASDAQ, N=NYSE. Passing exchange=NASDAQ returns 400 'Invalid exchange'.
x402 charges per call even on 400 param errors — get the params right before paying. Each malformed call costs $0.0075.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.stocktrends.com/v1/prices/history with query params symbol (ticker, e.g. AAPL) and exchange as a single-letter code (Q for NASDAQ, N for NYSE; valid set ['A','B','I','N','Q','T']), or alternatively a combined symbol_exchange param. Pay via x402 USDC on Base ($0.0075/call, no API key, auth=none). Read the weekly price/trend series from the JSON body. Note: every call is charged including 400 param errors, so format params correctly first — exchange must be the letter code, NOT the exchange name.

usage.callShape: GET https://stablefinance.dev/api/earnings?ticker=AAPL&limit=1 (x402, no body).
usage.outputShape: earnings[].{report_period,fiscal_period,ticker,source_type,filing_date,filing_window,filing_url,accession_number, quarterly:{revenue,revenue_surprise,earnings_per_share,eps_surprise,gross_margin,operating_income,net_income,free_cash_flow,...}, signals[].{type,metric,period,headline,details}}
quirks: Results under earnings[] (a list).
Each entry carries a rich quarterly{} object plus a signals[] array of human-readable headlines (EPS_BEAT, MARGIN_EXPANSION, GUIDANCE_RAISED, etc.).
A single quarter may appear multiple times (one per source_type, e.g. 8-K then 10-Q) -- dedupe on report_period if needed.
Omit ticker for the cross-ticker feed.
usage.guide: Most-recent earnings results for a ticker with YoY changes, estimate surprises, and derived signals (margin expansion, EPS beat, guidance). Omit ticker for the cross-ticker feed. GET https://stablefinance.dev/api/earnings?ticker=AAPL&limit=1 (x402, no body). Output: earnings[].{report_period,fiscal_period,ticker,source_type,filing_date,filing_window,filing_url,accession_number, quarterly:{revenue,revenue_surprise,earnings_per_share,eps_surprise,gross_margin,operating_income,net_income,free_cash_flow,...}, signals[].{type,metric,period,headline,details}}

entries.name: StableFinance Central Bank Interest Rates
entries.description: Current policy rates for major central banks (FED, ECB, BOJ, BOE, BOC, RBA, PBOC, SNB, RBI, BOK).

usage.callShape: GET https://stablefinance.dev/api/macro/interest-rates/snapshot?bank=FED (x402, no body). bank is a required query param per schema.
usage.outputShape: interest_rates[].{bank,name,rate,date}
quirks: GOTCHA: schema marks bank required, but the snapshot response IGNORES the bank filter and returns ALL central banks' current rates as a list -- you must client-side filter by bank code (FED/ECB/BOJ/...).
Get valid bank codes from /api/macro/interest-rates/banks; historical series from /api/macro/interest-rates.
Output under interest_rates[] (a list, not a single object despite 'snapshot').
usage.guide: Current policy rates for major central banks (FED, ECB, BOJ, BOE, BOC, RBA, PBOC, SNB, RBI, BOK). GET https://stablefinance.dev/api/macro/interest-rates/snapshot?bank=FED (x402, no body). bank is a required query param per schema. Output: interest_rates[].{bank,name,rate,date}

entries.name: StableFinance Stock Screener
entries.description: Screen US companies by fundamental criteria (gross_margin, revenue_growth, sector, etc.) using field/operator/value filters.

usage.callShape: POST https://stablefinance.dev/api/financials/search/screener with JSON body {filters:[{field,operator,value}], limit} (x402). THE ONLY POST endpoint -- takes a JSON body, not query params.
usage.outputShape: results[].{ticker, <requested_metric>} (each result echoes ticker plus the filtered metric value, e.g. results[].gross_margin)
quirks: POST with JSON body (all other StableFinance ops are GET with query params).
filters is REQUIRED, must have >=1 item; each filter = {field, operator, value}.
operator enum: eq|gt|gte|lt|lte|in (value can be string/number/boolean/array; use 'in' with an array).
limit 1..100 (optional).
Get valid field names + operators from /api/financials/search/screener/filters.
Results are minimal (ticker + matched metric) -- drill down with /api/financial-metrics or /api/prices/snapshot per the guidance.
usage.guide: Screen US companies by fundamental criteria (gross_margin, revenue_growth, sector, etc.) using field/operator/value filters. POST https://stablefinance.dev/api/financials/search/screener with JSON body {filters:[{field,operator,value}], limit} (x402). THE ONLY POST endpoint -- takes a JSON body, not query params. Output: results[].{ticker, <requested_metric>} (each result echoes ticker plus the filtered metric value, e.g. results[].gross_margin)

entries.name: AgentMarket
entries.description: Real-time market data via x402 — stock price quotes (price, % change, 52-week high/low), major market indices & macro indicators (S&P 500, NASDAQ, VIX, 10Y treasury, oil, gold, USD/EUR), and institutional SEC 13F holdings. No API key.

usage.callShape: GET https://market.memoryapi.org/x402/market/quote?symbol=AAPL (x402-gated; expects a stock symbol query param)
usage.outputShape: unknown — service is down, no successful response observed
quirks: Host market.memoryapi.org returns 502 Bad Gateway (nginx) on EVERY route including root / and sibling /x402/market/indices — the upstream backend is dead.
No 402 payment challenge is served while down, so a paid call cannot even be constructed.
Earlier registry probe (2026-06-02) saw 402 payable; service has since gone offline.
DO NOT pay until a fresh pre-flight returns 402 again.
usage.guide: This endpoint is currently broken. The host market.memoryapi.org returns 502 Bad Gateway on all routes (quote, indices, root), so the backend behind nginx is down. When live, it is an x402-gated GET that returns real-time stock quotes; you would call GET /x402/market/quote with a symbol query param (e.g. ?symbol=AAPL) and pay ~$0.001 USDC. Re-test with an unpaid pre-flight first: only pay if it returns HTTP 402 with a valid payment challenge — do not pay while it returns 502.

entries.name: x402stock FDA Catalysts
entries.description: FDA regulatory catalysts for a pharma/biotech/medtech company, from openFDA: drug recalls & approvals plus device 510(k) clearances, PMA approvals & recalls — one call across 5 openFDA datasets with recent items, match totals, and official FDA record links. Verified call company=Medtronic (a medtech company) returned 0 drug items but rich device data: 1580 clearances matched (10 returned), 12808 PMA approvals matched (10 returned), 1258 recalls matched (10 returned).

company.description: Company / applicant / sponsor / firm name to fuzzy-match across openFDA drug and device datasets, e.g. 'Medtronic', 'Pfizer'.

limit.description: Max items returned per section per dataset (5 datasets: drug recalls, drug approvals, device clearances, device approvals, device recalls).

inputSchema.description: All query params, no request body.

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/fda?company=<name>[&limit=1-50] — company is a REQUIRED query param (free-text, 2-120 chars, fuzzy-matched across openFDA drug+device datasets); limit is optional (default 10, max 50). No request body. x402 exact scheme, Base USDC (eip155:8453) — this endpoint's 402 also advertises an alternate MPP/Tempo rail, not used here.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous flat JSON on the paid 200: { source:'fda' (const), as_of:<ISO timestamp>, company:'Medtronic', drug:{ recalls:{total_matched,count,items:[{date,status,classification,product_type,product_description,reason,firm,recall_number,voluntary_mandated}]}, approvals:{total_matched,count,items:[{application_number,sponsor,approval_date,brand_names:[],active_ingredients:[],dosage_form,route,submission_class,review_priority,url}]} }, device:{ clearances:{total_matched,count,items:[{k_number,device_name,decision,decision_date,clearance_type,product_code,advisory_committee,date_received,applicant,url}]}, approvals:{total_matched,count,items:[{pma_number,supplement_number,trade_name,generic_name,decision_date,decision_code,supplement_type,advisory_committee,product_code,applicant,url}]}, recalls:{same shape as drug.recalls} }, attribution:'Source: openFDA, U.S. Food and Drug Administration' }. Item count per section is capped by `limit` (default 10); total_matched is the true openFDA match count regardless of limit.
quirks: company is a fuzzy free-text match against openFDA applicant/sponsor/firm fields across 5 datasets at once (drug recalls, drug approvals, device 510(k) clearances, device PMA approvals, device recalls) — a company's results can be lopsided: the verified call for company=Medtronic (a medtech company) returned 0 drug recalls/approvals but rich device data (1580 clearances matched, 12808 PMA approvals matched, 1258 recalls matched); a pure pharma company would likely show the inverse.
`limit` (optional, default 10, max 50) caps count/items.length per section, independently for each of the 5 datasets — total_matched is the true openFDA match count regardless of limit.
Every per-item field is nullable (openFDA records are frequently incomplete) — expect null dates/urls/names on some items.

Served through the newer `agents.x402stock.xyz` payment gateway — a different host from the existing 'x402stock Quote'/'x402stock Snapshot' entries (bare x402stock.xyz), but the same brand/provider and, per its own openapi.json, a transparent proxy in front of x402stock's own upstream API (call paths through agents.x402stock.xyz, not the bare domain, per its own docs).

Like sibling agents.x402stock.xyz endpoints indexed in this same sweep, the 402's accepts[].payTo and extra.zeroclick ids (agentPaymentId/zcRequestId) are minted per-request by the payment proxy — do not treat payTo as a stable merchant address.

Fixed price ($0.03, per the OpenAPI x-payment-info.price.mode:'fixed' and the 402's accepts[0].extra.billing note) — not a ceiling/dynamic quote; the live 402 (30000 atomic units) and the paid amount matched exactly.
Dual payment rails advertised on the same 402: x402 (Base USDC, scheme exact — what was paid) and MPP/Tempo (also USDC) via a separate www-authenticate challenge; MasterKey uses only the x402 accept.

The two existing x402stock entries in this subcat (Quote, Snapshot) are currently status:hidden/hiddenReason:needs-review for reasons unrelated to and predating this task (a prior per-provider un-bundling commit) — not touched here.
usage.guide: Call GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/fda with the required `company` query param (a free-text company/sponsor/applicant name, e.g. 'Medtronic' or 'Pfizer', 2-120 chars) and an optional `limit` (max 50, default 10). Pay the fixed $0.03 x402 quote (Base USDC, no API key) and retry with the payment header. The 200 returns a synchronous snapshot of that company's recent FDA activity across 5 openFDA datasets in one call: drug.recalls/drug.approvals (pharma recalls and new-drug approvals) and device.clearances/device.approvals/device.recalls (510(k) clearances, PMA approvals, and device recalls) — each with a total_matched count, the returned count/items, and an attribution string. No polling; results are catalyst-style event feeds useful for biotech/medtech stock research, not the company's full regulatory history.

entries.name: x402stock Filing Search
entries.description: Full-text search across every SEC EDGAR filing since 2001 by keyword or exact phrase, with optional filters for form type, ticker, and date range.

billing.description: amount is the price and is charged in full when you pay; a failed delivery is credited back in full.

q.description: Full-text keyword or exact phrase to search for across SEC EDGAR filings since 2001. Required. Encode a multi-word query's space as '+' — see quirks.

forms.description: Comma-separated SEC form types to narrow results, e.g. '10-K,8-K'. Optional.

ticker.description: US ticker symbol to narrow results to one company's filings. Optional.

limit.description: Max results to return. Optional, default 10, max 100.

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/filing-search?q=<KEYWORD>&forms=<10-K,8-K>&ticker=<TICKER>&startdt=<YYYY-MM-DD>&enddt=<YYYY-MM-DD>&limit=<1-100> — only q is required, the rest are optional filters, all as query params, no request body. x402 USDC exact scheme on Base (agents.x402stock.xyz is x402stock's own agent-facing payment gateway; it mirrors the upstream x402stock.xyz route/price/schema 1:1 and proxies through after payment).
usage.outputShape: Flat JSON: source ('sec_edgar'), as_of (ISO timestamp), query (echoed), forms/ticker (echoed filters or null), total_matches (number), count (results returned, <= limit), results[].{accession, form, filing_date, period_ending, filer, cik, description, url}. Verified body (q='climate change', limit=3): total_matches:10000, count:3, e.g. {accession:'0001144204-08-046376', form:'FWP', filing_date:'2008-08-13', period_ending:null, filer:'HSBC USA INC /MD/  (CIK 0000083246)', cik:'0000083246', description:null, url:'https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/83246/000114420408046376/v123310_fwp.htm'}.
quirks: q is the only required param (full-text keyword or exact phrase, min length 1); forms/ticker/startdt/enddt/limit are optional filters.

Encode a multi-word q's space as '+', not '%20'. In testing, the exact same query with '%20' reproducibly (5/5, across both curl and Node fetch) returned HTTP 401 {"error":"invalid_zeroclick_signature"} instead of the normal 402/200 flow, while '+' or any single-word query (14/14) hit the normal flow — the failing responses carried response header x-render-origin-server: Vercel vs x-render-origin-server: Render on the working ones, indicating a stale/misconfigured backend instance behind the same hostname rather than a real signature problem. Not fixable client-side beyond avoiding literal %20.

Despite being listed in the schema's 'required' array, every result field except form/filer/cik/url/accession is typed anyOf string|null and was frequently null in the verified call (all 3 results had description:null and period_ending:null) — 'required' means the key is always present, not that its value is non-null.

total_matches for a very common phrase ('climate change') came back as a round 10000, which is the well-known default max-hits-tracking ceiling of the Elasticsearch index behind SEC EDGAR's own full-text search — the provider's own documented example (q='artificial intelligence'&forms=10-K) instead returns a non-round 4821, so treat total_matches:10000 specifically as 'at least 10000', not an exact count.

agents.x402stock.xyz is a payment-gateway proxy in front of x402stock.xyz, not a separate provider or dataset (same serviceName/source:'x402stock', identical route/price/output schema confirmed by directly probing https://x402stock.xyz/api/v1/filing-search). Its 402 payTo is a fresh, single-use escrow address minted per request by the gateway (two independent unpaid probes of this exact route returned two different payTo values, 0x6f5b4d8bddbbc4d971f83c7b4950730c5cb2ff64 and 0x7e2bf7cce11a93cea883e26a28f53413b72bf31e, each tied to a 5-minute-expiry agentPaymentId/zcRequestId not stored here) — unlike x402stock.xyz's own direct route, whose payTo (0x3070Fbb3803819fB5BdfE9286fdc6325A877fA85) is stable across probes. Always re-quote at call time rather than trusting a cached payTo.
The 402 also advertises an MPP (Tempo USDC) rail alongside x402 (protocols.mpp block) — only the x402 accept is recorded here per registry policy of excluding MPP.
Flat $0.02 price regardless of limit or filter combination (confirmed via the live 402 and the paid charge, both 20000 atomic units).
usage.guide: Full-text search every SEC EDGAR filing since 2001. Call GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/filing-search?q=<keyword or phrase> (URL-encode a space as '+', not %20) with optional forms (e.g. '10-K,8-K'), ticker, startdt/enddt (YYYY-MM-DD), and limit (default 10, max 100). Pay the x402 challenge (flat $0.02, Base USDC, exact scheme) and read the result inline in the 200 response, no polling. Output: source, as_of, query, forms, ticker, total_matches, count, and results[] each with accession, form, filing_date, period_ending, filer, cik, description, and a direct SEC.gov document url.

entries.name: x402stock Frames
entries.description: Returns one reported XBRL financial fact (e.g. Revenues, Assets, NetIncomeLoss) for every US public company that disclosed it in a given calendar period, sourced from SEC EDGAR and sorted by value, for cross-company peer screening and sector comparisons.

billing.description: amount is the price and is charged in full when you pay; a failed delivery is credited back in full. (Exact entries appear only on fixed-price requests - ceiling-priced requests are offered the reserve-and-pay-actual entry instead.)

tag.description: XBRL concept/tag name to look up across all filers, e.g. Revenues, Assets, NetIncomeLoss, EarningsPerShareBasic.

period.description: Calendar period: CYyyyy for an annual duration fact (e.g. CY2024), CYyyyyQn for a quarterly duration fact (e.g. CY2024Q1), or CYyyyyQnI for a quarter-end instantaneous fact used by balance-sheet concepts (e.g. CY2024Q1I).

unit.description: SEC unit key for the concept (e.g. USD, USD-per-shares, shares). Defaults to USD.

limit.description: Max rows to return, sorted by value descending.

inputSchema.description: Query params only (GET, no request body). tag and period are required; taxonomy/unit/limit are optional with the defaults shown.

as_of.description: ISO timestamp the response was generated.

label.description: SEC's human-readable label for the tag; can be null.

total_filers.description: Total number of companies that reported this concept for this period across SEC EDGAR — NOT capped by limit.

count.description: Number of rows actually returned in data[] (<= limit).

start.description: Period start date; null for instantaneous (balance-sheet) facts.

accession.description: SEC accession number of the source filing.

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/frames?tag=<TAG>&period=<PERIOD> (optionally &taxonomy=&unit=&limit=) — required query params tag+period, no request body; x402 exact-scheme USDC on Base, fixed $0.02.
usage.outputShape: Flat JSON: source('sec_edgar'), as_of, tag, taxonomy, label (nullable human-readable tag name), unit, period, total_filers (total companies that ever reported this concept+period, NOT capped by limit — observed 2485 for Revenues/CY2024), count (rows actually returned, <= limit), and data[] sorted by value descending — each row {cik, entity, value, start (nullable; null for instantaneous facts), end, accession}. Verified: tag=Revenues/period=CY2024 returned total_filers:2485, count:50, topped by Walmart Inc. value:680985000000 (end 2025-01-31, accession 0000104169-26-000055).
quirks: tag and period are REQUIRED query params — omitting either would 400; taxonomy (default us-gaap), unit (default USD), and limit (default 50, max 500) are optional.
period must match ^CY\d{4}(Q[1-4]I?)?$: CY2024 for an annual duration fact, CY2024Q1 for a quarterly duration fact, or CY2024Q1I (instantaneous, quarter-end) for balance-sheet concepts like Assets.
total_filers is the TOTAL number of companies that disclosed the concept for that period across SEC EDGAR, not the number of rows returned — count and data.length are what's capped by limit.

Direct proxy of SEC EDGAR's own XBRL 'frames' API (data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/frames) — cross-sectional (one concept+period, every company that reported it), unlike x402stock's own Quote/Snapshot endpoints, which are per-ticker current-price feeds.
start is null for instantaneous (balance-sheet, *I period) facts; populated with the period-start date for duration (income-statement) facts like Revenues.

Fixed $0.02 regardless of tag/period/limit chosen (x-payment-info mode:fixed). The live 402 also advertises an MPP/Tempo rail alongside x402 (MPP is excluded per registry convention — only the x402 exact-scheme accept is captured here).

Reachable via both x402stock.xyz (bare upstream, x402-only) and agents.x402stock.xyz (ZeroClick-fronted, x402+MPP) — this entry calls the agents. host, per the provider's own docs instructing agents to always call through it rather than the bare upstream directly.
usage.guide: Cross-company XBRL 'frames' lookup from SEC EDGAR: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/frames with required query params tag (an XBRL concept name, e.g. Revenues, Assets, NetIncomeLoss, EarningsPerShareBasic) and period (CYyyyy for an annual duration fact, CYyyyyQn for a quarterly duration fact, or CYyyyyQnI — instantaneous, quarter-end — for balance-sheet concepts like Assets); optional taxonomy (default us-gaap), unit (default USD), and limit (default 50, max 500). No request body. Pay the fixed $0.02 x402 quote in USDC on Base (no API key, no sign-in) and the 200 returns inline JSON: source('sec_edgar'), as_of, tag, taxonomy, label (SEC's human-readable name for the tag, nullable), unit, period, total_filers (how many companies EVER reported this concept for this period — not capped by limit), count (rows actually returned), and data[] sorted by value descending — each row is {cik, entity, value, start (nullable; null for instantaneous facts), end, accession}. Verified live with tag=Revenues&period=CY2024: total_filers 2485, count 50, topped by Walmart Inc. at $680,985,000,000 (period ended 2025-01-31, accession 0000104169-26-000055). Best used for peer screening / sector comparisons across many companies for one metric and period; for a single company's own metric trend over time, a per-company tool is a better fit.

entries.name: x402stock News
entries.description: Curated, ticker-tagged US stock-market news — general market headlines, or filtered to one ticker — with title, description, source publisher, image, and timestamp.

billing.description: amount is the price and is charged in full when you pay; a failed delivery is credited back in full.

ticker.description: Optional ticker symbol to filter news by, e.g. AAPL. Omit for general market-wide news.

limit.description: Optional max number of articles to return (default 10, max 50).

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/news?ticker=AAPL&limit=3 — both query params optional, no request body, x402 USDC exact on Base (agents.x402stock.xyz is x402stock's own agent-facing payment gateway; it mirrors the upstream x402stock.xyz paths 1:1 and proxies through after payment).
usage.outputShape: source ('x402stock'), as_of, count, articles[].{id, title, description, url, image_url, author, publisher, publisher_homepage, published_at, tickers[], keywords[]}
quirks: ticker and limit are both OPTIONAL query params — omit ticker entirely for general market-wide news (not company-specific).
ticker pattern is ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9.-]{0,9}$ — uppercase symbol, no path segment, query param only.

An article's tickers[] is not restricted to the queried ticker — filtering by ?ticker=AAPL still returned articles co-tagged with other symbols (e.g. NVDA, CAT, TSLA) whenever AAPL was one of several tickers mentioned.

agents.x402stock.xyz is a payment-gateway proxy in front of x402stock.xyz, not a separate provider: the live 402's payTo (0x2bb20f2bc842d517d47809dc30c9f5c810f470c7) differs from x402stock.xyz's own direct payTo (0x3070Fbb3803819fB5BdfE9286fdc6325A877fA85) used by the already-indexed x402stock Quote/Snapshot backends that call x402stock.xyz directly — same brand/dataset (source:'x402stock' in the body, serviceName:'x402stock' in the 402), different payment recipient because of the gateway hop.
description/author/image_url on each article are nullable per schema (anyOf string|null), though all three were populated (non-null) in the verified call.

The 402 also advertises an MPP/Tempo payment rail (www-authenticate header, method 'tempo') alongside x402 — only the x402 (Base USDC, exact) offer is indexed here per registry policy of excluding MPP.
usage.guide: Fetch curated, ticker-tagged US stock-market news. Call GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/news with optional query params ticker (uppercase symbol, e.g. AAPL) and limit (default 10, max 50) — omit both for general market news. Pay the x402 challenge ($0.02 flat, Base USDC, exact scheme) and read the result inline in the 200 response, no polling. Output: source, as_of, count, and articles[] each with id, title, description, url, image_url, author, publisher, publisher_homepage, published_at, tickers[], and keywords[].

entries.name: x402stock Patents
entries.description: Look up a company's US patent filings from the USPTO Open Data Portal by applicant name, newest first — returning each filing's patent and application numbers, title, filing and grant dates, status, applicant, inventors, and a link once granted.

billing.description: amount is the price and is charged in full when you pay; a failed delivery is credited back in full. (Exact entries appear only on fixed-price requests - ceiling-priced requests are offered the reserve-and-pay-actual entry instead.)

company.description: Company/applicant name to search, e.g. 'Tesla'. Matches the USPTO APPLICANT field — subsidiaries or brand-name variants need separate queries.

limit.description: Max patents to return.

inputSchema.description: All query params, no request body.

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/patents?company=<Company>[&limit=1-100] — x402 exact scheme, Base USDC (eip155:8453), no request body. `company` is REQUIRED (matches the USPTO APPLICANT name); `limit` is optional (default 20, max 100).
usage.outputShape: Synchronous flat JSON on the paid 200: { source:'uspto', as_of:<ISO timestamp>, company:'Tesla', total_matched:1901, count:20, patents:[{patent_number,application_number,title,filing_date,grant_date,status,applicant,inventors:[],url}] (page size = `limit`, default 20, max 100, newest filing_date first), attribution:'Source: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) Open Data Portal' }.
quirks: company matches the USPTO APPLICANT field (a legal/company name, e.g. 'Tesla'), not a stock ticker; subsidiaries or brand-name variants need separate queries.

Results are newest-filing-first, so the default first page skews heavily PENDING: in the verified call (company=Tesla, limit defaulted to 20) all 20 returned rows had patent_number:null, grant_date:null and url:null, with status values like 'Docketed New Case - Ready for Examination' — those three fields only populate once USPTO actually grants the patent. application_number is the reliable identifier for a pending filing.
application_number is sometimes a PCT international application id (e.g. 'PCTUS2025061797') rather than a plain USPTO serial number.

total_matched (1901 for Tesla) is the FULL match count, not the page size — count/patents.length (<= limit, default 20, hard max 100) is what actually comes back; there is no offset/page param in the schema.

The x402 payTo address is minted fresh per request by the agents.x402stock.xyz proxy: two live 402s for this exact endpoint/query seconds apart returned two different payTo addresses (0x93b1c20f...e205e5e and 0x94d23ecd...2edddd2) at the same fixed 20000-atomic amount — don't treat payTo as a stable merchant address; always pay whatever the live 402 quotes.

Called through the agents.x402stock.xyz pay-per-use proxy, not the bare x402stock.xyz upstream (its llms.txt: 'Call these paths through https://agents.x402stock.xyz, never the upstream directly'); same brand/provider as the existing bare-host x402stock Quote/Snapshot entries, just a newer, wider product line — this endpoint isn't listed in x402stock's older public llms.txt endpoint table, only in the live /openapi.json served from agents.x402stock.xyz.

The live 402 also offers an MPP/Tempo payment path (www-authenticate: Payment method="tempo") alongside x402 — only the x402 (Base USDC, exact scheme) accept is captured here, per registry policy of excluding MPP.
usage.guide: Look up a company's US patent filings with GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/patents?company=<Company> (company is required and must match the USPTO applicant/company name, e.g. 'Tesla'; add &limit=1-100 to widen the page beyond the default 20). Pay the fixed $0.02 x402 quote (Base USDC, no API key) and retry with the payment header. The 200 returns a synchronous JSON page of matching USPTO filings, newest first, under `patents` — title, filing/grant dates, status, applicant, inventors, and (once granted) a patent number and link — plus `total_matched`/`count` and a USPTO attribution string. Most recently-filed results are still pending, so patent_number/grant_date/url are frequently null. No polling; no auth beyond the x402 payment.

entries.name: x402stock Private Stocks
entries.description: Live valuations for every PreStocks pre-IPO private-company token in one call — Anduril, Anthropic, Kalshi, Neuralink, OpenAI, Polymarket, and SpaceX — via Solana tokens backed 1:1 by SPV exposure. Per company: the SPV mark_price/mark_valuation, the on-chain token_price/implied_valuation, the token's premium-or-discount vs the mark (token_premium_percent), circulating supply, and the Solana contract_address. The catalog's only pre-IPO feed. Verified live (7 companies returned): e.g. {symbol:'ANTHROPIC', mark_price:755.9152, mark_valuation:1238447814705, token_price:750.4385, implied_valuation:1229475188087, token_premium_percent:-0.72, supply:7383.887916, contract_address:'Pren1FvFX6J3E4kXhJuCiAD5aDmGEb7qJRncwA8Lkhw'}.

backends.inputSchema: No input — GET with no path segments, query params, or request body. Returns every PreStocks private company in one call.
backends.outputSchema: JSON object: { source:'x402stock', as_of (ISO timestamp), venue:'prestocks', count (number of companies), companies: [{ symbol, name, description, mark_price, mark_valuation, token_price, implied_valuation, token_premium_percent, supply, contract_address (Solana mint), logo_url, url }], attribution (required pass-through string) }. Per the provider's own openapi.json; verified live with count 7.

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/private-stocks — no path segments, query params, or request body; x402 USDC on Base
usage.outputShape: companies[] — array of every PreStocks pre-IPO company, most-valuable first; each item has symbol, name, description, mark_price, mark_valuation, token_price, implied_valuation, token_premium_percent, supply, contract_address, logo_url, url. Top level also carries source, as_of, venue, count, attribution.
quirks: GET with no path/query/body — returns ALL companies in one call; the sibling GET /api/v1/private-stocks/{symbol} (NOT indexed by this entry) returns just one company for $0.01.

Fixed price $0.02 (20000 atomic USDC, 6dp) on Base (eip155:8453); provider's openapi.json x-payment-info marks price.mode:'fixed', matching two independent live probes — not dynamic, no re-quote risk.

The 402 challenge's payTo escrow address is minted fresh per request — two probes of this same endpoint returned two different payTo values (0x0396d1ca6d9567ef36fa98de7609646e17d4b17f and 0xcf4a5008ad9cf06b0ac255e65f5427d63c14109f) a few seconds apart. Always pay the payTo/accepts from the CURRENT 402, never a cached one.
The 402 also advertises an MPP/Tempo payment route (WWW-Authenticate: Payment method="tempo") alongside the x402 'exact' accept; only the x402 accept is used/stored here per project convention.

Verified live: exactly 7 companies (ANDURIL, ANTHROPIC, KALSHI, NEURALINK, OPENAI, POLYMARKET, SPACEX). Kalshi and Polymarket are prediction-market operators, not traditional startups, but ship in the same feed.

token_price/implied_valuation is the live on-chain trading price of the Solana SPV token; mark_price/mark_valuation is the SPV's own official mark. token_premium_percent is the live spread between them — the verified call ranged from -22.02% (SPACEX, trading well below its mark) to +5.65% (KALSHI, trading above its mark).
attribution is a field the provider requires be passed through to any end user of this data.

Payment for the API call itself is USDC on Base, even though the underlying tokens it describes are Solana SPL tokens (contract_address values are Solana mint addresses, e.g. 'Pren1FvFX6J3E4kXhJuCiAD5aDmGEb7qJRncwA8Lkhw') — two different chains for two different purposes.
usage.guide: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/private-stocks with no path segments, query params, or request body — pay the quoted x402 challenge ($0.02 USDC on Base) and retry with the X-PAYMENT header to get a 200. The response is a flat JSON object whose `companies` array covers every PreStocks pre-IPO private-company token in one call (verified live: Anduril, Anthropic, Kalshi, Neuralink, OpenAI, Polymarket, SpaceX). Each company entry gives the SPV mark_price/mark_valuation, the live on-chain token_price/implied_valuation, the token_premium_percent gap between the two, circulating supply, and the Solana contract_address. Use this for a one-call snapshot of the whole pre-IPO board; there is a sibling per-symbol endpoint for just one company, but it is not covered by this entry. Pass the `attribution` string through to any end user, per the provider's requirement. Price is fixed at $0.02 (confirmed via the provider's own OpenAPI spec, not dynamic), but each 402 challenge mints a fresh escrow payTo address, so always pay the address from the CURRENT challenge, not a cached one.

Each items[] entry: symbol (e.g. 'AAPLx'), underlying (e.g. 'AAPL'), pool (Raydium pool address), mint (SPL token mint, nullable), xstock_price_usd (on-chain decoded price, nullable), pool_price_raw_unit (nullable), multiplier (Token-2022 scaled-UI multiplier), liquidity (nullable), tick_current (nullable), underlying_price_usd (nullable), underlying_change_percent (nullable), underlying_market_status (nullable, e.g. 'closed'), premium_percent (nullable — xstock_price_usd vs underlying_price_usd, signed). Verified live call returned count:10, all 10 major xStocks (AAPLx, TSLAx, NVDAx, SPYx, QQQx, MSTRx, GOOGLx, AMZNx, METAx, COINx), us_market_open:false (US markets closed at call time).
quirks: Bare GET with zero params always returns ALL tracked xStocks in one call (10 as of the verified call) — there is no ticker filter on this path. The upstream OpenAPI separately lists /api/v1/xstocks/{ticker} (meterSlug xstocks_ticker, $0.02) for a single symbol; that per-ticker path is NOT indexed here (out of scope for this sweep) and would be its own backend if added later.

Per-item fields are almost all nullable (anyOf number|null or string|null) even though the schema lists all 13 keys as 'required' — only symbol, underlying, pool, and multiplier are non-nullable in practice; treat xstock_price_usd/pool_price_raw_unit/liquidity/tick_current/underlying_price_usd/underlying_change_percent/underlying_market_status/premium_percent/mint as possibly null.
premium_percent is the on-chain xStock price vs. its real-world underlying, signed: positive means the token trades ABOVE the real stock, negative means below (arbitrage signal).

Top-level us_market_open (nullable bool) gates interpretation: while US markets are open the AMM price is arb-anchored to the underlying; off-hours (observed in the verified call) it reflects the pool's own 24/7 price discovery, so premiums/discounts can run wider.

Price is decoded directly from Raydium CLMM pool state (sqrt_price_x64) on the public Solana ledger — not sourced from Backed/xStocks', Chainlink's, or Pyth's own API — per the response's own 'note' field.

The x402 payTo address and the extra.zeroclick agentPaymentId/zcRequestId nonces rotate on every fresh 402 (observed 3 different payTo addresses across 3 unpaid probes of the same idle endpoint within ~2 minutes); these are per-challenge billing metadata, not a stable recipient/id to hardcode — always settle whatever the live 402 quotes.

The same operation is also documented directly on the upstream host (https://x402stock.xyz/api/v1/xstocks per its own OpenAPI x-payment-info), but x402stock's own llms.txt instructs agents to call through https://agents.x402stock.xyz (identity/payment/proxying front door) — that agents. host is what was probed and paid here.
Response also advertises an MPP (Tempo USDC) settlement path as an alternative to x402 (Base USDC); only the x402 rail was exercised for this index.
usage.guide: Every tracked xStock (tokenized US equity) with its on-chain price decoded from Raydium CLMM pool state on Solana, the real underlying's live quote, and the premium/discount percent between them — plus pool liquidity, the Token-2022 scaled-UI multiplier, and a us_market_open arb-context flag. GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/xstocks with no params; pays $0.04 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453, scheme exact) or MPP/Tempo. Output: source, as_of, venue, protocol, program, note, us_market_open, sections.{onchain,underlying}, count, and items[] (symbol, underlying, pool, mint, xstock_price_usd, pool_price_raw_unit, multiplier, liquidity, tick_current, underlying_price_usd, underlying_change_percent, underlying_market_status, premium_percent). Use it to spot arbitrage / mispricing between a tokenized stock and its real-world underlying, or to monitor xStocks liquidity and on-chain health.

entries.name: NetIntel Currency Converter
entries.description: Convert any amount between 32 fiat currencies (live European Central Bank reference rates) and major cryptocurrencies (BTC, ETH, USDC, SOL, ICP, CELO and more, live Coinbase spot rates) — fiat↔fiat, crypto↔fiat, and crypto↔crypto — returning the converted amount, exchange rate, inverse rate, rate date, and rate source.

from.description: ISO 4217 fiat code (e.g. USD, EUR) or crypto symbol (e.g. BTC, ETH, USDC, SOL)

to.description: ISO 4217 fiat code or crypto symbol to convert into

amount.description: Amount of the `from` currency to convert

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/currency-exchange/convert?from=<CODE>&to=<CODE>&amount=<NUMBER> — all three query params required; `from`/`to` accept fiat ISO 4217 codes (32 supported) or crypto symbols (BTC, ETH, USDC, SOL, ICP, CELO, ...). Pay $0.01 USDC via x402 (Base or Solana).
usage.outputShape: Top-level JSON: from, to, amount (echoes input); converted_amount (number); exchange_rate (from->to rate); inverse_rate (to->from rate); rate_date (YYYY-MM-DD); is_historical (bool); source ('coinbase' for crypto pairs, ECB for fiat); score/grade (quality); findings[] describing which rate source/rule was applied.
quirks: Synchronous — result is returned inline in the 200 body, no polling.
Failed calls (4xx/5xx, incl. input-validation rejections) are never charged per NetIntel's agent fair-trade guarantee.
Crypto pairs are priced at latest Coinbase spot; fiat pairs use ECB reference rates (rate_date reflects the ECB business day, so fiat rate_date may lag weekends/holidays).
source field indicates provenance ('coinbase' when a crypto leg is involved).
usage.guide: Convert money across fiat and crypto without a paid forex API. Make a GET request to https://netintel.dev/currency-exchange/convert with three required query params: from, to, and amount (e.g. ?from=USD&to=BTC&amount=100). from/to may be fiat ISO 4217 codes (32 supported, ECB rates) or crypto symbols like BTC/ETH/USDC/SOL (Coinbase spot). An unpaid request returns HTTP 402 with x402 payment requirements; retry with an X-PAYMENT header ($0.01 USDC on Base eip155:8453 or Solana). The 200 response is synchronous JSON: read converted_amount for the result, plus exchange_rate/inverse_rate/rate_date/source for provenance. fiat↔fiat, crypto↔fiat, and crypto↔crypto all work.

quirks: Response wraps the payload under { ok, data:{...} }; the requested series live under data.series keyed by Valet code.
series takes RAW Bank of Canada Valet codes: FX pairs FXUSDCAD/FXEURCAD/FXGBPCAD, overnight target rate V39079, prime rate V80691311 (not friendly names/tenors).
Up to 10 comma-separated codes per call; recent caps at 60 daily observations per series.

Country-prefixed /v1/ca/* op — a distinct Bank-of-Canada dataset, not a path-param variant of any Greeneris sibling (series/recent are query params).
usage.guide: Fetch official Bank of Canada CAD reference rates — FX pairs (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD, GBP/CAD via FXUSDCAD/FXEURCAD/FXGBPCAD), the overnight target rate (V39079), and the prime rate (V80691311) — as normalized JSON from the BoC Valet API. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/ca/boc-rates?series=FXUSDCAD,V39079&recent=3 (both params optional: series = comma-separated Valet codes up to 10, default FXUSDCAD; recent = last N daily observations 1-60, default 1). entries.name: Greeneris DE Power Spot
entries.description: Hourly EPEX Spot day-ahead electricity spot prices (EUR/MWh) for the German/Luxembourg (DE-LU) and Austrian (AT) bidding zones, with a min/max/avg summary, sourced from the aWATTar market-data API.

zone.description: Bidding zone: de = Germany/Luxembourg (DE-LU), at = Austria. Query param, optional.

start.description: Window start, ISO 8601 or epoch (optional, use with end)

end.description: Window end, ISO 8601 or epoch (optional, use with start)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/de/power-spot?zone=de — all query params optional: zone (de=Germany/Luxembourg default, at=Austria), and an optional window start & end (ISO 8601 or epoch, used together for history). No body. A bare GET returns the default DE-LU rolling ~24h day-ahead window. x402 USDC on Base, no API key; the payment is the auth.
usage.outputShape: { ok:true, data:{ zone:'DE-LU', unit:'EUR/MWh', count:24, min:83.27, max:207.03, avg:149.29, prices:[ { start:'2026-07-30T18:00:00Z', end:'2026-07-30T19:00:00Z', price_eur_mwh:198.31 }, ... ], source:'Datenquelle: aWATTar (EPEX Spot day-ahead hourly prices)' } } — data.prices is an array of hourly day-ahead price intervals (start/end ISO UTC, price_eur_mwh number in EUR/MWh); data.count is its length; data.min/max/avg summarize the window.
quirks: All query params are optional; a bare GET returns the default zone DE-LU as a rolling ~24h day-ahead window. Pass ?zone=at for Austria.

Result payload is wrapped in { ok, data } — the hourly series lives under data.prices and data.count is its length (the 402 outputSchema example shows the inner data object un-wrapped, but the live paid response wraps it in { ok, data }).
Prices are day-ahead wholesale spot in EUR/MWh at hourly resolution; day-ahead data publishes once daily and the endpoint is served with a 1h cache.
start & end must be ISO 8601 or epoch and are used together to bound a history window.
Data originates from the aWATTar market-data API (EPEX Spot day-ahead hourly prices) — data.source is 'Datenquelle: aWATTar (EPEX Spot day-ahead hourly prices)'.
Zone codes are the short forms de|at (query), but data.zone is returned as the full bidding-zone name (e.g. DE-LU).

Sibling energy ops on the same host are separate services, not variants of this one: /v1/eu/power-price (Energy-Charts, ~44 European zones), /v1/nordics/power-price (Nord Pool/Baltic), /v1/fr/power-mix, /v1/gb/power-demand, /v1/gb/carbon.
usage.guide: German & Austrian wholesale day-ahead electricity spot prices. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/de/power-spot with optional query param zone (de=Germany/Luxembourg default, at=Austria) and an optional ISO 8601 / epoch window start & end (used together for history). No body, no API key — pay per call in USDC on Base via x402 (~$0.002). Response: { ok:true, data:{ zone, unit:'EUR/MWh', count, min, max, avg, prices:[ { start (ISO UTC), end (ISO UTC), price_eur_mwh (EUR/MWh) } ], source } }. Source is the aWATTar market-data API (EPEX Spot day-ahead hourly prices). Use for German/Austrian power-market pricing, energy-cost-aware scheduling, or intraday spot analytics; use the sibling per-country/region power endpoints (EU, Nordics, FR mix, GB demand/carbon) for other feeds.

usage.outputShape: { ok: boolean, data: { count: number, records: [ { timestamp_utc, consumption_mw, forecast_d_mw, forecast_d1_mw, co2_intensity_g_kwh, production_mw: { nuclear, wind, solar, hydro, gas, fuel_oil, coal, bioenergy, pumped_storage, battery_storage, battery_discharge }, exchange_mw: { physical_total, england, spain, italy, switzerland, germany_belgium } } ], source } } — e.g. one record: { timestamp_utc: '2026-07-30T17:45:00+00:00', consumption_mw: 51441, co2_intensity_g_kwh: 36, production_mw: { nuclear: 42980, wind: 2097, solar: 3670, hydro: 7774, gas: 3909, ... }, exchange_mw: { physical_total: -10037, england: -1880, spain: 2415, ... } }

Result payload is wrapped in { ok, data } — the records array lives under data.records and data.count is its length.

Data is France national grid only, sourced from RTE eCO2mix real-time via the ODRE portal (Licence Ouverte 2.0, attribution RTE/ODRE), refreshed every 15 minutes with a ~15-min cache — not a market/price feed.
Storage and exchange values can be negative (charging / net export); exchange_mw.physical_total is the net cross-border flow (negative = France net exporting).
Sibling energy ops on the same host are separate services, not variants of this one: /v1/de/power-spot, /v1/eu/power-price, /v1/nordics/power-price, /v1/gb/power-demand, /v1/gb/carbon.
usage.guide: France real-time electricity generation mix. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/fr/power-mix with optional query param rows (1-12, default 4 = last hour). No body, no API key — pay $0.002 USDC on Base via x402. Response: { ok: true, data: { count, records: [ { timestamp_utc, consumption_mw, forecast_d_mw, forecast_d1_mw, co2_intensity_g_kwh, production_mw: {nuclear, wind, solar, hydro, gas, coal, bioenergy, storage...}, exchange_mw: {physical_total, england, spain, italy, switzerland, germany_belgium} } ], source } }. Source is RTE eCO2mix via ODRE (Licence Ouverte 2.0), 15-min resolution/cache. Use for grid decarbonization, CO2-intensity-aware scheduling, or energy-mix analytics; use the sibling per-country power endpoints for other markets.

entries.name: Greeneris FX Latest Rates
entries.description: Latest European Central Bank reference exchange rates for any base currency, returned as normalized JSON (base, date, rates map).

base.description: Base currency code (query param, optional, default EUR)

symbols.description: Comma-separated target currency codes (query param, optional -> all)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/fx/latest?base=EUR&symbols=USD,GBP — both query params optional (base defaults to EUR; omit symbols to get all currencies). No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key; the payment is the auth.
usage.outputShape: { ok: boolean, data: { base, date (YYYY-MM-DD), rates: { <CCY>: number, ... }, source } } — e.g. { ok: true, data: { base: 'EUR', date: '2026-07-30', rates: { GBP: 0.85715, USD: 1.1476 }, source: 'ECB reference rates via frankfurter.app' } }
quirks: Both params are optional query params (not path/body); calling with no params returns EUR base against all ECB currencies.
Rates are ECB reference rates (via frankfurter.app), updated once per working day (~16:00 CET) and served with a ~1h cache — not a live tradable FX feed.
Result payload is wrapped in { ok, data } — the rates live under data.rates.
Sibling ops on the same host: /v1/fx/official and /v1/fx/history are separate services, not variants of this one.
usage.guide: Latest ECB reference exchange rates as normalized JSON. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/fx/latest with optional query params base (default EUR) and symbols (comma-separated target currencies; omit for all). No body, no API key — pay $0.001 USDC on Base via x402. Response: { ok: true, data: { base, date, rates: { <CCY>: number }, source } }. Rates refresh once per working day (~16:00 CET) with a ~1h cache; use /v1/fx/history for historical and /v1/fx/official for official rates.

entries.name: Greeneris FX Official Treasury Rates
entries.description: Official US Treasury Reporting Rates of Exchange — the legal USD conversion rates required for FBAR/8938 filings and US federal accounting, covering ~170 currencies, returned as normalized JSON.

currencies.description: Comma-separated Treasury 'Country-Currency' descriptors, max 30 (query param, optional -> all currencies)

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD; latest quarterly rate at or before this date (query param, optional, default today)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/fx/official?currencies=Euro Zone-Euro,Japan-Yen&date=2026-06-30 — both query params optional (omit currencies for all ~170; date defaults to today, snaps to latest quarterly rate at or before it). No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key; the payment is the auth.
usage.outputShape: { ok: boolean, data: { as_of (YYYY-MM-DD), count: number, rates: [ { country_currency, country, currency, rate_per_usd: number, record_date, effective_date } ], source } } — e.g. { ok: true, data: { as_of: '2026-06-30', count: 2, rates: [ { country_currency: 'Euro Zone-Euro', country: 'Euro Zone', currency: 'Euro', rate_per_usd: 0.877, record_date: '2026-06-30', effective_date: '2026-06-30' }, { country_currency: 'Japan-Yen', country: 'Japan', currency: 'Yen', rate_per_usd: 162.38, ... } ], source: 'US Treasury FiscalData, Reporting Rates of Exchange (quarterly official rates, public domain)' } }
quirks: Both params are optional query params (not path/body); calling with no params returns all ~170 currencies at the latest quarterly rate.
currencies uses Treasury 'Country-Currency' descriptors (e.g. 'Euro Zone-Euro', 'Japan-Yen'), NOT ISO codes — comma-separated, max 30 per call.
rate_per_usd is units of FOREIGN currency per 1 USD (not USD per unit).
Source is quarterly official US Treasury rates (public domain), served with a 7-day cache — for FBAR/8938 filings and US federal accounting, not a live tradable FX feed.
Result payload is wrapped in { ok, data } and rates is an ARRAY of per-currency objects (differs from the /v1/fx/latest ECB service, whose rates is a map).
Sibling ops on the same host: /v1/fx/latest (ECB reference rates) and /v1/fx/history are separate services, not variants of this one.
usage.guide: Official US Treasury Reporting Rates of Exchange as normalized JSON. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/fx/official with optional query params currencies (comma-separated Treasury 'Country-Currency' descriptors like 'Euro Zone-Euro,Japan-Yen', max 30; omit for all ~170) and date (YYYY-MM-DD; snaps to the latest quarterly rate at or before it, default today). No body, no API key — pay $0.005 USDC on Base via x402. Response: { ok: true, data: { as_of, count, rates: [ { country_currency, country, currency, rate_per_usd, record_date, effective_date } ], source } }. rate_per_usd is foreign units per 1 USD; rates update quarterly with a 7-day cache. Use these legal rates for FBAR/8938 filings and US federal accounting; use /v1/fx/latest for ECB daily reference rates and /v1/fx/history for historical.

entries.name: Greeneris OECD Leading Indicators
entries.description: OECD Composite Leading Indicator (amplitude-adjusted, long-term trend = 100) for a country or region, the reference early signal of business-cycle turning points, with a computed cycle_signal (expansion/downturn/slowdown/recovery).

area.description: OECD area code (query param, optional; e.g. USA, DEU, FRA, GBR, JPN, G20)

n.description: Last N monthly observations (query param, optional, 1-36)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/global/leading-indicators?area=USA&n=6 — both query params optional (area defaults to USA; n defaults to 6, range 1-36). No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key; the payment is the auth.
usage.outputShape: { ok: true, data: { area, area_name, indicator, trend_level, frequency, observations:[{period 'YYYY-MM', value}], cycle_signal, source } } — e.g. { ok:true, data:{ area:'USA', area_name:'United States', indicator:'composite_leading_indicator_amplitude_adjusted', trend_level:100, frequency:'monthly', observations:[{period:'2026-06', value:100.8024}], cycle_signal:'expansion', source:'OECD Composite Leading Indicators, sdmx.oecd.org (CC BY 4.0)' } }
quirks: Both params are optional query params (not path/body); calling with no query returns USA for the last 6 monthly observations.
Result payload is wrapped in { ok, data } — the indicator fields live under data (the Bazaar output example omitted this ok/data envelope).
trend_level is 100 by construction (amplitude-adjusted, long-term trend normalized to 100); values above 100 = above trend.
cycle_signal is a computed classification (expansion/downturn/slowdown/recovery) derived from the recent level/momentum, not a raw OECD field.
Monthly frequency, published ~mid-month by the OECD; served with a 24h cache. n caps at 36 observations.
Sourced from OECD Composite Leading Indicators (sdmx.oecd.org, CC BY 4.0); reuse permitted with attribution to the OECD.

Distinct global-macro op on the same host — /v1/global/macro and /v1/global/lei are separate services, not variants of this one; area is a query param, so this is one templated service, not one-per-country.
usage.guide: Fetch the OECD Composite Leading Indicator (amplitude-adjusted, trend=100) — the reference early signal for business-cycle turning points — for a country or region. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/global/leading-indicators with optional query params area (OECD code, default USA; e.g. DEU, FRA, GBR, JPN, G20) and n (last N monthly observations, 1-36, default 6). No body, no API key — pay $0.01 USDC on Base via x402. Response: { ok:true, data:{ area, area_name, indicator, trend_level, frequency, observations:[{period,value}], cycle_signal, source } }. cycle_signal (expansion/downturn/slowdown/recovery) is a computed classification; values above trend_level (100) mean above long-term trend. Monthly cadence, 24h cache.

entries.name: Greeneris Global Macro Indicators
entries.description: Annual macroeconomic indicator series (inflation, GDP, government debt, unemployment, etc.) for 200+ countries from the World Bank Indicators API, returned as normalized JSON.

country.description: ISO3 country code (query param, optional, default USA)

indicator.description: World Bank indicator id (query param, optional, default FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG). Common: FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG inflation %, NY.GDP.MKTP.CD GDP current US$, GC.DOD.TOTL.GD.ZS gov debt %GDP, SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS unemployment %.

years.description: Last N years, 1-20 (query param, optional, default 5)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/global/macro?country=USA&indicator=FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG&years=3 — all three query params optional (country defaults USA, indicator defaults FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG inflation, years defaults 5). No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key; the payment is the auth.
usage.outputShape: { ok: boolean, data: { country, country_name, indicator, indicator_name, last_updated (YYYY-MM-DD), observations: [{ year: string, value: number }], source } } — e.g. { ok: true, data: { country: 'USA', country_name: 'United States', indicator: 'FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG', indicator_name: 'Inflation, consumer prices (annual %)', last_updated: '2026-07-13', observations: [{ year: '2024', value: 2.9495 }, { year: '2023', value: 4.1163 }, { year: '2022', value: 8.0028 }], source: 'World Bank Open Data (CC BY 4.0), annual series' } }
quirks: All three params are optional query params (not path/body); calling with none returns US inflation (FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG) for the last 5 years.
Data is annual World Bank Open Data (CC BY 4.0) — not real-time; observations are returned newest-first and 24h cached.
country takes an ISO3 code (e.g. USA, FRA, DEU); indicator takes a World Bank indicator id — a wrong indicator id yields empty observations, not an error.
Result payload is wrapped in { ok, data } — the series lives under data.observations.
Sibling ops on the same host: /v1/global/lei and /v1/global/leading-indicators are separate services, not variants of this one.
usage.guide: Annual macroeconomic indicator series for 200+ countries from the World Bank Indicators API, normalized to JSON. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/global/macro with optional query params country (ISO3, default USA), indicator (World Bank indicator id, default FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG inflation %), and years (1-20, default 5). Common indicators: FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG inflation %, NY.GDP.MKTP.CD GDP current US$, GC.DOD.TOTL.GD.ZS gov debt %GDP, SL.UEM.TOTL.ZS unemployment %. No body, no API key — pay $0.005 USDC on Base via x402. Response: { ok: true, data: { country, country_name, indicator, indicator_name, last_updated, observations: [{ year, value }], source } }, newest-first, 24h cache.

entries.name: Greeneris Nordics Power Spot Price
entries.description: Nord Pool day-ahead electricity spot prices (EUR/MWh, 15-min resolution) for the Estonian, Finnish, Latvian and Lithuanian bidding zones, from the Estonian TSO Elering's open-data API.

zone.description: Bidding zone to filter (Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania) or 'all' for all four

start.description: Window start, ISO 8601 UTC (default end-24h). Max 7-day window.

zones.description: Keyed by zone (ee/fi/lv/lt); each value is an array of price points

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/nordics/power-price with optional query params: zone (ee|fi|lv|lt|all, default all), start & end (ISO 8601 UTC window, max 7 days, default last 24h). No body. All params optional — a bare GET returns the last 24h for all four zones. x402 USDC on Base, no API key.
usage.outputShape: { ok:true, data:{ start, end, unit:'EUR/MWh', zones:{ ee:[{time,price_eur_mwh}], fi:[...], lv:[...], lt:[...] }, source } } — each zone is an array of 15-min price points (time ISO UTC, price_eur_mwh number); when ?zone= filters one zone only that key is present.
quirks: All query params are optional; a bare GET returns the last 24h across all four zones (ee, fi, lv, lt).
Prices are day-ahead Nord Pool spot in EUR/MWh at 15-minute resolution; day-ahead prices publish once daily and the endpoint is served with a 1h cache.
start/end must be ISO 8601 UTC and span at most a 7-day window.
?zone= accepts one of ee|fi|lv|lt (single zone) or all; filtering to one zone returns only that key under data.zones.
Data originates from the Estonian TSO Elering open-data API (dashboard.elering.ee), which aggregates Nord Pool day-ahead prices.
usage.guide: Nord Pool day-ahead electricity spot prices for the Baltic-Nordic bidding zones (Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania), sourced from Elering open data. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/nordics/power-price (all params optional: zone=ee|fi|lv|lt|all default all; start & end = ISO 8601 UTC window, max 7 days, default last 24h). No body, no API key — pay per call in USDC on Base via x402 (~$0.002). Read prices from data.zones.<zone>[] where each point is { time (ISO UTC), price_eur_mwh }; data.unit is 'EUR/MWh'.

entries.name: Greeneris OECD CPI
entries.description: Headline national CPI (all items) as a year-on-year annual growth rate, monthly, for any OECD member — USA, GBR, JPN, CAN, FRA and more — sourced from the official OECD SDMX Data Explorer under one methodology.

country.description: OECD REF_AREA code (USA, GBR, JPN, FRA, CAN...)

last_n.description: Number of most recent months to return (1-24)

latest_annual_rate_percent.description: Latest headline CPI year-on-year growth rate, percent

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/oecd/cpi — no required input. Optional query params: ?country=<OECD REF_AREA code> (e.g. USA, GBR, JPN, FRA, CAN; default USA) and ?last_n=N (1-24 most recent months, default 1). No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key.
usage.outputShape: { ok:true, data:{ measure, country, country_name, latest_period:'YYYY-MM', latest_annual_rate_percent, observations:[{period:'YYYY-MM', annual_rate_percent}], source } } — CPI as year-on-year annual growth rate in percent.
quirks: Response wraps the payload in { ok, data:{...} }; the CPI fields live under data (the Bazaar output example omitted the ok/data envelope).
No required input — calling with no query returns just the latest USA print (country defaults to USA, last_n defaults to 1).
?last_n caps at 24 monthly observations.
country is an OECD REF_AREA code (3-letter, e.g. USA/GBR/JPN/FRA/CAN), not an ISO-2 code.
Recency varies by country; a series older than 18 months is refused with a 502 and is NOT charged.
Measures headline CPI (all items) as an annual growth rate — complements Eurostat HICP by covering non-EU OECD economies under one methodology.
Data sourced from the official OECD SDMX Data Explorer (dataset DSD_PRICES@DF_PRICES_ALL), CC BY 4.0; served with a 24h cache.
The only /v1/oecd/* Greeneris op in this sweep; country/last_n are query params, not path segments, so not a path-param variant of any sibling.
usage.guide: Fetch a country's headline CPI (all items) as a year-on-year annual growth rate, monthly, from the official OECD SDMX Data Explorer. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/oecd/cpi with optional ?country=<OECD REF_AREA code, e.g. USA/GBR/JPN/FRA/CAN, default USA> and ?last_n=N (1-24 months, default 1). No body, no API key — pay $0.002 USDC on Base via x402. Output: { ok, data:{ measure, country, country_name, latest_period, latest_annual_rate_percent, observations:[{period, annual_rate_percent}], source } }, rates in percent. Note: series older than 18 months return 502 and are not charged.

entries.name: Greeneris US Public Debt
entries.description: Total US public debt outstanding to the penny — debt held by the public, intragovernmental holdings and grand total per business day — from the official US Treasury FiscalData Debt to the Penny dataset (public domain).

since.description: Only records with record_date >= this ISO date (optional; history back to 1993)

limit.description: Max records, newest first (1-100)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/us/debt with optional query params: limit (1-100, newest first, default 1) and since (ISO record_date floor, history back to 1993). No body, no API key. A bare GET returns the single latest data point. x402 USDC on Base.
usage.outputShape: { ok:true, data:{ count, records:[{ record_date, debt_held_by_public_usd, intragovernmental_holdings_usd, total_public_debt_usd }], source } } — amounts in USD; records newest-first; total_public_debt_usd = debt_held_by_public_usd + intragovernmental_holdings_usd.
quirks: All query params are optional; a bare GET returns just the single most recent business-day record (limit defaults to 1).
Daily cadence on business days only (published ~3pm ET); the response is cached 6h upstream, so intraday re-calls return the same values.
Amounts are full-dollar figures to the penny (e.g. total_public_debt_usd ~39.8 trillion), not thousands/millions.
History available back to 1993 via since=YYYY-MM-DD combined with a larger limit.
Response wraps the payload under data{}; underlying source is the public-domain US Treasury FiscalData Debt to the Penny dataset.
usage.guide: Total US public debt outstanding to the penny, from the official US Treasury FiscalData Debt to the Penny dataset. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/us/debt?limit=3 (all params optional: limit = 1-100 newest-first records, default 1 = latest only; since = ISO record_date floor, history to 1993). No body, no API key — pay per call in USDC on Base via x402. Returns { ok, data:{ count, records:[{ record_date, debt_held_by_public_usd, intragovernmental_holdings_usd, total_public_debt_usd }], source } }.

entries.name: Greeneris US Treasury Average Interest Rates
entries.description: Monthly average interest rates the US Treasury pays on its outstanding securities, sourced from the official US Treasury FiscalData Average Interest Rates dataset (public domain), filterable by security type.

security.description: Exact security_desc filter, e.g. 'Treasury Bills', 'Treasury Notes', 'Treasury Bonds' (optional)

since.description: Only records with record_date >= this ISO date (optional)

limit.description: Max records, newest first (1-100)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/us/treasury-rates with optional query params: security (exact security_desc, e.g. 'Treasury Bills'), since (ISO record_date floor), limit (1-100, newest first, default 12). No body. All params optional — a bare GET returns the newest records. x402 USDC on Base, no API key.
usage.outputShape: { ok:true, data:{ count, rates:[{ record_date, security_type, security, avg_interest_rate_pct }], source } } — avg_interest_rate_pct is the average rate in percent; rates newest-first.
quirks: All query params are optional; a bare GET returns the newest ~12 records across security types.
security must be the EXACT security_desc string (e.g. 'Treasury Bills', 'Treasury Notes', 'Treasury Bonds'), not a maturity/tenor.
Monthly cadence, not daily — record_date is month-end; data updates monthly and is cached 24h upstream.
This is the AVERAGE interest rate the Treasury pays on outstanding securities (FiscalData), not live secondary-market yields.
Response wraps the payload under data{}; the underlying source is the public-domain US Treasury FiscalData API.
usage.guide: US Treasury monthly average interest rates by security type, from the official FiscalData Average Interest Rates dataset. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/us/treasury-rates?security=Treasury%20Bills&limit=3 (all params optional: security = exact security_desc, since = ISO record_date floor, limit = 1-100 newest-first). No body, no API key — pay per call in USDC on Base via x402. Returns { ok, data:{ count, rates:[{ record_date, security_type, security, avg_interest_rate_pct }], source } }.

entries.name: Greeneris ISIN Validation
entries.description: Offline ISIN validation: checks ISO 6166 structure (2-letter country or XS/EU prefix, 9-char NSIN, check digit) and the Luhn base-36 checksum, returning validity plus the parsed country code, NSIN, check digit and whether it is international.

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/validate/isin?isin={ISIN} — the ISIN is a required query param (12 chars). No request body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key; the payment is the authentication.
usage.outputShape: { ok: true, data: { isin, valid (bool), country_code, nsin, check_digit, is_international (bool), source } }
quirks: ISIN passed as the required ?isin= query param, not a path segment or JSON body.

Pure offline deterministic computation (ISO 6166 structure regex + Luhn base-36 checksum) — it does NOT confirm the security exists in any reference database; source field says 'no securities reference data'.
Result body nests the payload under data; is_international is true for XS/EU-prefixed ISINs.
Provider caches results for ~1 year; sibling /validate paths (iban, email, bic, lei) are separate operations, not path-param variants.
usage.guide: Validate an ISIN before routing an order or paying a market-data API. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/validate/isin?isin=US0378331005 — ISIN is a required 12-char query param, no body. Pay per call in USDC on Base via x402 (no API key). Returns { ok, data: { isin, valid, country_code, nsin, check_digit, is_international, source } }. Offline structure + Luhn-checksum validation only; it does not verify the security exists in a reference database.

entries.name: OpenWebNinja Redfin Market Trends
entries.description: Get Redfin housing-market trends for a US/Canada region (5-digit zip, Canadian postal area, or Redfin region URL) — latest snapshot (median list/sale price, sale-to-list ratio, avg days on market, inventory, YoY change) plus multi-year monthly time series for home prices, homes sold, days on market, sale-to-list, homes sold above list and price drops.

location.description: Region to fetch market trends for. Accepts a 5-digit US zip code, a Canadian postal-code area, or a full Redfin region URL (e.g. 'https://www.redfin.com/city/30749/NY/New-York' or 'https://www.redfin.com/zipcode/90210').

country_code.description: Country to scope the lookup. Use 'US' for redfin.com or 'CA' for redfin.ca.

snapshot.description: Latest formatted snapshot: medianListPrice, medianSalePrice, medianSalePerList, medianListPerSqFt, medianSalePerSqFt, avgNumOffers, avgDownPayment, numHomesSold, numHomesOnMarket, avgDaysOnMarket, yoySalePrice, yoySalePerSqft.

home_prices.description: Home-price metrics (Median Sale Price, # of Homes Sold, Median Days on Market), each with label, current_value and a time_series[] of {date, value, yoy_change}.

demand.description: Demand metrics (Sale-to-List Price, Homes Sold Above List Price, Homes with Price Drops), each with label, current_value and a time_series[] of {date, value, yoy_change}.

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.openwebninja.com/real-time-redfin-data/market-trends?location=<zip|postal|redfin-url>&country_code=US — pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base, Polygon or Arbitrum). Results returned inline in the 200 JSON under data (region, snapshot, home_prices[], demand[]); no polling.
usage.outputShape: { status:'OK', request_id, parameters:{location,country_code}, data:{ region:{region_id,region_type,name,country_code,url}, region_name, region_url, snapshot:{medianListPrice,medianSalePrice,medianSalePerList,medianListPerSqFt,medianSalePerSqFt,avgNumOffers,avgDownPayment,numHomesSold,numHomesOnMarket,avgDaysOnMarket,yoySalePrice,yoySalePerSqft}, home_prices:[{label,current_value,time_series:[{date,value,yoy_change}]}], demand:[{label,current_value,time_series:[{date,value,yoy_change}]}] } }. Verified with location='90210' → HTTP 200: snapshot medianListPrice $7.7M, medianSalePrice $5.02M, avgDaysOnMarket 102, numHomesOnMarket 219, plus multi-year monthly time series (home_prices: Median Sale Price/# of Homes Sold/Median Days on Market; demand: Sale-to-List Price/Homes Sold Above List Price/Homes with Price Drops).
quirks: location is the only required param; it accepts a 5-digit US zip, a Canadian postal-code area, or a full Redfin region URL (city/zipcode). Set country_code=CA for redfin.ca lookups.
snapshot values are pre-formatted display strings (e.g. '$7.7M', '93.3%', '102'); the time_series values are raw numeric strings (prices in whole dollars, ratios as decimals, days as numbers).
Flat price $0.003 per call (amount 3000, USDC 6dp), quoted identically in the 402 across Base/Polygon/Arbitrum; the exact amount is always in the endpoint's own 402 challenge.
Response is synchronous in the 200 body; no job id, no polling.

Same-host namespace alias: also reachable at /realtime-real-estate-data/redfin/market-trends (same op) — indexed under the alphabetically-first prefix real-time-redfin-data. Distinct from /realtime-finance-data/market-trends, which is stock/finance movers, not real estate.
usage.guide: Get Redfin housing-market trends for a region. GET https://x402.openwebninja.com/real-time-redfin-data/market-trends with query params: ?location=<required — 5-digit US zip like '90210', a Canadian postal-code area, or a full Redfin region URL like 'https://www.redfin.com/city/30749/NY/New-York'>, &country_code=<US|CA, default US>. Pay per call via x402 (flat $0.003 USDC on Base, Polygon or Arbitrum; no API key). Read the latest headline numbers from data.snapshot (medianListPrice, medianSalePrice, medianSalePerList sale-to-list ratio, avgDaysOnMarket, numHomesOnMarket inventory, yoySalePrice), and historical trends from data.home_prices[] (Median Sale Price, # of Homes Sold, Median Days on Market) and data.demand[] (Sale-to-List Price, Homes Sold Above List Price, Homes with Price Drops), each carrying a time_series[] of {date, value, yoy_change}. Result is synchronous in the 200; no polling. Verified 2026-07-30 with location='90210' → HTTP 200, $0.003 charged, full snapshot + time series returned.

entries.name: 24kLabs Debt Payoff Planner
entries.description: Orders multiple debts by snowball (smallest balance) or avalanche (highest APR), simulates month-by-month payoff, and returns months-to-debt-free, total interest paid, and interest saved vs minimums.

debts.description: List of debts, each { name, balance, apr, min_payment }.

extra_payment.description: Extra monthly payment above the sum of minimums.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/debt-payoff-planner with a JSON body { debts:[{name,balance,apr,min_payment}], extra_payment, strategy:'snowball'|'avalanche' }. x402 USDC on Base, no API key. Result returns synchronously in the 200 body under `result`.
usage.outputShape: { service: string, result: { strategy, months_to_debt_free, years_to_debt_free, total_interest_paid, total_paid, interest_saved_vs_minimums, payoff_order:[{name,payoff_month,interest_paid}] }, latency_ms: number } — e.g. result: {"strategy":"avalanche","months_to_debt_free":38,"years_to_debt_free":3.17,"total_interest_paid":4739.3,"total_paid":24739.3,"interest_saved_vs_minimums":10842.89,"payoff_order":[{"name":"Card A","payoff_month":15,"interest_paid":731.6}, ...]}

`apr` is expressed as a whole-number percent (22 = 22%); `extra_payment` is the amount above the sum of minimums.
/api/v1/debt-payoff-planner is an identical alias on the same host (api.24klabs.ai) — do not double-pay across the two.
usage.guide: Debt payoff planner over x402. POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/debt-payoff-planner with { debts:[{name,balance,apr,min_payment}], extra_payment, strategy } where strategy is 'snowball' (smallest balance first) or 'avalanche' (highest APR first). entries.name: 24kLabs Currency Exchange Rate

Same-host namespace alias exists at /api/v1/fx-rate; index only /api/fx-rate.
Verified: converting 100 USD to EUR returned rate 0.8714, result 87.14, date 2026-07-30.
usage.guide: POST to https://api.24klabs.ai/api/fx-rate with a JSON body containing the source currency in 'from', the target currency in 'to', and the numeric 'amount' to convert (all three required; use ISO 4217 codes like USD, EUR, GBP).
