entries.name: 24kLabs Kelly Position Sizing
entries.description: Computes optimal bet/position size via the Kelly criterion from win probability, payoff (win/loss) ratio, and bankroll, with a fractional-Kelly multiplier and the resulting recommended stake.

win_prob.description: Win probability as a percentage (0-100), e.g. 55 = 55%

win_loss_ratio.description: Payoff ratio: average win divided by average loss

bankroll.description: Total bankroll/account size in currency units

win_prob.description: Probability of a win in [0, 1] (e.g. 0.6). Paired with win_loss_ratio.

win_loss_ratio.description: Payoff ratio b of win size to loss size (> 0). Paired with win_prob.

edge.description: Expected edge — alternative input, paired with odds instead of win_prob/win_loss_ratio.

odds.description: Odds b (> 0) — alternative input, paired with edge.

bankroll.description: Bankroll to size the position against.

clamp.description: Clamp the Kelly fraction to [0, 1], default true.

kelly_fraction.description: Full Kelly fraction of bankroll (before the fractional multiplier).

clamped.description: Whether the Kelly fraction was clamped to [0, 1].

applied_fraction.description: Kelly fraction after applying the fractional-Kelly multiplier.

position_size.description: Recommended stake in bankroll units (applied_fraction * bankroll).

usage.callShape: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/kelly-position-sizing with a JSON body {win_prob, win_loss_ratio, bankroll, kelly_fraction}. Synchronous — result is inline in the 200 body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key.
usage.outputShape: service (op id), result { kelly_pct (full Kelly % of bankroll), applied_kelly_pct (after fractional multiplier), edge, win_prob (as fraction), win_loss_ratio, recommended_stake (in bankroll units) }, latency_ms
quirks: win_prob is a PERCENTAGE 0-100 in the request (55 = 55%), but is echoed back in result.win_prob as a fraction (0.55).
kelly_fraction is the fractional-Kelly multiplier: 0.5 applies half-Kelly; omit or 1 for full Kelly.
recommended_stake is in the same currency units as bankroll.
The provider description mentions fixed-fractional risk sizing from stop distance and account risk %, but the verified example uses the win-probability/payoff Kelly path.
/api/v1/kelly-position-sizing is the same operation on the same host (a namespace alias) — call either; this entry pins the /api/ path.
usage.guide: Kelly-criterion position sizing. POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/kelly-position-sizing with JSON {win_prob (win probability 0-100, e.g. 55), win_loss_ratio (payoff ratio, e.g. 2), bankroll (e.g. 10000), kelly_fraction (fractional-Kelly multiplier, e.g. 0.5)}. Returns result.kelly_pct (full Kelly % of bankroll), result.applied_kelly_pct (after the fractional multiplier), result.edge, and result.recommended_stake (in bankroll units). Synchronous, x402 USDC on Base ($0.003/call), no API key.

POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/percentage-calc with a JSON body; set `op` to choose the operation (e.g. {"op":"change","from":80,"to":100}) and it returns {"service":"percentage-calc","result":{"op":"change","result":25},"latency_ms":0}. Supports percent-of, percent-change, tip, and X-is-what-percent-of-Y. x402 USDC on Base ($0.001/call), no API key.

entries.name: 24kLabs Return, CAGR & Max Drawdown
entries.description: Compute portfolio return and risk metrics from a value series (or start/end/years): total return, CAGR, annualized volatility, Sharpe ratio (given a risk-free rate) and maximum drawdown, via a pay-per-call x402 endpoint.

series.description: Ordered array of portfolio/asset values (numbers) over equally-spaced periods, e.g. [100,108,102,120,115,135]. Alternatively supply start/end/years.

periods_per_year.description: Number of periods per year for annualization (e.g. 12 for monthly, 252 for daily).

risk_free.description: Annual risk-free rate (percent) used for the Sharpe ratio, e.g. 2.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/return-cagr-drawdown with a JSON body {"series": [100,108,102,120,115,135], "periods_per_year": 12, "risk_free": 2}. series is an ordered array of values over equally-spaced periods (or supply start/end/years instead); periods_per_year annualizes; risk_free (annual %) drives the Sharpe ratio. Pure x402 (USDC on Base, no API key). Synchronous — metrics are returned inline in the response under 'result'.
usage.outputShape: JSON object {service, result:{total_return_pct, cagr_pct, years, start_value, end_value, annualized_volatility_pct, max_drawdown_pct, sharpe_ratio}, latency_ms}. Observed paid result for the example body: {total_return_pct:35, cagr_pct:105.4949, years:0.4167, start_value:100, end_value:135, annualized_volatility_pct:34.783, max_drawdown_pct:-5.5556, sharpe_ratio:2.9754}.
quirks: Input is a value series (ordered array of period values), NOT period returns; alternatively supply start/end/years per the resource description.
periods_per_year controls annualization (12=monthly, 252=daily); risk_free is an annual percent and only affects the Sharpe ratio.
max_drawdown_pct is negative; cagr_pct is annualized off the fractional 'years' derived from series length / periods_per_year.
Same-host namespace alias exists at /api/v1/return-cagr-drawdown; index only /api/return-cagr-drawdown.
Pure calculation endpoint (model 'none' per discovery); no external data source, so results are deterministic for a given input.
usage.guide: POST to https://api.24klabs.ai/api/return-cagr-drawdown with a JSON body containing 'series' (an ordered array of portfolio/asset values over equally-spaced periods, e.g. [100,108,102,120,115,135]), optional 'periods_per_year' (annualization factor, 12=monthly / 252=daily) and optional 'risk_free' (annual % risk-free rate for the Sharpe ratio). It is x402-paid (~$0.003 USDC on Base, scheme exact) and responds synchronously with result.{total_return_pct, cagr_pct, years, start_value, end_value, annualized_volatility_pct, max_drawdown_pct, sharpe_ratio}. Provide a value series, not per-period returns; alternatively supply start/end/years.

entries.name: 24kLabs Black-Scholes Option Pricer
entries.description: Prices a European call/put option and returns its Greeks (delta, gamma, theta, vega, rho) from spot, strike, days-to-expiry, rate and volatility, with optional implied-vol solve when a market price is supplied.

rate.description: Risk-free annual interest rate as a whole-number percent (5 = 5%).

volatility.description: Annualized volatility as a whole-number percent (20 = 20%).

market_price.description: Optional; when supplied the service solves for implied volatility.

op.description: Which calculation to run. REQUIRED. price returns the fair value; greeks returns price plus all greeks; iv solves for implied volatility from market_price.

S.description: Spot price of the underlying (> 0). REQUIRED.

T.description: Time to expiry in years (> 0). REQUIRED.

r.description: Risk-free rate, continuous, as a decimal (e.g. 0.05). REQUIRED.

sigma.description: Volatility as a decimal (needed for op=price and op=greeks).

q.description: Continuous dividend yield as a decimal, default 0.

market_price.description: Observed option price, used for op=iv instead of sigma.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/black-scholes-options-pricer with a JSON body { spot, strike, days_to_expiry, rate, volatility, type:'call'|'put' } (optional market_price to solve implied vol). x402 USDC on Base, no API key. Result returns synchronously in the 200 body under `result`.
usage.outputShape: { service: string, result: { price, delta, gamma, theta_per_day, vega_per_1pct, rho_per_1pct, type }, latency_ms: number } — verified live: result: {"price":0.7308,"delta":0.2265,"gamma":0.052497,"theta_per_day":-0.0318,"vega_per_1pct":0.0863,"rho_per_1pct":0.018,"type":"call"}
quirks: Deterministic Black-Scholes finance calculator, not an AI model despite the provider's generic 'ai'/'24klabs' 402 tags.
`rate` and `volatility` are whole-number percents (5 = 5%, 20 = 20%), not decimals.
Greeks are reported per-convention: theta_per_day (time decay per calendar day), vega_per_1pct and rho_per_1pct (sensitivity per 1 percentage-point move).
Supplying an optional `market_price` switches the call to solve for implied volatility.
usage.guide: European option pricer + Greeks over x402. POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/black-scholes-options-pricer with { spot, strike, days_to_expiry, rate, volatility, type } where rate and volatility are whole-number percents and type is 'call' or 'put'. Returns the fair value (price) plus delta, gamma, theta_per_day, vega_per_1pct and rho_per_1pct synchronously in the 200 body under `result`. Pass an optional market_price to solve for implied volatility instead. x402 USDC on Base ($0.005/call), no API key.

entries.name: 24kLabs Bond Price / Yield / Duration Calculator

coupon_rate.description: Annual coupon rate as a percentage, e.g. 5 = 5%

frequency.description: Coupon payments per year, e.g. 2 for semi-annual

entries.name: 24kLabs Compound Interest Projection

POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/compound-interest-projection with a JSON body {principal, annual_rate (percent), years, compounds_per_year, contribution} and pay ~$0.002 via x402 (Base USDC). entries.name: 24kLabs Impermanent Loss Calculator
entries.description: Computes impermanent loss % and hold-vs-LP value for a 50/50 liquidity pool from the volatile asset's price ratio (new/old), netting optional fees earned to show the true LP outcome.

price_ratio.description: Ratio of the volatile asset's new price to its old price (new/old).

initial_value.description: Initial USD value of the position.

fees_earned.description: Optional trading fees earned by the LP position, in USD.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/impermanent-loss-calculator with a JSON body {price_ratio, initial_value, fees_earned}. Pure x402 (USDC on Base, no API key). Synchronous: the result is returned inline in the 200 body under result.
usage.outputShape: body.service (string), body.result (object with price_ratio, impermanent_loss_pct, value_ratio_lp_vs_hold, hold_value, lp_value, lp_value_with_fees, il_dollar, net_vs_hold_with_fees), body.latency_ms (number).

POST a JSON body with price_ratio (the volatile asset's new/old price ratio), initial_value (USD size of the position), and optional fees_earned (USD). Costs ~$0.003 USDC on Base via x402 (no API key). The 200 response returns result.impermanent_loss_pct (negative %), result.hold_value vs result.lp_value, result.il_dollar (USD IL), and result.lp_value_with_fees / result.net_vs_hold_with_fees when fees_earned is supplied.

entries.name: 24kLabs Loan & Mortgage Amortization Schedule
entries.description: Computes a full loan/mortgage amortization table from principal, APR and term (plus optional extra payment): monthly payment, per-period principal/interest split, running balance, total interest, and payoff date.

apr.description: Annual percentage rate as a whole-number percent, e.g. 6.5 for 6.5%.

extra_payment.description: Optional extra monthly payment above the scheduled payment.

schedule.description: Per-period rows { period, payment, principal, interest, balance, date }.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/loan-amortization-schedule with a JSON body { principal, apr, term_years, extra_payment?, start_date? }. x402 USDC on Base, no API key. Result returns synchronously in the 200 body under `result`.
usage.outputShape: { service: string, result: { monthly_payment, payoff_months, scheduled_term_months, total_principal, total_interest, total_paid, payoff_date, months_saved, schedule:[{period,payment,principal,interest,balance,date}] } } — e.g. result: {"monthly_payment":1580.17,"payoff_months":304,"scheduled_term_months":360,"total_principal":250000,"total_interest":260001.34,"total_paid":510001.34,"payoff_date":"2049-04-01","months_saved":56,"schedule":[{"period":1,"payment":1680.17,"principal":326,"interest":1354.17,"balance":249674,"date":"2024-01-01"}, ...]}
quirks: Deterministic finance calculator, not an AI model despite the provider's generic 'ai'/'24klabs' 402 tags.
`apr` is a whole-number percent (6.5 = 6.5%); `extra_payment` is added on top of the scheduled monthly payment and shortens the payoff (result.months_saved), while `payment` rows include the extra.

`start_date` is optional (ISO YYYY-MM-DD) and just labels the per-period `date` values; `scheduled_term_months` is term_years*12 and `payoff_months` reflects early payoff when extra_payment is supplied.
/api/v1/loan-amortization-schedule is an identical alias on the same host (api.24klabs.ai) — do not double-pay across the two.
The `schedule` array is one row per month for the full term (can be hundreds of rows); the 200 body is ~33 KB for a 30-year loan.
usage.guide: Loan/mortgage amortization schedule over x402. POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/loan-amortization-schedule with { principal, apr, term_years } plus optional { extra_payment, start_date } (apr as a whole-number percent, e.g. 6.5). It returns the monthly_payment, scheduled_term_months, payoff_months (and months_saved when extra_payment is set), total_principal/total_interest/total_paid, payoff_date, and a full per-period `schedule` array of { period, payment, principal, interest, balance, date }. x402 USDC on Base ($0.003/call), no API key; result is synchronous under `result`.

entries.name: 24kLabs NPV / IRR Cashflow Evaluator
entries.description: Evaluates a cashflow series (index 0 = t0) at a given discount rate, returning net present value, internal rate of return, payback period, and profitability index.

usage.callShape: POST https://api.24klabs.ai/api/npv-irr-calculator with a JSON body {cashflows: number[], discount_rate: number} (x402, Base USDC ~$0.004). Synchronous: the evaluation is returned inline in the 200 under result.
usage.outputShape: { service, result: { npv, irr_pct, discount_rate_pct, payback_period, profitability_index, total_undiscounted }, latency_ms }
quirks: cashflows is an ordered array where index 0 is the t0 outlay (typically negative); each subsequent element is the cashflow for the next period.

entries.name: 2s Agriculture Stats

backends.inputSchema: GET query params: commodity_desc (string, REQUIRED — e.g. CORN, SOYBEANS, CATTLE), year (string, four-digit calendar year), year__GE / year__LE (string, year range bounds), state_alpha (string, 2-letter US state code), county_name (string), statisticcat_desc (string — e.g. YIELD, PRODUCTION, AREA HARVESTED, PRICE RECEIVED), agg_level_desc (string — NATIONAL/STATE/COUNTY), short_desc (string, full data-item description), freq_desc (string, frequency). No request body.
backends.outputSchema: { data: { ok (true), items[]: { commodity, year, state, county (nullable), category, dataItem, value (number|null), valueRaw (string|null), unit }, total (int), source: {provider,url,license} }, meta: { endpoint, version, caller, cost:{usd}, settlement:{txHash,network,success} } }

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/agriculture/stats?commodity_desc=CORN&state_alpha=IA&statisticcat_desc=YIELD&year=2023 (commodity_desc REQUIRED; year/year__GE/year__LE/state_alpha/county_name/statisticcat_desc/agg_level_desc/short_desc/freq_desc optional; all query params, no request body)
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. Rows under body.data.items[] (array), each: {commodity, year, state, county (null for state/national aggregate rows), category, dataItem (full NASS description e.g. 'CORN, GRAIN - YIELD, MEASURED IN BU / ACRE'), value (number or null), valueRaw (string), unit}. body.data.total = row count, body.data.ok = true, body.data.source {provider='USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) QuickStats', url, license='Public domain (US Government work)'}. Cost at body.meta.cost.usd; settlement at body.meta.settlement {txHash,network,success}.
quirks: commodity_desc is the ONLY required parameter; all filters are query-string params, not path segments or a JSON body.
Results are nested under body.data.items[] (an array even for a single row) — read items[].
county is null on state-level and national aggregate rows (a single query mixes county rows + a state total); filter by county being null/non-null to separate them.
value can be null (suppressed/withheld cells) — valueRaw carries the raw string; NASS also emits multiple dataItem variants (e.g. GRAIN vs SILAGE yield) in one response, so filter on dataItem/unit.
QuickStats caps results at 50,000 rows — a broad query returns HTTP 400 RESULT_TOO_LARGE telling you to add filters (narrow by state_alpha/year/statisticcat_desc).
US federal data only (public domain), values echo NASS units (BU / ACRE, TONS / ACRE, etc.).
Price $0.001 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key.

Narrow broad queries or a 400 RESULT_TOO_LARGE is returned (QuickStats' 50,000-row cap). Source is USDA NASS QuickStats, public domain. Verified 2026-07-30 with {commodity_desc:'CORN',state_alpha:'IA',statisticcat_desc:'YIELD',year:'2023'} -> HTTP 200, 114 rows (IA corn grain+silage yields; state-level CORN GRAIN YIELD 201 BU/ACRE), $0.001 charged (tx 0xb42f6cbe8f53c12a57af5ed821153a1408e02d6f2d2060cad2fc1bd6c6e574cd).

The response is synchronous JSON: read the schedule from body.data.items[], each row giving the report .date, .symbol, fiscal .year/.quarter, expected vs actual EPS and revenue (actuals are null until the company reports), and .hour (bmo/amc). body.data.total is the row count. entries.name: 2s Inflation Calculator
entries.description: Adjust a US dollar amount for inflation between two dates ('what is $100 in 1990 worth today?') using CPI-U (CPIAUCNS — the same not-seasonally-adjusted all-items index as the official BLS inflation calculator, data back to 1913); returns the inflation-adjusted amount, cumulative inflation %, annualized rate, and the CPI index values used on each date. Source: BLS CPI via FRED.

amount.description: Dollar amount to adjust. Required query param.

from.description: Start date, YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY. Required query param.

to.description: End date, YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY. Optional query param; defaults to the latest available CPI month.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/inflation/calculator?amount=<number>&from=<YYYY|YYYY-MM-DD>[&to=<YYYY|YYYY-MM-DD>] (x402 paid, no request body). amount and from are required query params; to is optional and defaults to the latest available CPI month.
usage.outputShape: body.data.items[0] holds the result: .amount, .from, .to (resolved), .adjustedAmount (inflation-adjusted dollars), .cumulativeInflationPct, .annualizedPct, .cpiFrom + .cpiFromDate, .cpiTo + .cpiToDate, .seriesId ('CPIAUCNS'). body.data.ok (bool), body.data.total (int, =1), body.data.source{provider:'Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis — FRED',url,license}. Billing echoed at body.meta{endpoint:'inflation.calculator',cost.usd,settlement{txHash,network,success}}.
quirks: All inputs are QUERY PARAMS on a GET request (no JSON body): ?amount=100&from=1990.
Result is nested under body.data.items[0] (a single-element array), NOT at the top level.
from and to accept a bare year (YYYY) — normalized to Jan 1 (e.g. '1990' -> 1990-01-01) — or a full YYYY-MM-DD.
to defaults to the latest available CPI month (observed cpiToDate 2026-06-01 when called on 2026-07-30) — results drift up over time as new CPI prints land.
Uses CPI-U CPIAUCNS (not seasonally adjusted, all-items) — the same series as the official BLS inflation calculator; data back to 1913. US dollars only.
Source is BLS CPI via FRED (St. Louis Fed); FRED attribution required for redistribution.
Advertises two accepts: Base USDC (eip155:8453) and Solana USDC; paid cleanly on Base at $0.0012.
usage.guide: Adjust a US dollar amount for inflation between two dates. GET https://2s.io/api/inflation/calculator?amount=<number>&from=<YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD> — amount and from are required query params; optionally add to=<YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD> (without it, it uses the latest available CPI month). No request body. Pay per call via x402 ($0.0012 USDC on Base eip155:8453, also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key, no signup. Result is synchronous JSON: read body.data.items[0] — .adjustedAmount is the inflation-adjusted value, plus .cumulativeInflationPct, .annualizedPct, and the CPI index values used (.cpiFrom/.cpiTo with their dates) and .seriesId (CPIAUCNS). Uses CPI-U (BLS CPI via FRED), the same index as the official BLS calculator, data back to 1913. Verified 2026-07-30 with amount=100&from=1990 -> HTTP 200: $100 (1990) = $262.13 today, 162.13% cumulative / 2.68% annualized, $0.0012 charged (tx 0x5df975993e1195277eed10b8946c3cdebca960cf0e916fae956f277f079b9fab).

entries.name: 2s Company News
entries.description: Fetch recent news articles about a specific US-listed company by ticker — headlines with source, summary, URL, image, related symbol, category, and publish time (newest first), aggregated by Finnhub. Optional from/to date window (defaults to the last 14 days).

ticker.description: US-listed ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL. Required.

from.description: Start of the news window, YYYY-MM-DD. Optional; defaults to ~14 days ago.

to.description: End of the news window, YYYY-MM-DD. Optional; defaults to today.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/stocks/company-news?ticker=AAPL (x402 paid, no request body). Optional query params: from and to (YYYY-MM-DD) to set the news window; defaults to the last ~14 days.
usage.outputShape: body.data.items[] (array of news articles, newest first). Each item: .datetime (ISO), .headline, .source (publisher), .summary, .url (article link), .category, .image, .related (ticker), .id. body.data.ok, body.data.total (total available; the returned items[] may be a capped page — observed 100 items with total 248), body.data.meta{symbol,from,to} (the resolved window), body.data.source{provider:'Finnhub',url,license}. Settlement/cost echoed at body.meta{endpoint,cost.usd,settlement{txHash,network,success}}.
quirks: Result is nested under body.data.items[] — NOT the top-level {ok,total,items} shown in the 402 bazaar example.
ticker is a query-string param, not a path segment.
body.data.total can exceed items[].length (observed total 248 with 100 items returned) — items[] is a newest-first page, not the full set.
News is aggregated by Finnhub (attribution required per Finnhub API terms); coverage is US-listed companies only.
Provider offers a free trial: append ?trial=1 (or header X-2s-Trial:1) for one free real call per endpoint per hour (not used for the registry price).
usage.guide: Call GET https://2s.io/api/stocks/company-news with a required query param ticker set to a US-listed ticker symbol (e.g. ?ticker=AAPL). Optionally narrow the window with from and to (YYYY-MM-DD); without them it returns roughly the last 14 days. It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.001 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key, no signup — the pay layer handles the 402. The response is synchronous JSON: read the articles from body.data.items[] (newest first) — each has .headline, .source, .summary, .url, .datetime, .image, and .related (the ticker). body.data.total is the total available and may be larger than the returned page. News is aggregated by Finnhub.

entries.name: 2s Insider Sentiment
entries.description: Aggregated monthly insider sentiment for a US-listed company: net change in insider share holdings and Finnhub's MSPR (Monthly Share Purchase Ratio, -100 to +100) per month over a chosen window.

ticker.description: US-listed ticker, e.g. AAPL. Required.

from.description: Window start date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional; defaults to ~1 year ago.

to.description: Window end date (YYYY-MM-DD). Optional; defaults to today.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/stocks/insider-sentiment?ticker=AAPL (x402 paid, no request body). ticker is a required query param; from/to (YYYY-MM-DD) are optional window bounds.
usage.outputShape: body.data.items[] (one object per month with any insider activity). Each item: .symbol, .year (integer), .month (1-12 integer), .change (net change in insider share holdings, signed integer), .mspr (Monthly Share Purchase Ratio, -100..+100 float; higher = more net insider buying). body.data.total (count), body.data.source{provider:'Finnhub',url,license}, body.data.meta{symbol,from,to} (the resolved window). Settlement/cost echoed at body.meta{endpoint,cost.usd,settlement{txHash,network,success}}.
quirks: Result is nested under body.data.items[] — read items[], not a top-level items.
ticker/from/to are query-string params, not path segments or a request body.
Only months with insider activity are returned (observed 11 rows for a ~1-year AAPL window), so items[] is sparse — do not assume 12 consecutive months.
mspr can pin to exactly -100 or +100 for months with all-selling or all-buying activity.
Data is Finnhub-sourced (US-listed tickers); attribution is required per Finnhub API terms.
The x402 bazaar output example is unwrapped (top-level ok/items); the real paid response wraps it under body.data with settlement in body.meta.
usage.guide: Call GET https://2s.io/api/stocks/insider-sentiment with a required query param ticker set to a US-listed symbol (e.g. ?ticker=AAPL); optionally add from and to (YYYY-MM-DD) to bound the window (defaults to ~1 year). It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.001 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key or signup — the pay layer handles the 402. The response is synchronous JSON: read one row per active month from body.data.items[], each with .year, .month, .change (net insider share-holding change) and .mspr (Finnhub Monthly Share Purchase Ratio, -100..+100 — higher means more net insider buying). Only months with activity appear, so the array is sparse. Data is by Finnhub.

ticker.description: US-listed ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL, MSFT, BRK.B. Required.

Settlement/cost echoed at body.meta{endpoint,cost.usd,settlement{txHash,network,success}}.

ticker is a query-string param, not a path segment or request body.

US-listed tickers only; market data sourced from Massive (formerly Polygon.io).

It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.0018 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC); no API key, no signup — the pay layer handles the 402. entries.name: Agentstools Macro Compare
entries.description: Compare one macroeconomic or development indicator (GDP per capita, inflation, unemployment, govt debt, CO2 per capita, etc.) across two or more countries in a single call, returning the latest cited value per country, a highest-to-lowest ranking, and computed signals (max, min, spread, mean), each value sourced to World Bank/IMF.

indicator.description: Canonical indicator key (e.g. gdp_current_usd, gdp_per_capita_usd, gdp_growth, inflation_cpi, unemployment, govt_debt_gdp, current_account_gdp, population, life_expectancy, gini, co2_per_capita, internet_users_pct) or a raw World Bank series code (e.g. NY.GDP.PCAP.CD).

country.description: Two or more countries as ISO-3166 alpha-2, alpha-3, or names, comma-separated (at least two).

year.description: Optional reference year; the latest available value at or before it is used (default: latest).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/macro/compare with query params ?indicator=<key>&country=<c1,c2,...>[&year=<int>]. `indicator` is a canonical key or raw World Bank code; `country` is a comma-separated list of AT LEAST TWO ISO-2/ISO-3 codes or names; optional `year` picks the latest value at or before it. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: indicator, label, unit, category, ranking[] (each {country, country_iso3, year, value, rank, source, source_code, unit}, sorted highest-to-lowest), signals {count, max:{country_iso3,value}, min:{country_iso3,value}, spread, mean}, and attribution[] (source strings). Verified live for {indicator:gdp_per_capita_usd, country:US,DE,JP,CN}: ranking USA 90026.52 (rank 1), Germany 60496.44 (2), Japan 35951.04 (3), China 13861.97 (4); signals {count:4, spread:76164.55, mean:50083.99}; attribution ["Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators (CC-BY 4.0)"].
quirks: `country` MUST list at least two countries (comma-separated); fewer than two returns HTTP 400.
An unknown indicator or country returns 400; no data returns 404; an upstream data-source failure returns 502.
Countries accept ISO-3166 alpha-2 (US), alpha-3 (USA), or plain names, mixed freely.
For each country the service takes the latest available value at or before the optional `year`; the year actually used is echoed per row in `ranking[].year`.

Every value is cited: ranking rows carry source + source_code (e.g. worldbank / NY.GDP.PCAP.CD) and the top-level attribution[] lists every source used — include the attribution when redistributing (World Bank WDI is CC-BY 4.0; IMF WEO requires attribution).

Sibling ops on this host are different: /macro/indicator returns a cited time-series for one indicator across countries ($0.01); /macro/forecast returns IMF WEO forward-looking forecasts for one country ($0.01).
usage.guide: Compare one macroeconomic/development indicator across several countries in a single keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/macro/compare?indicator=<key>&country=<c1,c2,...>[&year=<int>]. `indicator` is a canonical key (gdp_current_usd, gdp_per_capita_usd, gdp_growth, inflation_cpi, unemployment, govt_debt_gdp, current_account_gdp, population, life_expectancy, gini, co2_per_capita, internet_users_pct, ...) or a raw World Bank code (e.g. NY.GDP.PCAP.CD); `country` is a comma-separated list of AT LEAST TWO ISO-2/ISO-3 codes or names; optional `year` picks the latest value at or before that year. Synchronous — the 200 body carries {indicator, label, unit, category, ranking[] (highest-to-lowest, each cited to its source), signals{count,max,min,spread,mean}, attribution[]}. Fewer than two countries or an unknown key/country returns 400; no data 404; upstream failure 502. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: ?indicator=gdp_per_capita_usd&country=US,DE,JP,CN -> USA ranks 1 ($90,026), China ranks 4 ($13,862), spread 76,164.

entries.name: Agentstools Macro Forecast
entries.description: Forward-looking IMF World Economic Outlook (WEO) macro forecasts for one country — real GDP growth, inflation, nominal GDP, GDP per capita, government debt, current account and unemployment — returned as cited year-to-value series that include the IMF's projected future years.

country.description: A single country as ISO-3166 alpha-2, alpha-3, or a common name (e.g. US, USA, United States). Required.

indicators.description: Comma-separated forecast keys; default all. One or more of: real_gdp_growth, inflation, gdp_usd, gdp_per_capita_usd, govt_debt_gdp, current_account_gdp, unemployment.

note.description: Note that values past the latest actual year are IMF projections.

source_code.description: IMF WEO series code (e.g. NGDP_RPCH, PCPIPCH).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/macro/forecast with query params: country (required — ISO-2, ISO-3 or name) and indicators (optional — comma-separated forecast keys from [real_gdp_growth, inflation, gdp_usd, gdp_per_capita_usd, govt_debt_gdp, current_account_gdp, unemployment], default all). No request body. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: country, country_iso3, note (projections disclaimer), forecasts[] (one per requested indicator, each with indicator, label, unit, source='imf', source_code (WEO code), country_iso3, and values[] of {year, value}), and attribution[] (required IMF WEO strings). Verified live for {country:US, indicators:real_gdp_growth,inflation}: two series spanning 1980..2031 (years past the latest actual, e.g. 2026-2031, are IMF projections), e.g. real_gdp_growth 2026=2.3, 2027=2.1; inflation 2026=3.2. source_code NGDP_RPCH (growth) and PCPIPCH (inflation).
quirks: country is REQUIRED; omit it and the call 400s. Accepts ISO-2 (US), ISO-3 (USA) or a common name.
indicators is optional and comma-separated; omit it to get ALL forecast series. Valid keys: real_gdp_growth, inflation, gdp_usd, gdp_per_capita_usd, govt_debt_gdp, current_account_gdp, unemployment.
Each series' values[] mixes historical actuals with IMF PROJECTIONS — years past the latest actual (e.g. 2026+) are forecasts, as flagged by the response `note`. Verified series ran 1980..2031.
Values are cited to the IMF World Economic Outlook (source_code is the WEO series code); the required `attribution` string must be preserved on redisplay.
The upstream IMF endpoint occasionally returns a transient 403; the service retries internally.
Errors: unknown country or forecast key -> 400, no data -> 404, upstream failure -> 502.
usage.guide: Get forward-looking IMF World Economic Outlook macro forecasts for a country with one keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/macro/forecast?country=<ISO-2|ISO-3|name>&indicators=<comma-separated keys>. `country` is required; `indicators` is optional (comma-separated from real_gdp_growth, inflation, gdp_usd, gdp_per_capita_usd, govt_debt_gdp, current_account_gdp, unemployment) and defaults to all series. Synchronous — the 200 body carries {country, country_iso3, note, forecasts[], attribution[]}; each forecasts[] item is an indicator with a values[] list of {year, value} that INCLUDES the IMF's projected future years past the latest actual (the differentiator versus history-only sources). Every value is cited to the IMF WEO (source_code) and the attribution[] must be shown. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {country:'US', indicators:'real_gdp_growth,inflation'} -> real_gdp_growth 2026=2.3%, inflation 2026=3.2%, series through 2031.

entries.name: Agentstools Macro Indicator
entries.description: One macroeconomic or development indicator (GDP, inflation, unemployment, population, debt, CO2, etc.) for one or more countries as a cited time-series, fused from World Bank / IMF (and optionally FRED) with per-value source, year and country provenance.

indicator.description: Canonical indicator key or a raw World Bank series code such as NY.GDP.MKTP.CD.

country.description: One or more countries as ISO-2, ISO-3, name, or a World Bank aggregate code (e.g. WLD, EUU), comma-separated for several at once.

years.description: A single year or a Y1:Y2 range, e.g. 2015:2023.

range.description: Most recent N years (ignored when years is set).

source.description: Preferred source (default auto = first candidate with data).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/macro/indicator with QUERY params (no body): indicator (required, canonical key or raw World Bank code), country (required, one or more ISO-2/ISO-3/name/aggregate codes comma-separated), and one of years (single year or Y1:Y2 range) or range (most recent N years, 1-65); optional source in [auto, worldbank, imf, fred]. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: indicator (string), label (human name, e.g. 'GDP (current US$)'), unit (string), category (string), year_range {from, to}, countries[] each {country, country_iso3, source, source_code, unit, latest {year, value, source, source_code, country_iso3, unit}, values[] (full history, same value shape)}, and attribution[] (source strings, e.g. 'Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators (CC-BY 4.0)'). Verified live for {indicator:gdp_current_usd, country:US,DE, range:5}: USA latest 2025 value 30769700000000 and Germany latest 2025 value 5050922925047.05, both sourced worldbank / NY.GDP.MKTP.CD.
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.
The param is `country` (singular) even for several countries; pass them comma-separated, e.g. country=US,DE.

indicator accepts either a canonical key (gdp_current_usd, gdp_per_capita_usd, gdp_growth, inflation_cpi, unemployment, population, govt_debt_gdp, current_account_gdp, life_expectancy, gini, co2_per_capita, internet_users_pct, and ~17 more) or a raw World Bank series code such as NY.GDP.MKTP.CD.
Window: use `years` (a single year or a Y1:Y2 range like 2015:2023) OR `range` (most recent N years, 1-65); when both are set, `years` wins and `range` is ignored.

For each country the service resolves the indicator across an ordered candidate-source list and takes the first with data, so per-country `source`/`source_code` may differ; force one with source=worldbank|imf|fred (default auto).
Attribution is required (World Bank data is CC-BY 4.0; IMF WEO requires attribution) — the attribution[] strings are returned so you can display them.
Errors: unknown indicator or country -> 400, empty result -> 404, upstream source failure -> 502.
usage.guide: Fetch one macroeconomic or development indicator for one or more countries as a cited time-series with a single keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/macro/indicator with QUERY params: indicator (required — a canonical key like gdp_current_usd, inflation_cpi, unemployment, population, govt_debt_gdp, co2_per_capita, or a raw World Bank code such as NY.GDP.MKTP.CD), country (required — one or more ISO-2/ISO-3/name/aggregate codes comma-separated, e.g. US,DE), plus a window via years (a single year or a Y1:Y2 range like 2015:2023) or range (most recent N years, 1-65). Optional source=auto|worldbank|imf|fred picks the provenance (default auto = first candidate source with data). Synchronous — the 200 body carries indicator, label, unit, category, year_range, countries[] (each with latest + full values[] history tagged by source/year/ISO3/unit), and attribution[]. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {indicator:'gdp_current_usd', country:'US,DE', range:5} -> USA & Germany GDP current-USD series 2021-2025 from World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD.

entries.name: Agentstools Income Tax Estimate
entries.description: Estimates US federal individual income tax for a given tax year from a layered progressive bracket table — returns taxable income, federal tax, marginal and effective rates, and a per-bracket breakdown, with an optional flat state estimate; pure computation over your inputs, not tax advice.

gross_income.description: Total gross income before deductions (>= 0). REQUIRED.

deductions.description: Total deductions; omit to use the standard deduction.

state.description: Optional two-letter state code to add a flat-state income estimate and combined total.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/tax/income?gross_income=<AMOUNT>&filing_status=<STATUS>&tax_year=<YEAR> — all inputs are query params, no request body. Only gross_income is required (filing_status defaults single, tax_year defaults 2026). Optional deductions (omit for standard deduction) and a two-letter state code. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.005. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: filing_status (string echo), gross_income (number echo), deduction_kind ("standard" | "itemized"), standard_deduction (number), deduction_used (number actually applied), taxable_income (number = gross minus deduction_used), federal_tax (number USD), marginal_rate (number, top bracket reached e.g. 0.22), effective_rate (number = tax over gross income e.g. 0.1317), brackets[] (per-bracket: rate, from, to, amount_in_bracket, tax), tax_year (int), source (string, cites IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 etc.), disclaimer (string). When a state code is supplied, a flat-state estimate and combined total are added.
quirks: gross_income is the ONLY required input and is passed as a query param on a GET (no body); omitting it 4xx.
filing_status enum: single | married_jointly | married_separately | head_of_household (default single). tax_year defaults 2026.
Omit deductions to use the standard deduction (deduction_kind="standard"); supply deductions to itemize.
Supply an optional two-letter state code to add a flat-state income estimate and a combined federal+state total.
Pure local computation from a progressive bracket table (each rate applies only to its income slice); a reference estimate, NOT tax advice.

Verified live: single, gross 100000, 2026 -> taxable_income 83900, federal_tax 13170, marginal_rate 0.22, effective_rate 0.1317, standard_deduction 16100, with a 3-tier bracket breakdown (10%/12%/22%).
usage.guide: Estimate US federal individual income tax for a tax year. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/tax/income?gross_income=<AMOUNT> (required) with optional filing_status (single | married_jointly | married_separately | head_of_household, default single), tax_year (default 2026), deductions (omit for standard deduction), and a two-letter state code for a flat-state estimate + combined total. No body. Pays $0.005 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns taxable_income, federal_tax, marginal_rate, effective_rate, standard_deduction/deduction_used, and a per-bracket breakdown, cited to IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32. Pure computation, a reference estimate, not tax advice. Verified live: single/gross 100000/2026 -> taxable 83900, federal_tax 13170, marginal 0.22, effective 0.1317.

entries.name: x402node Commodity Price
entries.description: Live spot/futures price for a given commodity (cocoa, coffee, grains, gold, silver, oil, gas, copper, etc.) versus USD via a single templated zero-param x402 GET, returning price, unit, source and timestamp.

commodity.description: Commodity name (1st path segment). Supported enum: brent, cattle, cocoa, coffee, copper, corn, cotton, gas, gold, hogs, juice, oats, palladium, platinum, rice, silver, soybean, sugar, wheat, wti.

quote.description: Quote currency (2nd path segment). Only 'usd' is exposed across the family.

slug.description: Ticker slug (3rd path segment). Usually <commodity>-usd, but metals/energy differ: gold->xau-usd, silver->xag-usd, platinum->xpt-usd, palladium->xpd-usd, gas->natgas-usd (all others, e.g. cocoa->cocoa-usd).

format.description: Optional response format hint (query param). Not required.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/commodity/price/{commodity}/{quote}/{slug} — e.g. /commodity/price/cocoa/usd/cocoa-usd (zero-param path; optional ?format= hint, no JSON body). Pay via x402 (USDC on Base or Solana); fixed $0.005. run.ts substitutes the {commodity}/{quote}/{slug} path segments at call time.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON object (verified from paid 200 for COCOA): commodity (e.g. 'COCOA'), symbol (Yahoo ticker, e.g. 'CC=F'), price (number, e.g. 5118), currency (e.g. 'USD'), unit (e.g. 'per metric ton'), source (e.g. 'Yahoo Finance'), as_of (ISO-8601 UTC timestamp), note (human-readable 'COCOA = 5118 USD per metric ton.'), plus a marketing _hint field to ignore.
quirks: TEMPLATED path-param family /commodity/price/{commodity}/{quote}/{slug}: the varying segments are the input, so this is ONE service, not one entry per commodity. Only cocoa was in this discovery sweep; the rest are same-host path-param variants indexed under this templated service.

The 3rd path segment is a distinct ticker slug, NOT always <commodity>-usd: cocoa->cocoa-usd, coffee->coffee-usd, corn->corn-usd, cotton->cotton-usd, wheat->wheat-usd, soybean->soybean-usd, sugar->sugar-usd, rice->rice-usd, oats->oats-usd, juice->juice-usd, cattle->cattle-usd, hogs->hogs-usd, copper->copper-usd, brent->brent-usd, wti->wti-usd — BUT gold->xau-usd, silver->xag-usd, platinum->xpt-usd, palladium->xpd-usd, gas->natgas-usd. Use the correct slug per the mapping.

Supported commodity enum (openapi, 21 pairs, all vs USD): brent, cattle, cocoa, coffee, copper, corn, cotton, gas, gold, hogs, juice, oats, palladium, platinum, rice, silver, soybean, sugar, wheat, wti.
Zero-parameter GET at the fixed pair path — no query or body needed (optional ?format= hint only); just call the path.
Underlying source is Yahoo Finance (paid response source='Yahoo Finance', symbol e.g. 'CC=F') — a futures/spot quote, not an onchain oracle. Unit varies by commodity (e.g. cocoa 'per metric ton').
Distinct from x402node's universal query-based /commodity/price?symbol=<c>&lang= endpoint ($0.01, auto-localizes currency/unit) — that is a separate, pricier operation.
Different service from the free BlockRun 'Commodity Price' (blockrun.ai/api/v1/commodity/price/{sym}, Pyth feeds, $0): different provider/host/source/shape/price — not a backend of it.
Live 402 advertises BOTH a Base (eip155:8453 USDC) and a Solana (USDC) accept at the same 5000-atomic ($0.005) amount; either network works. Paid via Base.
Response includes a marketing _hint field that can be ignored.
usage.guide: Fetch a live commodity price with a single zero-argument GET to https://api.x402node.dev/commodity/price/{commodity}/{quote}/{slug} — e.g. /commodity/price/cocoa/usd/cocoa-usd. No API key — pay per call over x402 (USDC on Base or Solana; this run cost $0.005). Substitute the path: {commodity} (cocoa/coffee/corn/gold/silver/wti/brent/gas/copper/... — 21 supported), {quote} is always usd, and {slug} is the ticker slug which is usually <commodity>-usd but differs for metals/energy (gold->xau-usd, silver->xag-usd, platinum->xpt-usd, palladium->xpd-usd, gas->natgas-usd). Read body.price (number), body.currency + body.unit (e.g. USD 'per metric ton'), body.as_of (quote timestamp), body.source (provenance, 'Yahoo Finance'); body.note gives a ready-to-read summary and body.symbol is the Yahoo ticker. Ignore _hint. Synchronous — no polling. For localized currency/unit use the separate universal /commodity/price?symbol= endpoint instead.

entries.name: x402node FX Carry Signal
entries.description: Ranked FX carry-trade signal: computes carry (policy-rate) differentials across ~32 major currencies from BIS central-bank policy rates (dataset CBPOL) and returns currency pairs ranked by spread (borrow low-yield, hold high-yield). Optionally pin the funding currency.

top.description: Optional. Return the top N carry opportunities, default 15, max 100. Passed as a query param.

funder.description: Optional. Funding (short/borrow) currency code, e.g. JPY/CHF/EUR; only returns carry opportunities that short that currency. Passed as a query param.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/finance/carry?top=<N>&funder=<CCY> (x402 Base or Solana USDC, no body). Both params optional: top defaults to 15 (max 100); funder pins the funding/short currency (e.g. JPY). Pay the fixed $0.02 x402 quote and retry with the payment header.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous flat JSON (from the paid 200): { source:'Computed from BIS central bank policy rates (dataset CBPOL)', as_of:'2026-07-21', method:'carry_spread = long policy rate − short(funding) policy rate...', funder:'any', universe_size:32, highest_yield:{ccy:'TRY',rate:37}, lowest_yield:{ccy:'CHF',rate:0}, count:10, carry_ranking:[{rank:1, pair:'TRY/CHF', long:'TRY', short:'CHF', carry_spread:37, long_rate:37, short_rate:0, long_country:'Türkiye', short_country:'Switzerland'}, ...], note: caveat string, _hint: promo string }.
quirks: Both params (top, funder) are query params and OPTIONAL — a bare GET works and returns the default top 15. There are NO required inputs.
Fixed price ($0.02 in OpenAPI x-payment-info, matching the 20000-atomic live 402 accept) — not a dynamic quote.
Live 402 advertises BOTH a Base (eip155:8453 USDC) and a Solana (USDC) accept at the same 20000-atomic amount; either network works. Paid via Base.

carry_spread is the policy-rate differential in percentage points ONLY — the provider note explicitly states it does NOT account for expected FX moves, volatility, or rollover/swap costs; combine with /finance/forex for the FX leg. Not investment advice.
funder=<CCY> filters to opportunities that short/borrow that currency; when omitted, funder is reported as 'any' and the ranking spans all positive spreads desc.
Response includes a promotional _hint field that can be ignored.
usage.guide: Get a ranked FX carry-trade signal in one paid call. Issue a plain GET to https://api.x402node.dev/finance/carry (optionally add top=<N> to cap the list, default 15 / max 100, and funder=<CCY> to only see opportunities that short a given funding currency such as JPY or CHF) with no body, and pay the fixed x402 quote (~$0.02 USDC on Base or Solana, no API key). On the 200, read the flat JSON: `carry_ranking[]` lists currency pairs sorted by `carry_spread` (long policy rate minus short/funding rate, in percentage points) with long/short currency, rates and countries; `highest_yield`/`lowest_yield` and `universe_size` summarize the set; `as_of` is the BIS data date. It is the policy-rate differential only — combine with /finance/forex for the FX leg. Synchronous — no polling.

entries.name: x402node Central Bank Policy Rates
entries.description: Current central-bank policy (benchmark) interest rates for 46 countries/areas — Fed, ECB, BoJ, BoE, PBoC and more — normalized from BIS official data (dataset CBPOL), each with the setting central bank and last-change date. Optionally filter to one country.

country.description: Optional. 2-letter area/region code to filter to a single central bank (e.g. us/cn/jp/gb/xm for euro area). Omit to return all 46. Passed as a query param.

detail.description: Optional. Set to 'full' to append rate-definition notes (compilation). Passed as a query param.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/finance/central-rates?country=<2-letter code>&detail=full (x402 Base or Solana USDC, no body). Both params optional: a bare GET returns all 46 central banks; country filters to one (e.g. us/jp/xm); detail=full adds definition notes. Pay the fixed $0.012 x402 quote and retry with the payment header.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous flat JSON (from the paid 200): { source:'Bank for International Settlements (BIS), dataset CBPOL', as_of:'2026-07-21', count:46, rates:[{ area:'US', country:'United States', rate:3.625, date:'2026-07-21', source:'US Federal Reserve System' }, { area:'XM', country:'Euro area', rate:2.25, date:'2026-07-21', source:'European Central Bank' }, { area:'JP', country:'Japan', rate:1, date:'2026-07-21', source:'Bank of Japan' }, ...], note: caveat string, _hint: promo string }.
quirks: Both params (country, detail) are query params and OPTIONAL — a bare GET works and returns all 46 central banks. There are NO required inputs (documented example input is {}).
Fixed price ($0.012 in OpenAPI x-payment-info, matching the 12000-atomic live 402 accept) — not a dynamic quote.
Live 402 advertises BOTH a Base (eip155:8453 USDC) and a Solana (USDC) accept at the same 12000-atomic amount; either network works. Paid via Base.

rate is the policy rate in percent; date is the last change/observation date per bank (some legacy euro-area members show a 1998-12-31 date because their national rate was superseded by the ECB). Rates are end-of-period, normalized from BIS.
country=<code> uses a 2-letter area code (us/cn/jp/gb; xm = euro area), NOT a full ISO country name.
Response includes a promotional _hint field that can be ignored. For carry/rate-differential analysis, the provider's /finance/carry endpoint derives spreads from this same data.
usage.guide: Get current central-bank policy rates in one paid call. Issue a plain GET to https://api.x402node.dev/finance/central-rates (optionally add country=<2-letter code> such as us/jp/gb/xm to filter to one central bank, or detail=full for definition notes) with no body, and pay the fixed x402 quote (~$0.012 USDC on Base or Solana, no API key). On the 200, read the flat JSON: `rates[]` lists each central bank's { area, country, rate (percent), date (last change), source } — e.g. Fed 3.625, ECB/euro-area 2.25, BoJ 1, PBoC 3; `source` is BIS dataset CBPOL, `as_of` is the data date, `count` the number of banks. Synchronous — no polling. For rate-differential/carry signals combine with /finance/carry or /finance/forex.

entries.name: X402node Currency Convert
entries.description: Convert an amount between two fiat currencies at the current ECB reference rate (via Frankfurter); returns the input amount, converted amount, the exchange rate, and the rate date.

amount.description: Amount of the `from` currency to convert (optional; defaults handled server-side).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/finance/convert?amount=<N>&from=<ISO4217>&to=<ISO4217> — `from` and `to` are required query params, `amount` is optional; no request body. Unpaid request returns HTTP 402; retry with an X-PAYMENT header ($0.005 USDC on Base eip155:8453 or Solana).
usage.outputShape: Flat JSON: from, to (echoed ISO codes); amount (input number); rate (from->to ECB reference rate); converted (amount*rate); date (YYYY-MM-DD ECB business day); source ('ECB via Frankfurter'); plus a boilerplate _hint field (ignore).
quirks: Synchronous — the conversion result is returned inline in the 200 body, no polling.
Fiat-only: rates are ECB reference rates via Frankfurter (no crypto pairs). `date` reflects the ECB business day, so it can lag on weekends/holidays.
Pay on Base (USDC) or Solana (USDC) — either network works; the 402 quote is the same $0.005 on both.
The 402 body carries only a boilerplate _hint; the full x402 accepts are in the `payment-required` response header.
usage.guide: Convert an amount between two fiat currencies at the current ECB reference rate. Issue GET https://api.x402node.dev/finance/convert with three query params: from and to (required ISO 4217 codes, e.g. from=USD&to=EUR) and amount (optional number, e.g. amount=100); no request body. An unpaid request returns HTTP 402 with x402 payment requirements — retry with an X-PAYMENT header ($0.005 USDC on Base eip155:8453 or Solana, no API key). The 200 response is synchronous flat JSON: read `converted` for the result and `rate` for the exchange rate, with `date` (ECB business day) and `source` ('ECB via Frankfurter') for provenance. Fiat only — for crypto pairs use a crypto/forex converter instead. Verified USD->EUR 100 = 87.138 at rate 0.87138.

entries.name: x402node Economic Calendar
entries.description: Upcoming high-impact macroeconomic events from the live Forex Factory calendar (central-bank rate decisions, FOMC, CPI, NFP, GDP) — each with currency, scheduled time, forecast/previous values and minutes until release. Filter by impact, currency and time window.

impact.description: Minimum impact: high (default), medium, low, or all. Passed as a query param.

currency.description: Filter by currency code(s), comma = OR, e.g. USD,EUR (default all). Passed as a query param.

hours.description: Optional. Only events within the next N hours. Passed as a query param.

upcoming.description: true (default) for future events only; false to include past events this/next week. Passed as a query param.

limit.description: Max events to return, 1-100 (default 30). Passed as a query param.

in_minutes.description: Minutes until release, relative to now.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/finance/econ-calendar?impact=high&limit=20 (x402 Base or Solana USDC, no body). All params optional query params: impact (high default / medium / low / all), currency (comma = OR, e.g. USD,EUR), hours (within next N hours), upcoming (true default / false to include past this/next week), limit (1-100, default 30). Pay the fixed $0.01 x402 quote and retry with the payment header.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous flat JSON (from the paid 200): { count:5, filter:{ impact:'high', currency:'all', within_hours:null, upcoming_only:true }, next_high_impact:{ title:'BOJ Policy Rate', currency:'JPY', date:'2026-07-30T22:50:00-04:00', in_minutes:50 }, events:[{ title:'BOJ Policy Rate', currency:'JPY', impact:'High', date:'2026-07-30T22:50:00-04:00', in_minutes:50, forecast:'<1.00%', previous:'<1.00%', actual:null }, ...], source:'Forex Factory weekly calendar', note:'... Not financial advice.', _hint: promo string }. Each event carries currency, impact, event-local ISO date, in_minutes-until-release, and forecast/previous/actual (actual is null until the release fires).
quirks: All five params (impact, currency, hours, upcoming, limit) are OPTIONAL query params — a bare GET works and returns the default (impact=high, limit=30, upcoming only). There are NO required inputs.
Fixed price ($0.01 in OpenAPI x-payment-info, matching the 10000-atomic live 402 accept) — not a dynamic quote.
Live 402 advertises BOTH a Base (eip155:8453 USDC) and a Solana (USDC) accept at the same 10000-atomic amount; either network works. Paid via Base.

Data is the live Forex Factory weekly calendar — a forward-looking schedule, so results are time-sensitive and change as events fire; in_minutes is computed relative to request time and actual is null until a release publishes.
date is an event-LOCAL ISO timestamp (includes the source offset, e.g. -04:00), not UTC-normalized.
Provider explicitly labels the payload 'Not financial advice'. Response includes a promotional _hint field that can be ignored.
usage.guide: Get upcoming high-impact macro events in one paid call. Issue a plain GET to https://api.x402node.dev/finance/econ-calendar (optionally add impact=<high|medium|low|all>, currency=<CODE[,CODE]>, hours=<N>, upcoming=<true|false>, limit=<1-100>) with no body, and pay the fixed x402 quote (~$0.01 USDC on Base or Solana, no API key). On the 200, read the flat JSON: `events[]` lists each event with title, currency, impact, event-local ISO `date`, `in_minutes` until release, and `forecast`/`previous`/`actual` values; `next_high_impact` surfaces the soonest high-impact event; `count`, `filter` and `source` (Forex Factory weekly calendar) summarize the set. It is a forward-looking schedule (actual is null until release) — re-fetch to refresh. Synchronous — no polling. Not financial advice.

entries.name: x402node Forex Rates
entries.description: Real-time European Central Bank reference exchange rates (via Frankfurter) for a base currency, with batchable targets and inverse rates in one call.

from.description: Base currency code (single), e.g. USD. Alias: base. Default USD. Passed as a query param.

to.description: Target currency or comma-separated list, e.g. EUR or EUR,GBP,JPY,CNY. Alias: symbols. Passed as a query param.

rates.description: Map of target currency code -> rate (1 unit of base in that target).

inverse_rates.description: Map of target currency code -> inverse rate (1 unit of that target in base).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/finance/forex?from=USD&to=EUR (x402 Base or Solana USDC, no body). from is a query param (alias: base, default USD); to is a query param (alias: symbols) that accepts a single code or a comma-separated batch, e.g. to=EUR,GBP,JPY,CNY. Pay the fixed $0.008 x402 quote and retry with the payment header.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous flat JSON (from the paid 200): { base:'USD', date:'2026-07-30', rates:{ CNY:6.7551, EUR:0.87138, GBP:0.74691, JPY:162.94 }, inverse_rates:{ CNY:0.148036, EUR:1.147605, GBP:1.338849, JPY:0.006137 }, source:'ECB via Frankfurter', note:'...', _hint: promo string }. rates[X] = 1 base in target X; inverse_rates[X] = 1 target X in base.
quirks: from/to are query params (aliases base/symbols), never a body; to is effectively required to get useful output (omitting it returns no rates).
to is batchable: pass a comma-separated list (to=EUR,GBP,JPY,CNY) to get all pairs in one call at the same fixed price.
Uniquely returns inverse_rates alongside rates (1 target in base) in the same payload.
Fixed price ($0.008 in OpenAPI x-payment-info, matching the 8000-atomic live 402 accept) - not a dynamic quote.
Live 402 advertises BOTH a Base (eip155:8453 USDC) and a Solana (USDC) accept at the same 8000-atomic amount; either network works. Paid via Base.

Rates are ECB reference rates (via frankfurter.app), published once per working day (~16:00 CET) - not a live tradable/intraday FX feed; date reflects the ECB business day and may lag on weekends/holidays.
Response includes a promotional _hint field that can be ignored.

Same underlying ECB/Frankfurter source as the separate 'Greeneris FX Latest Rates' service, but a different provider, call shape (from/to pair vs base/symbols) and output (adds inverse_rates) - kept as its own service, not a backend of it.
usage.guide: Fetch real-time ECB reference exchange rates in one paid call. Issue a plain GET to https://api.x402node.dev/finance/forex?from=<BASE>&to=<TARGET(S)> (e.g. from=USD&to=EUR, or batch from=USD&to=EUR,GBP,JPY,CNY) with no body, and pay the fixed x402 quote (~$0.008 USDC on Base or Solana, no API key). On the 200, read the flat JSON: `rates` maps each target code to the rate (1 base in that target), `inverse_rates` maps each target to its inverse (1 target in base), `date` is the ECB reference date, and `source` names the upstream (ECB via Frankfurter). Batch multiple targets with commas at the same price. Synchronous - no polling. Note: ECB reference rates update once per working day (~16:00 CET), not intraday.

entries.name: X402node Forex Convert
entries.description: Convert an amount between two fiat currencies at the live FX rate (e.g. CNY->USD, USD->CNY, USD->GBP) via a single templated x402 endpoint, paid per call in USDC on Base or Solana — no API key.

inputSchema.amount: string (query param, e.g. ?amount=100 — the quantity of the FROM currency to convert)

usage.callShape: SYNC: GET https://api.x402node.dev/forex/convert/{from}/{to}/{from}-{to} with the currency pair substituted into the path (e.g. cny/usd/cny-usd) and the quantity of the FROM currency as ?amount=<n> query param -> JSON conversion result inline in the 200. Pay per call over x402 (Base USDC or Solana USDC). This is a TEMPLATED path-param service: the {from}/{to} pair is an input (cny/usd, usd/cny, usd/gbp, ...).
usage.outputShape: JSON live conversion for the requested pair. Verified call GET /forex/convert/cny/usd/cny-usd?amount=100 -> {"amount":100,"from":"CNY","to":"USD","result":14.82,"rate":0.1482,"pair":"CNY/USD","source":"Yahoo Finance (live)","as_of":"2026-07-31T01:58:22.000Z","note":"100 CNY = 14.82 USD."}
quirks: PATH-PARAM TEMPLATED: /forex/convert/{from}/{to}/{from}-{to} — the pair appears twice in the URL (both the /{from}/{to} segments and a trailing /{from}-{to} slug). One service; the pair is an input, not one entry per pair. Sibling pairs seen in this sweep: cny/usd, usd/cny, usd/gbp (openapi lists many more, e.g. aud/jpy, aud/usd).

The amount to convert is a QUERY param (?amount=100), not a JSON body. It is the quantity of the FROM currency; omitting it (probed) still returns 402 but the documented default example is amount=100.
Distinct from /forex/rate/{from}/{to} which returns just the exchange rate; this returns the converted value plus the rate.
Live rate sourced from Yahoo Finance (per response 'source' field). Accepts payment on Base (eip155:8453) OR Solana — either network works.
Price is a fixed $0.004 (accepts amount '4000' at 6 USDC decimals); confirmed against the openapi x-payment-info fixed price and the live 402 header.
usage.guide: Convert between two fiat currencies at the live FX rate from X402node: GET https://api.x402node.dev/forex/convert/{from}/{to}/{from}-{to} (substitute the pair, e.g. cny/usd/cny-usd) with the quantity of the FROM currency as ?amount=<n> (documented example ?amount=100). Returns a JSON conversion result (converted value + rate + source + timestamp) inline in the 200; pay per call ($0.004) in USDC on Base or Solana over x402, no API key. This is ONE templated service keyed on the {from}/{to} pair.

entries.name: x402node Forex Rate
entries.description: Live foreign-exchange spot rate for a major currency pair (e.g. GBP/EUR, USD/JPY) via a templated path, sourced from Yahoo Finance.

from.description: Base currency code (lowercase), e.g. gbp, usd, eur, jpy

to.description: Quote currency code (lowercase), e.g. eur, gbp, usd, jpy

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/forex/rate/{from}/{to}/{from}-{to} — the currency pair is carried in the PATH (both the two /from/to segments AND the combined from-to segment). No request body, no required query params. run.ts substitutes {from} and {to} in all three positions. x402 USDC on Base or Solana, no API key.
usage.outputShape: pair (e.g. 'GBP/EUR'), base, quote, rate (number), source ('Yahoo Finance (live)'), as_of (ISO 8601), note (human one-liner). Verified: {pair:'GBP/EUR', base:'GBP', quote:'EUR', rate:1.1681, source:'Yahoo Finance (live)', as_of:'2026-07-31T02:05:23.000Z', note:'1 GBP = 1.1681 EUR.'}
quirks: Templated service: the pair is a PATH parameter, not a query param or body. The path repeats the codes as /forex/rate/{from}/{to}/{from}-{to} (e.g. /forex/rate/gbp/eur/gbp-eur); run.ts fills all three {from}/{to} occurrences from a single {from,to} input.

Supported pairs (32, lowercase from/to): aud/jpy, aud/usd, cad/usd, chf/usd, cny/hkd, cny/usd, eur/gbp, eur/jpy, eur/usd, gbp/eur, gbp/jpy, gbp/usd, hkd/cny, hkd/usd, jpy/aud, jpy/eur, jpy/gbp, jpy/usd, krw/usd, nzd/usd, sgd/usd, usd/aud, usd/cad, usd/chf, usd/cny, usd/eur, usd/gbp, usd/hkd, usd/jpy, usd/krw, usd/nzd, usd/sgd.

A universal query-param sibling exists at GET https://api.x402node.dev/forex/rate?base=USD&quote=CNY (same $0.004) for ANY pair incl. those not in the per-pair list, and supports an optional amount= for conversion; the per-pair templated form indexed here is the documented zero-param variant.
For amount conversion of a fixed pair use the sibling /forex/convert/{from}/{to}/{from}-{to}?amount=100 (separate operation).
Accepts payment on Base OR Solana USDC — either network works.
Fixed price $0.004 (4000 atomic USDC units), sourced from Yahoo Finance (live).
Synchronous — result inline in the 200, no polling.
usage.guide: Fetch a live FX spot rate for a major currency pair. Call GET https://api.x402node.dev/forex/rate/{from}/{to}/{from}-{to} with the pair in the path (lowercase codes, e.g. gbp/eur -> /forex/rate/gbp/eur/gbp-eur). No body, no required query params. The wallet pays $0.004 USDC automatically via the x402 402 flow (Base or Solana, no API key). Read the number from body.rate (with body.pair, body.base, body.quote, body.source, body.as_of). Supported pairs: aud/jpy, aud/usd, cad/usd, chf/usd, cny/hkd, cny/usd, eur/gbp, eur/jpy, eur/usd, gbp/eur, gbp/jpy, gbp/usd, hkd/cny, hkd/usd, jpy/aud, jpy/eur, jpy/gbp, jpy/usd, krw/usd, nzd/usd, sgd/usd, usd/aud, usd/cad, usd/chf, usd/cny, usd/eur, usd/gbp, usd/hkd, usd/jpy, usd/krw, usd/nzd, usd/sgd. For any other pair, or to convert an amount, use the universal sibling /forex/rate?base=X&quote=Y&amount=N. Synchronous — no polling.

entries.name: OpenWebNinja Stock Quote (Yahoo Finance)
entries.description: Get a real-time stock/ETF/index quote sourced from Yahoo Finance (price, day and 52-week ranges, volume, exchange) for one or more ticker symbols, via the OpenWeb Ninja x402 gateway.

symbol.description: Stock symbol / ticker. Up to 100 symbols are supported in a single request (comma-separated). Examples: 'AAPL' or 'MSFT,AMZN'. Note: every 10 symbols is billed as a single request (e.g. 78 symbols = 8 requests).

data.description: Quote object for a single symbol (schema documents an array of these for multi-symbol requests). Fields include symbol, name, exchange, type, price, day_low, day_high, year_low, year_high, currency, volume, exchange_timezone, exchange_timezone_short, exchange_timezone_utc_offset_sec, full_exchange_name; docs also list change, change_percent, previous_close, market_state, tradeable, crypto_tradeable.

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.openwebninja.com/realtime-finance-data/stock-quote-yahoo-finance?symbol=<ticker> — pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base, Polygon or Arbitrum, no API key). The quote is returned inline in the 200 JSON under body.data; no polling.
usage.outputShape: body.status ('OK'); body.request_id; body.data — for a single symbol an object with the quote fields (observed for AAPL: symbol, name 'Apple Inc.', exchange 'NMS', type 'EQUITY', price 313.305, day_low, day_high, year_low, year_high, currency 'USD', volume, exchange_timezone, exchange_timezone_short 'EDT', exchange_timezone_utc_offset_sec, full_exchange_name 'NasdaqGS', exchange_data_max_delay_sec). quirks: symbol is the ONLY required query param; pass it URL-encoded in the query string (this is GET, no body).
Multiple symbols: comma-separate them in symbol (e.g. symbol=MSFT,AMZN), up to 100 per request.
Billing is per batch of 10 symbols: e.g. 78 symbols is charged as 8 requests (~$0.003 each). A single symbol is one request ($0.003).
For a single symbol, body.data is returned as an object, not an array — the provider schema documents an array for multi-symbol requests, so handle both shapes.
Data source is Yahoo Finance; prices may be quote-time snapshots and can be delayed for some exchanges (exchange_data_max_delay_sec was 0 for AAPL/NasdaqGS).
method enum in the schema is GET/HEAD/DELETE, but only GET returns quote data.
usage.guide: Get a real-time stock/ETF/index quote from Yahoo Finance via the OpenWeb Ninja x402 gateway. GET https://x402.openwebninja.com/realtime-finance-data/stock-quote-yahoo-finance with one query param: ?symbol=<ticker> (required, URL-encoded). entries.name: Agentstools Agri Production
entries.description: Returns US crop production, yield, acreage or grain-stocks series for a commodity (corn, soybeans, wheat, cotton) from USDA NASS QuickStats, with an optional state and as-of year, as a normalized cited series plus the year-over-year change and a multi-year history.

state.description: Optional 2-letter US state code; omit for national totals.

agg_level.description: Aggregation level, e.g. STATE or NATIONAL.

short_desc.description: USDA short description of the series.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/agri/production?commodity=<corn|soybeans|wheat|cotton>&metric=<production|yield|acreage|stocks>[&state=<2-letter>][&year=<2000-2100>] — all inputs are query params, no request body; every param is optional (defaults commodity=corn, metric=production, national, latest year). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: commodity, metric, region (state code or 'US'), agg_level (STATE|NATIONAL), unit (e.g. 'BU / ACRE'), frequency (e.g. annual), source ('USDA NASS QuickStats'), attribution, short_desc (USDA series label), as_of (year), latest{period, value, unit}, yoy_change{previous_period, previous_value, change, change_pct}, history[] (each: period, value, unit — descending years back to 2000).
quirks: All params are optional and passed on a GET query string (no body); defaults are commodity=corn, metric=production, national aggregation, latest available year.
commodity is limited to corn|soybeans|wheat|cotton; metric to production|yield|acreage|stocks — other values are rejected.
state is an optional 2-letter US code (e.g. IA) selecting state-level QuickStats; omit for national totals.
year (2000-2100) selects an as-of year; omitting it returns the latest available period.
Data is USDA NASS QuickStats (public government data) with attribution echoed in the response; history[] carries the full annual series, not just the latest value.
Verified live: commodity=corn, metric=yield, state=IA -> region 'IA', unit 'bu/acre', latest 2025 = 210 BU/ACRE, yoy_change -1 (-0.474%) vs 2024's 211, plus a 26-year history back to 2000.
usage.guide: Fetch US crop statistics from USDA NASS QuickStats with a single keyless x402 GET. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/agri/production?commodity=<corn|soybeans|wheat|cotton>&metric=<production|yield|acreage|stocks> with an optional state (2-letter US code, e.g. IA) and year (2000-2100). No request body; all params optional (defaults: corn, production, national, latest). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base. Synchronous — the 200 body carries the normalized latest{period,value,unit}, yoy_change{previous_period,previous_value,change,change_pct}, a multi-year history[], plus unit/source/attribution and the USDA short_desc. entries.name: Agentstools DeFi Math
entries.description: DeFi math helper that evaluates one of seven formulas per call — APR↔APY conversion for a compounding frequency, funding-rate annualization, impermanent loss, liquidation price, leverage/margin, and LP-vs-hold value — as pure local computation over your query-param inputs, not financial advice.

op.description: Which DeFi formula to evaluate. REQUIRED.

apr.description: APR as a decimal for op=apr_to_apy.

apy.description: APY as a decimal for op=apy_to_apr.

n.description: Compounding periods per year for the rate conversions.

periods_per_year.description: Funding periods per year for op=funding_annualized, default 1095.

price_ratio.description: Price ratio k for op=impermanent_loss and op=lp_value.

maintenance_margin.description: Maintenance margin as a decimal for op=liquidation_price, default 0.005.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/quant/defi?op=<FORMULA>&<inputs> — all inputs are query params, no request body. op is the only always-required param and selects the formula; each op reads a different subset of the other params (e.g. op=apr_to_apy needs apr and n; op=impermanent_loss needs price_ratio; op=liquidation_price needs entry_price, leverage, side; op=leverage needs notional and equity). x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.002. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON whose fields depend on op. Always echoes op and returns disclaimer:"computation only, not financial advice". For op=apr_to_apy it echoes apr and n and returns apy (decimal). Other ops return their computed field(s): apy_to_apr -> apr; funding_annualized -> annualized rate; impermanent_loss -> the IL fraction (IL = 2*sqrt(k)/(1+k) - 1); liquidation_price -> the long/short liquidation level; leverage -> leverage and margin; lp_value -> LP position value vs holding.
quirks: op is the ONLY always-required query param and picks the formula; each formula reads a different subset of the remaining params — supplying the wrong ones for an op yields a 4xx.
op enum: apr_to_apy | apy_to_apr | funding_annualized | impermanent_loss | liquidation_price | leverage | lp_value.
All inputs are query params on a GET — no request body.
The x402 402 challenge carries an EMPTY JSON body ({}); the payment requirements (accepts, Base USDC $0.002) live in the base64 `payment-required` response header, not the body.
impermanent_loss uses IL = 2*sqrt(k)/(1+k) - 1 for price ratio k (k=2 -> -5.7191%); funding_annualized defaults periods_per_year=1095; liquidation_price defaults maintenance_margin=0.005.
Pure local computation, a reference calculator — every response includes disclaimer "computation only, not financial advice".
Verified live: op=apr_to_apy, apr=0.1, n=12 -> apy 0.10471306744129683 (matches the openapi example 0.104713).
usage.guide: Evaluate a DeFi math formula. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/quant/defi?op=<FORMULA> (op required) with the params that formula needs, all as query params (no body): apr_to_apy -> apr + n; apy_to_apr -> apy + n; funding_annualized -> rate + periods_per_year (default 1095); impermanent_loss -> price_ratio (k); liquidation_price -> entry_price + leverage + side (long|short) + maintenance_margin (default 0.005); leverage -> notional + equity; lp_value -> price_ratio + optional initial_value. Pays $0.002 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns the computed value(s) inline in the 200 with a "computation only, not financial advice" disclaimer. Verified live: op=apr_to_apy&apr=0.1&n=12 -> apy 0.10471306744129683.

entries.name: Agentstools Monte-Carlo Option Simulation
entries.description: Monte-Carlo geometric-Brownian-motion simulation of an asset's terminal price (mean, std, percentiles) and, when a strike is supplied, the discounted European call/put price with standard error and probability of finishing in the money.

inputSchema.S: number (required) — spot price of the underlying (>0)
inputSchema.r: number (required) — drift / risk-free rate as a decimal
inputSchema.K: number (optional) — strike; include to also price a European payoff
inputSchema.q: number (optional) — continuous dividend yield as a decimal, default 0
inputSchema.steps: integer (optional) — time steps per path, default 1

K.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

S.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

T.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

paths.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

r.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

seed.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

sigma.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

steps.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

type.description: Input/filter query param (name from the provider's own example; added during baked-query remediation so it stays discoverable).

outputSchema.terminal: {mean, std, p05, p50, p95, min, max}
outputSchema.option: {type, strike, price, standard_error, prob_itm} (present only when K supplied)

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/quant/montecarlo?S=<SPOT>&T=<YEARS>&r=<RATE>&sigma=<VOL>&K=<STRIKE>&type=call&paths=20000&steps=1&seed=42 — all inputs are query params, no body. Required: S, T, r, sigma. Add K to also price a European option. x402 v2 exact on Base USDC, $0.005, synchronous (result inline in the 200).
usage.outputShape: {paths, steps, terminal:{mean, std, p05, p50, p95, min, max}, option:{type, strike, price, standard_error, prob_itm}, disclaimer}. Verified live: for S=K=100,T=1,r=0.05,sigma=0.2,paths=20000,seed=42 -> terminal.mean 105.04, option.price 10.40, prob_itm 0.559 (converges to the Black-Scholes call value).
quirks: Pure local computation over your inputs — not market data and 'not financial advice' (returns a disclaimer).
Compute is hard-capped at paths x steps = 200000 on the host; larger requests are bounded.
The 'option' block only appears when a strike K is supplied; without K you get terminal-price stats only.
Pass a seed for reproducible runs; more paths lowers the reported standard_error.
usage.guide: Price a European option or study an asset's terminal-price distribution by Monte-Carlo GBM. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/quant/montecarlo with query params S (spot), T (years), r (rate), sigma (vol) required; add K (strike) plus optional type (call/put), q (dividend yield), paths, steps, seed to also get the discounted option price, its standard error, and probability of finishing in the money. Pay per call via x402 USDC on Base ($0.005), no API key or account. Result is returned inline in the 200 — no polling.

entries.name: Agentstools Portfolio Risk Metrics

year.description: Calendar year; defaults to a recent year.
