available.description: true when the route computed a result; false (with reason) when the upstream Census key is not configured or unreachable.

count.description: Number of monthly data rows found (0 when no Census rows match).

signals.description: null when count is 0; otherwise {latest_month, latest_value, trend_pct_first_to_last, supplier_concentration_hhi (Herfindahl-Hirschman index), top_partners[]{cty_code, name, value}}.

note.description: Present when count is 0, e.g. 'No Census rows for that commodity/year/partner.'

attribution.description: e.g. 'Source: U.S. Census Bureau' — must be shown.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/trade/flow?hs6=<HS_OR_HTS>[&direction=imports|exports][&partner=<census_country_code>][&year=<int>] — all inputs are query params, no request body. Only `hs6` is required (direction defaults to imports, year defaults to recent). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.015 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.

Degrades cleanly: if the upstream free Census API key is not configured or unreachable it returns available:false with a reason instead of erroring; when available:true and rows exist, signals carries the trend, top_partners and Herfindahl-Hirschman supplier-concentration index (a supply-chain-risk score).
Public-domain US Census Bureau data; the value is the computed trend + concentration, not a raw resell. Not investment or trade advice; attribution must be shown.

GET https://api.agentstools.dev/trade/flow?hs6=<HS_OR_HTS_CODE> (required) plus optional direction (imports|exports, default imports), partner (Census partner-country code), and year (default recent). entries.name: Agentstools Trade HTS

keyword.description: Product-description keyword to search the HTS (e.g. 'laptop'). Provide this OR hts.

hts.description: An HTS or HS code, 4 to 10 digits, to expand into its subheading and statistical lines. Provide this OR keyword.

limit.description: Max lines to return, default 20.

query.description: Echo of the parsed inputs: { keyword, hts, limit }.

units.description: Units of quantity, e.g. ['No.'] (may be empty).

special.description: Special preferential duty rate with program symbols (may be empty).

footnotes.description: Chapter 99 footnotes flagging additional Section 301/232 duties.

sources.description: { errors, partial } provenance metadata; partial=true when upstream USITC was briefly unavailable.

Provide keyword OR hts. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.005 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.

quirks: All input is query params on a GET (no request body). Pass keyword (product-description search) OR hts (a 4-10 digit HTS/HS code to expand into its lines); limit is optional (1-60, default 20).
Data is the authoritative public-domain USITC Harmonized Tariff Schedule; output is reference information, NOT customs or legal advice (see attribution).

Each result line carries all three duty-rate columns — general (MFN), special (preferential, with program symbols), other (column-2) — plus any Chapter 99 footnotes flagging extra Section 301/232 duties.
The provider labels this the cheap supporting lookup that feeds the /trade/tariff duty-compute endpoint; /trade/flow (trade flows) is a separate op.
Returns partial results (sources.partial=true, sources.errors populated) when the upstream is briefly unavailable rather than erroring.

GET https://api.agentstools.dev/trade/hts?keyword=<product term> to search for candidate HTS numbers, OR ?hts=<4-10 digit HTS/HS code> to expand a code into its subheading and statistical lines; add &limit=<1-60> (default 20). Sourced from the public-domain USITC HTS; feeds the downstream /trade/tariff duty compute. Reference data only, not customs or legal advice; USITC attribution must be shown.

entries.name: Agentstools Tariff Estimate
entries.description: Estimate the effective US import duty for one HTS code from one origin country — the base MFN/FTA rate, the additional trade-war layers (Section 301, Section 232, IEEPA) with their Chapter 99 provisions, the combined effective ad-valorem rate, and an optional landed-cost estimate (USITC HTS-sourced).

hts.description: HTS or HS code, 4 to 10 digits, dots optional (e.g. 8471.30). REQUIRED.

origin.description: Country of origin as an ISO code, e.g. CN, MX, DE. REQUIRED.

customs_value.description: Optional entered customs value in USD; supplying it adds a landed-cost estimate.

query.description: Echo of the parsed inputs (hts, hts_normalized, origin, customs_value).

hts_line.description: Matched HTS line: hts (full 10-digit), description, units[], rate_line.

base_rate.description: Base column rate: raw (e.g. 'Free'), type, ad_valorem_percent, has_specific, column (e.g. general_mfn).

additional_duties.description: Trade-war layers (Section 301 / Section 232 / IEEPA) applicable to the origin+chapter.

landed_cost.description: Present when customs_value supplied: customs_value, estimated_ad_valorem_duty, estimated_landed_cost, note.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/trade/tariff?hts=<HTS_OR_HS_CODE>&origin=<ISO_COUNTRY>[&customs_value=<USD>] — all inputs are query params, no request body. `hts` and `origin` are required; `customs_value` is optional (adds a landed-cost estimate). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.03 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: query (echo: hts, hts_normalized, origin, customs_value), hts_line{hts (full 10-digit), description, units[], rate_line}, base_rate{raw, type, ad_valorem_percent, has_specific, column}, additional_duties[]{program, legal_basis, ad_valorem_percent, chapter99_provision, effective_date, source_url, matched_by}, effective_rate{base_ad_valorem_percent, additional_ad_valorem_percent, effective_ad_valorem_percent, has_unquantified_components}, chapter99_provisions_cited[], landed_cost{customs_value, estimated_ad_valorem_duty, estimated_landed_cost, note} (only when customs_value given), sources{errors, partial, hts_available}, disclaimer, attribution[]

The HTS code accepts dots or not (e.g. 8471.30 == 847130); the response echoes hts_normalized and resolves it to the full 10-digit hts_line.

additional_duties is where the real value is: it layers the current trade-war programs (Section 301, Section 232, IEEPA) with their Chapter 99 provisions and effective dates. These change frequently — the disclaimer explicitly says to re-verify the cited Chapter 99 provisions and exclusions before relying on it.
landed_cost is ad-valorem ONLY: per-unit/specific and compound duties are NOT included (require quantity) and it excludes MPF/HMF, freight and insurance.
Data is USITC Harmonized Tariff Schedule (public domain); attribution[] must be shown. Response also carries a 'disclaimer' string (not customs/legal advice) — it is not data.

Verified live: hts=8471.30 (portable ADP machines), origin=CN, customs_value=10000 -> base_rate Free (general_mfn 0%), additional IEEPA China (fentanyl) 20% (Chapter 99 9903.01.24, eff 2025-03-04), effective 20%, estimated duty $2000, landed cost $12000. (The 402 example body cited a Section 301 List 4A 7.5% layer instead — the applicable additional program is date/policy-dependent.)
Payment is gated before the call — a 402 pre-flight with the quote in the base64 'payment-required' header is normal x402 behavior.
usage.guide: Estimate the effective US import duty for one HTS code + origin with a single keyless x402 GET. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/trade/tariff?hts=<HTS/HS code, 4-10 digits, dots optional>&origin=<ISO country code, e.g. CN, MX, DE>, plus optional customs_value=<USD> to get a landed-cost estimate. Note the landed cost is ad-valorem only (no specific/compound duties, MPF/HMF, freight or insurance) and the trade-war layers change often — re-verify the cited Chapter 99 provisions. Attribution to the USITC HTS (public domain) must be shown.

Verified live for {metric:generation_mix, region:texas} (2026-08-06T05): total_generation_mwh 70186, renewable_share_pct 29.326, mix led by Natural Gas 48.118%, Wind 29.325%, Coal 15.425%, Nuclear 7.058%; storage[] battery 29 MWh. (metric=demand returns latest hourly demand + change vs prior hour; metric=retail_price returns avg monthly cents/kWh by state with MoM change + short history.)

region (14-value enum: us, california, carolinas, central, florida, mid_atlantic, midwest, new_england, new_york, northwest, southeast, southwest, tennessee, texas) applies to generation_mix and demand; retail_price is keyed by `state` (two-letter code or US) instead.
generation_mix percentages exclude battery/pumped storage (they can be negative when charging) — those appear in a separate storage[] block.
Data is US-government public domain from the EIA; the returned attribution string must be preserved on redisplay.
history (1..120) only affects metric=demand and retail_price.
Errors: unknown metric/region/state -> 400, empty result -> 404, upstream failure -> 502, missing upstream key -> 503.
usage.guide: Get authoritative US electricity data from the EIA in one keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/energy/electricity?metric=<generation_mix|demand|retail_price>&region=<grid region>&state=<two-letter code>&history=<N>. Use metric=generation_mix with region (e.g. texas, california, new_england) for the latest hourly fuel mix with per-fuel MWh, pct, and renewable_share_pct; metric=demand with region for latest hourly demand + change vs prior hour; metric=retail_price with state for the average monthly retail price in cents/kWh with MoM change and optional history. entries.name: Agentstools Natural Gas
entries.description: Authoritative US natural gas data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA): the daily Henry Hub spot price ($/MMBtu) or weekly working gas in underground storage (Bcf, Lower 48 or one of five EIA regions), each returned with the latest value, the change vs the prior period (week-over-week for storage), and a short history array, sourced to the EIA.

metric.description: henry_hub = daily Henry Hub spot price; storage = weekly working gas in underground storage (default henry_hub).

region.description: Storage region — only applies when metric=storage (default lower_48).

history.description: Number of recent data points to include in the history array.

wow_change.description: Change vs the prior period (week-over-week for storage, prior trading day for henry_hub).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/energy/natural-gas with QUERY params (no body): metric in [henry_hub, storage] (default henry_hub), region in [lower_48, east, midwest, south_central, mountain, pacific] (default lower_48, only used when metric=storage), and history (integer 1-120, number of recent data points). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: metric, route, region (storage only), unit, frequency, as_of, provenance {series, series_description, area}, latest {period, value, units}, wow_change {previous_period, previous_value, change, change_pct}, history[] (each {period, value, units}), and attribution (string). Verified live for {metric:storage, region:east, history:6}: EIA series NW2_EPG0_SWO_R31_BCF (Weekly East Region Natural Gas Working Underground Storage, Bcf), latest period 2026-07-31 value 678 BCF, week-over-week change +24 (+3.67%) vs 654 on 2026-07-24.
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.
metric defaults to henry_hub (daily Henry Hub spot price, $/MMBtu); set metric=storage for weekly working-gas-in-storage (Bcf) — the number markets watch on the Thursday EIA storage report.
region only applies when metric=storage; valid regions are lower_48 (default), east, midwest, south_central, mountain, pacific.
history caps at 120 data points.
wow_change is week-over-week for storage and prior-trading-day for henry_hub, despite the field name.
Data is US-government public domain; the attribution string ('Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration') is returned and should be displayed.
Errors: unknown metric/region -> 400, empty result -> 404, upstream EIA failure -> 502, missing upstream key -> 503.
The provider returns the full x402 quote in the base64 `payment-required` HEADER with an empty JSON body — a client that only reads accepts from the body will fail to pay.
usage.guide: Fetch authoritative US natural gas data from the EIA with a single keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/energy/natural-gas with QUERY params: metric=henry_hub (daily Henry Hub spot price in $/MMBtu) or metric=storage (weekly working gas in underground storage, Bcf), region=lower_48|east|midwest|south_central|mountain|pacific (storage only, default lower_48), and history=N (1-120 recent points). Synchronous — the 200 body carries metric, unit, frequency, as_of, provenance (EIA series id + description), latest {period,value,units}, wow_change (change vs prior period), a history[] series, and attribution. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {metric:'storage', region:'east', history:6} -> East region working gas storage, latest 678 Bcf on 2026-07-31, +24 Bcf (+3.67%) week-over-week, from EIA series NW2_EPG0_SWO_R31_BCF.

entries.name: Agentstools Petroleum Prices
entries.description: Returns US petroleum market data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA): retail gasoline/diesel by PADD region (weekly), WTI/Brent crude spot (daily), and weekly crude/gasoline/distillate inventories — as a normalized latest value with change vs the prior period, a short history, and a region-vs-US spread.

metric.description: Which petroleum series to return (default gas_prices).

region.description: PADD region for retail gasoline/diesel (default us). Ignored for crude/inventory metrics.

history.description: Number of recent data points to include in history[].

spread.description: Difference vs the national average (regional retail metrics only).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/energy/petroleum?metric=<gas_prices|diesel_prices|crude_wti|crude_brent|crude_stocks|gasoline_stocks|distillate_stocks>[&region=<us|east_coast|midwest|gulf_coast|rocky_mountain|west_coast>][&history=<1-120>] — all inputs are query params, no request body; every param is optional (defaults metric=gas_prices, region=us). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: metric, route, region, unit (e.g. '$/gal'), frequency (weekly|daily), attribution, provenance{series (EIA id), series_description, area (e.g. 'PADD 5')}, as_of, latest{period, value, units}, change{previous_period, previous_value, change, change_pct}, history[] (each: period, value, units), regional_spread{vs, baseline_value, spread} (regional retail metrics only).
quirks: All params are optional and passed on a GET query string (no body); defaults are metric=gas_prices and region=us.

metric enum: gas_prices, diesel_prices (weekly retail by PADD region), crude_wti, crude_brent (daily spot, $/barrel), crude_stocks, gasoline_stocks, distillate_stocks (weekly inventories, thousand barrels). Unknown metric/region → 400.
region (us|east_coast|midwest|gulf_coast|rocky_mountain|west_coast) is PADD region for retail gasoline/diesel only; it is ignored for crude spot and inventory metrics.
history (1-120) sets how many recent points history[] returns; empty result → 404, upstream failure → 502, missing upstream key → 503.
regional_spread is present for regional retail prices and gives the difference vs the national average; data is US-government public domain with the attribution string echoed in every response.

Verified live: metric=gas_prices, region=west_coast, history=8 → unit '$/gal', PADD 5, latest 2026-08-03 = $5.13/GAL, change +0.013 (+0.2541%) vs 2026-07-27, 8-week history, regional_spread +1.051 vs US baseline 4.079.
usage.guide: Fetch authoritative US petroleum market data from the EIA with a single keyless x402 GET. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/energy/petroleum?metric=<gas_prices|diesel_prices|crude_wti|crude_brent|crude_stocks|gasoline_stocks|distillate_stocks> with an optional region (PADD: us|east_coast|midwest|gulf_coast|rocky_mountain|west_coast, retail metrics only) and history (1-120 points). No request body; all params optional (defaults gas_prices, us). Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base. Synchronous — the 200 body carries the normalized latest{period,value,units}, change{previous_period,previous_value,change,change_pct}, a short history[], plus unit/frequency/attribution, EIA provenance{series,series_description,area}, and (for regional retail) a regional_spread vs the national average. Use for energy-cost modeling, fuel-price tracking, WTI/Brent crude spot, and US crude/gasoline/distillate inventory levels.

entries.name: Agentstools Renewable Share
entries.description: Returns the renewable share (solar, wind, hydro and geothermal) of the latest hourly US electricity generation for a grid region, from the EIA grid monitor, as a percentage plus renewable/total MWh and a per-fuel-type breakdown.

as_of.description: Hour of the latest reading, e.g. 2026-08-07T06.

fueltype.description: EIA fuel-type code, e.g. WAT, WND, GEO, SUN, SNB.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/energy/renewables?metric=share&region=<grid-region> — all inputs are query params, no request body; both params are optional (defaults metric=share, region=us). metric only accepts 'share'; region is one of us|california|carolinas|central|florida|mid_atlantic|midwest|new_england|new_york|northwest|southeast|southwest|tennessee|texas. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.008 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: metric, route, region, unit ('MWh'), frequency ('hourly'), attribution ('Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration'), as_of (latest hour, e.g. '2026-08-07T06'), renewable_share_pct (number), renewable_generation_mwh (number), total_generation_mwh (number), renewables[] (each: fueltype (EIA code e.g. WAT/WND/GEO/SUN/SNB), name, value_mwh, renewable (bool), pct).
quirks: Both params are optional and passed on a GET query string (no body); defaults are metric=share, region=us.

metric is limited to the single value 'share'; region must be one of the 14 EIA grid regions (us, california, carolinas, central, florida, mid_atlantic, midwest, new_england, new_york, northwest, southeast, southwest, tennessee, texas).
Data is the latest single hourly reading (frequency 'hourly') from the EIA grid monitor — not a history series; renewable_share_pct = renewable_generation_mwh / total_generation_mwh.

A per-fuel-type breakdown is returned in renewables[] (hydro/wind/geothermal/solar and solar+battery); individual value_mwh/pct can be negative for a fuel type (e.g. solar net of storage charging at night).
The 402 challenge is carried in the 'payment-required' response header (x402 v2 base64), and the unpaid 402 body is an empty {} — accepts must be read from the header.

Verified live: metric=share, region=california -> as_of 2026-08-07T06, renewable_share_pct 32.46, renewable_generation_mwh 12056 of total_generation_mwh 37141, breakdown Hydro 16.2% / Wind 12.8% / Geothermal 3.1% / Solar+battery 0.4% / Solar -0.1%.
usage.guide: Get the renewable share of US electricity generation for a grid region with a single keyless x402 GET. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/energy/renewables?metric=share&region=<region> where region is one of us|california|carolinas|central|florida|mid_atlantic|midwest|new_england|new_york|northwest|southeast|southwest|tennessee|texas (default us) and metric is always 'share'. No request body. Pays $0.008 USDC via x402 on Base. Synchronous — the 200 body carries renewable_share_pct plus renewable_generation_mwh / total_generation_mwh and a per-fuel-type renewables[] breakdown (hydro, wind, geothermal, solar, solar+battery), sourced from the EIA grid monitor for the latest hourly reading. Use for clean-energy/grid-mix monitoring, ESG dashboards, or carbon-aware scheduling; use the sibling /energy/electricity, /energy/natural-gas and /energy/petroleum endpoints for other EIA feeds.

entries.name: Agentstools Federal Agency Procurement Profile
entries.description: Profiles a US federal agency's procurement in one call from USASpending.gov — reported obligations, outlays and budget authority for its active fiscal year plus the top vendors it buys from, top NAICS industries and top product/service codes (PSC), scoped by award-type group and fiscal year.

year.description: Federal fiscal year; defaults to the agency's active fiscal year.

query.description: Echo of parsed inputs {agency, award_type, time_period{start_date, end_date}}.

agency.description: {name, toptier_code, abbreviation, active_fiscal_year, obligated_amount, outlay_amount, budget_authority_amount, percent_of_total_budget_authority}.

top_vendors.description: Ranked vendors {name, code, amount, uei, recipient_id}.

sources.description: {errors, partial} — partial:true when a block was briefly unavailable.

attribution.description: Must be shown — 'Data from USAspending.gov (U.S. Treasury, CC0 public domain)'.

Provide agency name OR toptier code. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.008 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.

usage.guide: Profile a US federal agency's procurement with a single keyless x402 GET. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/govcon/agency?agency=<AGENCY_NAME> (or ?toptier_code=<CODE>), optionally &award_type=(contracts|direct_payments|grants|idvs|loans|other) and &year=<fiscal_year>. Synchronous — the 200 body carries the agency's reported obligations/outlays/budget authority for its active fiscal year plus top_vendors, top_naics and top_psc rankings (each with amounts), a query echo, sources{partial} and USASpending.gov attribution. A missing agency returns HTTP 400. Use it for govcon competitive-intelligence and market-sizing: who sells what to which agency.

award_type.description: Friendly award-type group; the route builds the upstream USASpending filter for you.

recipient.description: Recipient / contractor name to match, e.g. 'Lockheed Martin'.

agency.description: Awarding agency name to filter by.

summary.description: Computed over the returned page: {count, total_amount, top_recipients[]{name,total}, top_agencies[]{name,total}, note}.

Verified live for {award_type:contracts, recipient:'Lockheed Martin', year:2024, limit:10}: count 10, has_next true, top award DEAC0494AL85000 (LOCKHEED MARTIN CORP, Dept of Energy, $48,063,737,196.35), summary.total_amount 241583433201.79 over the page, attribution 'Data from USAspending.gov (U.S. Treasury, CC0 public domain)'.

Partial answers are returned if a source block is briefly unavailable (sources.partial=true / sources.errors populated), never a 500.
Data is US public domain (CC0); include the attribution[] (USAspending.gov, U.S. Treasury) when redistributing. Not legal, investment or procurement advice.

Sibling ops on this host are different operations, not aliases: /govcon/award (one award detail by generated_internal_id), /govcon/agency (federal agency procurement profile), /govcon/awards (award search).
usage.guide: One-call federal footprint for a single US contractor over x402 (keyless). GET https://api.agentstools.dev/govcon/recipient?recipient=<name> (or ?uei=<UEI>)[&award_type=contracts|grants|idvs|loans|direct_payments|other][&year=<fiscal_year>]. Fuses several USAspending.gov queries into one object: total federal dollars, the matched recipient entities with UEIs (a name can span several records, which this reconciles), top awarding agencies, top NAICS industries won under, a per-fiscal-year spend trend, and recent awards each with a generated_internal_id you can pass to /govcon/award for full detail. Synchronous — the 200 body carries the whole profile. A missing recipient returns 400; a briefly-unavailable source yields a partial answer (sources.partial=true), never a 500. Data is USAspending.gov (CC0) — attribute it. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: ?recipient=Lockheed Martin -> uei G4KDGE4JFFK7, total_federal_amount ~$247.6B, top agency Department of Defense, top NAICS Aircraft Manufacturing.

entries.name: Agentstools 13F Filing
entries.description: One SEC Form 13F filing normalized to clean JSON: the cover page (manager, period, report type) plus every consolidated position with issuer, CUSIP, resolved ticker, share count, value in US dollars, percent of portfolio and voting authority, with a portfolio total, concentration block and crypto-ETF exposure slice.

accession.description: SEC accession number (requires cik). Direct pull of one exact filing.

cik.description: SEC EDGAR filer CIK, any zero-padding accepted.

name.description: Manager name (best-effort resolve; supply cik if not found).

quarter.description: Quarter period-end date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD (default latest).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/holdings/filing with QUERY params (no body): either accession + cik (direct pull of one exact filing) OR cik (or best-effort name) with optional quarter (ISO YYYY-MM-DD, default latest). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: found (bool), manager {name, cik}, quarter (period-end date), portfolioValueUsd, positions (count), concentration {top10Pct, hhi, positions}, cryptoEtfExposure {holds_crypto_etf, totalValueUsd, pctOfPortfolio, byAsset, holdings[]}, holdings[] each {issuer, cusip, class, putCall, valueUsd, shares, sshPrnamtType, investmentDiscretion, voting {sole, shared, none}, ticker, match, match_score, pctOfPortfolio}, stale_days, filing {accession, form, filedDate, periodOfReport, isAmendment, reportType, index_url, info_table_url}, attribution, disclaimer. Verified live for {accession:'0001193125-26-226661', cik:'1067983'} -> Berkshire Hathaway Inc 2026-03-31 13F-HR, portfolioValueUsd 263095703570, 29 positions (top: AAPL 21.99%, AXP 17.43%, KO 11.56%), cited to accession/period/EDGAR URL.
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.
Two ways to select a filing: accession REQUIRES cik alongside it (direct exact pull); otherwise pass cik (or best-effort name) with an optional quarter (default = latest filing).
cik accepts any zero-padding (1067983 or 0001067983 both work).
This is the cheap granular per-filing route ($0.01); the sibling Agentstools 13F Holdings by Security (/holdings/security) pivots by held security to find who holds a ticker.
CUSIP->ticker is best-effort: each holding carries match (exact|fuzzy|none) and, when fuzzy, match_score; ticker can be null when unresolved.
Form 13F reports LONG 13(f) securities only and is lagged up to 45 days after quarter-end (stale_days is reported); informational, not investment advice.
Attribution is returned (SEC EDGAR / Form 13F, US public domain) and should be displayed.
usage.guide: Pull one SEC Form 13F filing as clean JSON with a single keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/holdings/filing with QUERY params: give accession together with its filer cik for a direct exact pull, OR give cik (or a best-effort name) with an optional quarter=YYYY-MM-DD (default latest) to let the route pick the filing. Synchronous — the 200 body carries the cover page (manager {name,cik}, quarter, filing {accession, form, periodOfReport, reportType, isAmendment, EDGAR index_url + info_table_url}) plus the full information table as holdings[] (one per security: issuer, cusip, class, resolved ticker + match quality, shares, valueUsd, pctOfPortfolio, sshPrnamtType, investmentDiscretion, and the sole/shared/none voting split), together with portfolioValueUsd, a concentration block (top10Pct, hhi), the crypto-ETF exposure slice, stale_days and attribution. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {accession:'0001193125-26-226661', cik:'1067983'} -> Berkshire Hathaway Q1 2026 13F-HR, $263B portfolio, 29 positions led by AAPL/AXP/KO.

entries.name: Agentstools Regulatory Footprint
entries.description: Finds US federal regulatory and enforcement documents naming a business entity in the Federal Register — rules, proposed rules, notices and presidential documents normalized to title, type, issuing agency, date, abstract and link, newest first, with a total match count.

name.description: Business entity name to search (the primary query, e.g. 'Apple Inc').

agency.description: Optional Federal Register agency slug filter, e.g. 'federal-trade-commission'.

cik.description: Optional SEC CIK id hint to disambiguate the entity.

qid.description: Optional Wikidata QID id hint to disambiguate the entity.

limit.description: Max documents to return, default 10.

inputSchema.description: All inputs are query params on a GET (no request body). No field is strictly required by the schema, but `name` is the useful input; the others are optional filters/hints.

query.description: Echo of the parsed inputs, e.g. {name, agency}.

count.description: Total number of Federal Register documents matched (can be large; the full match count, not the page size).

returned.description: Number of documents actually returned in this page (<= limit, default 10).

type.description: Document type, e.g. Rule, Proposed Rule, Notice, Presidential Document.

sources.description: {errors{}, partial (bool), rate_limited (bool), providers[] e.g. ['federal_register']} — response is marked partial rather than failing on an upstream problem.

attribution.description: e.g. 'Federal Register (federalregister.gov), U.S. National Archives / GPO' — must be shown.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/legal/regulatory?name=<entity>[&agency=<agency-slug>][&cik=<sec-cik>][&qid=<wikidata-qid>][&limit=1-25] — all inputs are query params, no request body. `name` is the primary query; agency/cik/qid are optional filters/hints; limit defaults to 10 (max 25). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON on the paid 200: { query{name, agency}, kind:'regulatory', count (total matches, can be thousands), returned (page size, <= limit), recent:[{title, type, agency, agencies[], date, abstract, html_url, document_number}] newest first, sources{errors{}, partial, rate_limited, providers:['federal_register']}, disclaimer, attribution:['Federal Register (federalregister.gov), U.S. National Archives / GPO'] }.
quirks: GET with all inputs as query params (no body); `name` is the primary query. Method is GET per the openapi/402 (the bazaar schema also lists HEAD/DELETE as allowed methods, but GET is the read verb).

`count` is the TOTAL Federal Register match count and can be very large (observed 2693 for name='Apple Inc'), while `returned` (<= `limit`, default 10, max 25) is the actual page size — do not treat count as the number of documents in the response.

The entity-name search is broad full-text over the Federal Register, so `recent[]` often includes general rulemaking/notices that merely mention the term rather than being about the entity (the Apple Inc query returned Medicare, NRC, FCC, ITC, DOJ-v-RealPage, SEC SRO notices, etc.).
Optional cik (SEC CIK) and qid (Wikidata QID) id hints can disambiguate the entity; agency (a Federal Register agency SLUG, e.g. 'federal-trade-commission') narrows to one agency.
Per-document `abstract` is frequently null (many notices carry no abstract); `date` is the publication date and `html_url` links to federalregister.gov.

Public-domain Federal Register data; the value is the normalization/entity-mention filtering, not a raw resale. Degrades cleanly: on an upstream problem the response is marked sources.partial/rate_limited rather than 500. Not legal advice, not a consumer report, not for FCRA-regulated eligibility decisions; attribution must be shown.

Same underlying source (Federal Register) as the existing 'x402stock Regulatory' entry, but a different provider AND a different query contract (entity-name mentions vs agency-slug/keyword) — kept as a separate service, not merged.
usage.guide: Get a US federal regulatory/enforcement footprint for a business entity with one keyless x402 GET. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/legal/regulatory?name=<entity> (primary input), optionally &agency=<Federal Register agency slug>, &cik=<SEC CIK>, &qid=<Wikidata QID> to disambiguate, and &limit=1-25 (default 10). No request body. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless. Synchronous — the 200 body carries query (input echo), count (total Federal Register matches, can be thousands), returned (page size), and recent[] documents (title, type, agency/agencies[], date, abstract, html_url, document_number) newest first, plus sources (with partial/rate_limited flags), a disclaimer and Federal Register attribution. Use it for due-diligence and compliance to surface the rules, proposed rules, notices and presidential documents that name an entity in the Federal Register. Note count is the total match count while returned/recent.length is the page size; the name search is broad full-text, so review results for relevance.

entries.name: Agentstools Realestate Compare
entries.description: Rank two or more US geographies (states, metro CBSA codes, county FIPS or ZIPs) against each other on one real-estate metric in a single call — price momentum YoY (FHFA HPI), gross rental yield, price-to-income ratio, median home value, median gross rent or median household income — returning a best-to-worst ranking plus signals (max, min, spread, mean) and public-source attribution.

geo.description: Two or more geographies (states, metro CBSA codes, county FIPS codes or ZIPs), comma-separated (at least two).

metric.description: The metric to rank on (default price_momentum_yoy).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/realestate/compare with query params ?geo=<g1,g2,...>[&metric=<key>]. `geo` is a comma-separated list of AT LEAST TWO US geographies (states, metro CBSA codes, county FIPS or ZIPs); `metric` is one of price_momentum_yoy (default), gross_rental_yield, price_to_income, median_home_value, median_gross_rent, median_household_income. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: metric, metric_label, ranking[] (each {geo, kind, label, geography, value, rank}, sorted best-to-worst), signals {count, metric_direction ('higher_is_better'|'lower_is_better'), max:{geo,value}, min:{geo,value}, spread, mean}, attribution[] (source strings), disclaimer. Verified live for {geo:'CA,TX,FL', metric:'price_momentum_yoy'}: ranking FL -0.495 (rank 1), CA -0.534 (2), TX -1.633 (3); signals {count:3, metric_direction:'higher_is_better', spread:1.138, mean:-0.8873}; attribution ["Source: U.S. Federal Housing Finance Agency, House Price Index (public domain)"].
quirks: `geo` MUST list at least two geographies (comma-separated); fewer than two returns HTTP 400.
Geographies can be mixed types: 2-letter states (CA), metro CBSA codes, county FIPS codes, or ZIPs; each ranking row echoes the resolved `kind` (state/metro/county/zip) and `label`.

Ranking direction depends on the metric: for price_to_income a LOWER value ranks higher (more affordable, signals.metric_direction 'lower_is_better'); for all other metrics a HIGHER value ranks higher.
An unknown metric returns 400; no data for the requested geographies returns 404.

Values are aggregate market-tier indicators fused from public US-government sources (e.g. FHFA House Price Index for price momentum); response always includes attribution[] and a disclaimer — this is not an appraisal, not a per-address valuation, and not investment advice. US-only.
Static price ($0.02), Base USDC only (no Solana option).
usage.guide: Compare several US geographies on one real-estate metric in a single keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/realestate/compare?geo=<g1,g2,...>[&metric=<key>]. `geo` is a comma-separated list of AT LEAST TWO US geographies — states (CA), metro CBSA codes, county FIPS codes, or ZIPs, freely mixed; `metric` is one of price_momentum_yoy (default, FHFA HPI YoY %), gross_rental_yield, price_to_income, median_home_value, median_gross_rent, median_household_income. Synchronous — the 200 body carries {metric, metric_label, ranking[] (best-to-worst, each {geo,kind,label,geography,value,rank}), signals{count,metric_direction,max,min,spread,mean}, attribution[], disclaimer}. Note ranking direction: for price_to_income lower is better, otherwise higher is better. Fewer than two geographies or an unknown metric returns 400; no data 404. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: ?geo=CA,TX,FL&metric=price_momentum_yoy -> FL ranks 1 (-0.495%), CA 2 (-0.534%), TX 3 (-1.633%), spread 1.138.

entries.name: Agentstools Real Estate Market
entries.description: A composite US real-estate market profile for one geography (state, metro CBSA, county, ZIP, or address): FHFA House Price Index level and momentum, Census ACS demographics/housing/income/tenure/vacancy, and computed derivatives (gross rental yield, price-to-income, rent-to-income, homeownership and vacancy rates), each value cited with its own source, code, geography, period and unit. Aggregate market tier, US only — not an appraisal or per-address valuation.

geo.description: A state (2-letter code or name), metro CBSA code, county FIPS, ZIP, or a street address.

type.description: How to read geo. In auto a 5-digit number is a ZIP; use cbsa or county to disambiguate.

range.description: Most recent N House Price Index observations of history.

geo.description: Resolved geography: input, kind (state/cbsa/county/zip/address), label, geography, state.

prices.description: FHFA House Price Index block: level, place_id, geography, flavor, frequency, momentum {available, latest_index, latest_period, yoy_pct, qoq_pct, cagr_5yr_pct, trend}, history[] {year, period, index}, source, source_code.

demographics_housing.description: Census ACS 5-Year block: geography, period, metrics {median_home_value, median_gross_rent, median_household_income, population, occupied_units, owner_occupied_units, renter_occupied_units, total_housing_units, total_occupancy_units, vacant_units}, each {value, source, source_code, geography, period, unit}.

rents.description: median_gross_rent (ACS) plus optional HUD Fair Market Rents by bedroom count when the provider has a HUD token configured.

national_context.description: Optional national housing context from the Federal Reserve; may be null.

derivatives.description: Computed metrics: gross_rental_yield_pct, price_to_income, rent_to_income, homeownership_rate_pct, vacancy_rate_pct, price_momentum_yoy_pct.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/realestate/market with QUERY params (no body): geo (required — a state 2-letter code or name, a metro CBSA code, a county FIPS, a ZIP, or a street address), type (optional — auto|state|county|cbsa|zip|address; how to read geo), range (optional integer 1-40 — most recent N House Price Index observations of history). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.03 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: geo {input, kind, label, geography, state}; prices {level, place_id, geography, flavor, frequency, momentum {available, latest_index, latest_period {year, period, frequency}, yoy_pct, qoq_pct, cagr_5yr_pct, trend}, history[] {year, period, index}, source, source_code}; demographics_housing {geography, period, metrics{median_home_value, median_gross_rent, median_household_income, population, occupied_units, owner_occupied_units, renter_occupied_units, total_housing_units, total_occupancy_units, vacant_units} each {value, source, source_code, geography, period, unit}}; rents {median_gross_rent, fair_market_rents_note}; national_context (object or null); derivatives {gross_rental_yield_pct, price_to_income, rent_to_income, homeownership_rate_pct, vacancy_rate_pct, price_momentum_yoy_pct}; attribution[]; disclaimer. Verified live for {geo:'CA'} -> HTTP 200: California state HPI latest_index 420.62 (2026 Q1, yoy -0.534%, cagr_5yr 4.442%, trend falling), ACS median_home_value $695,400, median_gross_rent $1,956/mo, median_household_income $96,334, derivatives gross_rental_yield_pct 3.375, price_to_income 7.219, homeownership_rate_pct 55.79, vacancy_rate_pct 7.55.
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.

geo accepts a state (2-letter code or name), a metro CBSA code, a county FIPS, a ZIP, or a street address; use type to disambiguate (auto reads a 5-digit number as a ZIP; pass type=cbsa or type=county to read a 5-digit number as a metro/county). Multi-word place names (e.g. 'New York') are valid — URL-encode the space.
Aggregate market-tier profile only — a state/metro/county/ZIP indicator, NOT an appraisal and NOT a per-address valuation. Coverage is United States only.

HUD Fair Market Rents are only included when the provider has a HUD token configured; the verified run returned rents.fair_market_rents_note 'HUD Fair Market Rents omitted (HUD_API_TOKEN not configured); ACS median gross rent shown.' — plan for FMR to be absent.
national_context may be null (the optional Federal Reserve national housing context was null in the verified run).
Every value carries its own provenance (source, source_code, geography, period, unit) and the response lists attribution[] for each source used (FHFA public domain, Census ACS).
Errors: blank or unknown geo -> 400, a geography with no data -> 404.
usage.guide: Fetch a composite US real-estate market profile for one geography with a single keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/realestate/market with QUERY params: geo (required — a state 2-letter code or name like 'CA' or 'California', a metro CBSA code like 31080, a county FIPS, a ZIP, or a street address), plus optional type=auto|state|county|cbsa|zip|address to disambiguate how geo is read (auto treats a 5-digit number as a ZIP; use type=cbsa or type=county to read one as a metro/county), and optional range=1..40 for the most recent N House Price Index observations of history. Synchronous — the 200 body fuses the FHFA House Price Index (level, yoy/qoq/5yr-CAGR momentum, trend, short history), Census ACS 5-Year demographics/housing/income/tenure/vacancy, an optional Federal Reserve national context, optional HUD Fair Market Rents (only when the provider has a HUD token), and computed derivatives (gross_rental_yield_pct, price_to_income, rent_to_income, homeownership_rate_pct, vacancy_rate_pct); every value is cited by source/code/geography/period/unit with an attribution[] list. This is an aggregate market-tier profile, not an appraisal or per-address valuation, US only. Pays $0.03 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {geo:'CA'} -> California HPI 420.62 (2026 Q1, trend falling), median home value $695,400, median gross rent $1,956/mo, gross rental yield 3.375%.

entries.name: Agentstools Congress Trades
entries.description: Normalized US House congressional stock trades from STOCK Act Periodic Transaction Reports (PTRs) — filter by ticker or member over an optional date window and get each disclosed buy/sell/exchange with amount range, ticker, asset, transaction and disclosure dates, disclosure lag, owner, and a link to the source filing PDF.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol to filter by, e.g. AAPL.

member.description: House member surname or full-name substring to filter by, e.g. Aderholt.

chamber.description: Chamber; defaults to house (senate is deferred/not yet covered).

startdt.description: Window start date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD (defaults to 90 days ago).

enddt.description: Window end date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD (defaults to today).

found.description: true when at least one matching trade was found; false with an empty trades[] when none match.

query.description: Echo of the parsed filters {ticker, member, chamber}.

filings_scanned.description: Number of PTR filings scanned to produce the result.

trades.description: Each disclosed trade: {member, chamber, state_district, ticker, asset_description, type (buy|sell|exchange), owner, amount_range, amount_low, amount_high, transaction_date, disclosure_date, disclosure_lag_days, filing{doc_id, ptr_url}}.

partial.description: true when the result may be incomplete (e.g. upstream coverage limits).

coverage_note.description: Optional note on coverage gaps; null when full.

attribution.description: 'US House Clerk Periodic Transaction Reports (US public domain)' — must be shown.

congress_notice.description: STOCK Act disclosure notice: amounts are disclosed as RANGES, not exact values.

disclaimer.description: Informational only, not investment advice; self-reported filings may be delayed, amended or incomplete.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/congress/trades?[member=<surname>][&ticker=<TICKER>][&chamber=house|senate][&startdt=YYYY-MM-DD][&enddt=YYYY-MM-DD] — all inputs are query params, no request body. usage.outputShape: {found (bool), query{ticker, member, chamber}, window{start, end}, trades_returned (int), filings_scanned (int), trades[]{member, chamber, state_district, ticker, asset_description, type (buy|sell|exchange), owner, amount_range, amount_low, amount_high, transaction_date, disclosure_date, disclosure_lag_days, filing{doc_id, ptr_url}}, partial (bool), coverage_note (nullable), attribution, congress_notice, disclaimer}
quirks: All inputs are query params on a GET (no body). No single param is strictly required — chamber defaults to house and the window defaults to the last 90 days — but you filter by `member` (surname/full-name substring) and/or `ticker`.

found can be false with trades_returned:0 and an empty trades[] when no PTRs match the filter/window — this is a valid empty result, not an error (verified live: member=Aderholt, 2026-01-01..2026-06-30 -> found:false, trades_returned:0, filings_scanned:0).
chamber:senate is deferred/not yet covered — house is the supported chamber.
Amounts are disclosed as RANGES per the STOCK Act (amount_range plus amount_low/amount_high), not exact values; each trade cites its source filing PDF (filing.ptr_url on disclosures-clerk.house.gov).
Public-domain US House Clerk PTR data; attribution must be shown. Informational only, NOT investment advice — filings are self-reported and may be delayed, amended or incomplete.

usage.guide: Look up US House congressional stock trades (STOCK Act Periodic Transaction Reports) with a single keyless x402 GET. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/congress/trades and filter by member (House member surname or full-name substring, e.g. Aderholt) and/or ticker (e.g. AAPL), with optional chamber (house, default; senate deferred), startdt and enddt (ISO YYYY-MM-DD; window defaults to the last 90 days). entries.name: Alphavantage Earnings Call Transcript
entries.description: Full quarterly earnings-call transcripts for a stock — pass a ticker and quarter and get the complete call transcript as structured segments (speaker, title, content) with per-segment sentiment. AlphaVantage data served over x402 via the Locus gateway.

quarter.description: Fiscal quarter in YYYYQN format, e.g. 2025Q1.

transcript.description: Ordered call segments: {speaker, title, content, sentiment}.

usage.callShape: POST https://alphavantage.x402.paywithlocus.com/alphavantage/earnings-call-transcript with JSON body {"symbol":"AAPL","quarter":"2025Q1"} (both required). Result is inline in the 200 body under `data` (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.008 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: 200 body {success, data:{symbol, quarter, transcript[]{speaker, title, content, sentiment}}, request{id, statusUrl}, payment{...}} — the transcript is inline under data; request.statusUrl exists but the result is already present (synchronous).
quirks: x402 on the paywithlocus DOMAIN but genuinely x402, NOT MPP: the host x402.paywithlocus.com is Locus's x402 gateway and the 402 says 'Retry with a valid x402 v2 exact PAYMENT-SIGNATURE for USDC on Base'. Paid-verified live 2026-08-08 ($0.008 on Base). curate.mjs's isMpp filter is scoped to exempt x402.paywithlocus.com so this survives.
Response wraps the payload: the transcript is at data.transcript[] (not top-level). A request.statusUrl is returned but the result is already inline — treat as synchronous, no poll needed.
Both symbol and quarter are REQUIRED (quarter in YYYYQN, e.g. 2025Q1). Priced $0.008 USDC/call via x402 on Base.
AlphaVantage data served through the Locus (paywithlocus) x402 gateway — backend provider is Locus, the data owner is AlphaVantage.
usage.guide: Get a full quarterly earnings-call transcript with one keyless x402 POST. POST https://alphavantage.x402.paywithlocus.com/alphavantage/earnings-call-transcript with JSON {symbol, quarter} (both required; quarter in YYYYQN, e.g. AAPL / 2025Q1). Pays $0.008 USDC via x402 on Base. Synchronous — the 200 body wraps the result under `data`: {symbol, quarter, transcript[]} where each segment is {speaker, title, content, sentiment}. Use it to pull and analyze what executives said on an earnings call (with per-segment sentiment). Genuine x402 (on the paywithlocus x402 gateway), not MPP.

entries.name: Agentstools FEC Contributions
entries.description: Searches FEC Schedule A itemized federal campaign contributions by contributor name, recipient committee id or candidate id and returns normalized receipts — contributor employer/occupation/city/state, amount, cycle and recipient committee — each cited to its FEC transaction id and filing image, plus a summary of totals and top recipients.

committee_id.description: FEC recipient committee id, e.g. C00401224.

limit.description: Max records to return, default 20.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/fec/contributions with QUERY params (no body): supply at least one of contributor_name / committee_id / candidate_id, and narrow with optional employer, two_year_transaction_period (even-year cycle), min_amount and limit (1-100, default 20). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: found (bool), query (echo of the applied filters), total_matched (int), returned (int), summary {total_amount, record_count, top_recipients[{committee_id, committee_name, candidate_name, total, count}]}, contributions[{contributor_name, employer, occupation, city, state, amount, date, recipient {committee_id, committee_name, candidate_id, candidate_name}, receipt_type, two_year_transaction_period, memo_text, citation {transaction_id, pdf_url}}], attribution[], disclaimer. Verified paid response: total_matched 559282, returned 20 for contributor_name='smith' min_amount=200; e.g. SMITH, THOMAS M (Weyerhaeuser, VP Tax) $384.60 to WEYERHAEUSER COMPANY PAC (C00007948), cited to transaction PR37898619821.
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.

At least one identifier filter (contributor_name, committee_id or candidate_id) should be supplied; broad name queries can match hundreds of thousands of records (total_matched 559282 for 'smith'), so use limit and min_amount to narrow.
Contribution `date` is often null; use two_year_transaction_period for the cycle and citation.transaction_id / citation.pdf_url to trace a record to its FEC filing image.

Data is FEC / OpenFEC (api.open.fec.gov), US public domain; response carries attribution[] and a disclaimer — informational due-diligence/compliance/research ONLY, NOT for soliciting contributions or commercial solicitation of donors (52 U.S.C. §30111(a)(4)).
402 body is empty ({}) — the x402 challenge (accepts + bazaar input/output schema) is carried in the base64 `payment-required` response header, not the body.
Bazaar input schema lists methods GET/HEAD/DELETE, but this is a read op — use GET.
usage.guide: Search FEC Schedule A federal campaign contributions with a single keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/fec/contributions with QUERY params: at least one of contributor_name / committee_id / candidate_id, optionally narrowed by employer, two_year_transaction_period (even-year cycle e.g. 2024), min_amount and limit (1-100, default 20). Synchronous — the 200 body carries found, total_matched, a summary {total_amount, top_recipients}, and contributions[] where each record has the contributor (name/employer/occupation/city/state), amount, cycle, recipient committee/candidate, and a citation (transaction_id + FEC filing pdf_url). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {contributor_name:'smith', limit:20, min_amount:200}. Use it for compliance / PEP-exposure / opposition-research due diligence; not a donor solicitation list.

entries.name: Agentstools 13F Changes
entries.description: Deterministic quarter-over-quarter diff of an institutional manager's SEC Form 13F portfolio, bucketing every position as new/added/reduced/sold-out/unchanged with per-position share and dollar deltas plus a net-flow summary, from two consecutive filings.

cik.description: SEC EDGAR filer CIK, any zero-padding accepted.

name.description: Manager name (best-effort resolve; supply cik if not found).

quarter.description: Quarter period-end date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD (default latest). Route also loads the immediately preceding quarter's filing.

changes.description: Positions bucketed by change type; keys new/added/reduced/sold_out/unchanged, each an array of position objects.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/holdings/changes with QUERY params (no body): cik (or best-effort name) with an optional quarter (ISO YYYY-MM-DD, default latest). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.05 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: found (bool), manager {name, cik}, quarter, prev_quarter, summary {new, added, reduced, sold_out, unchanged, added_value_usd, reduced_value_usd, net_flow_usd}, changes {new[], added[], reduced[], sold_out[], unchanged[]} where each position is {issuer, cusip, class, ticker, cryptoAsset, shares, prevShares, deltaShares, valueUsd, prevValueUsd, deltaValueUsd, pctSharesChange}, stale_days, filings {current, previous} each {accession, form, filedDate, periodOfReport, isAmendment, reportType, index_url, info_table_url}, attribution, disclaimer. Verified live for {cik:'1067983'} -> Berkshire Hathaway Inc, quarter 2026-03-31 vs prev 2025-12-31: 3 new (DAL, GOOG, MACYS), 4 added (incl. GOOGL +203.99%), 6 reduced, 16 sold out (VISA, MASTERCARD, UNH, DPZ...), 16 unchanged; net_flow_usd -3,870,863,278 (net selling). Both filings cited by accession/period/EDGAR URL.
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.
Selects the filing by cik (or best-effort name) plus optional quarter (default = latest); the route automatically loads the immediately preceding quarter and diffs the two by CUSIP.
cik accepts any zero-padding (1067983 or 0001067983 both work).
cryptoAsset tags spot-Bitcoin/Ether-ETF positions in each bucket so an agent can spot a fund initiating or trimming crypto-ETF exposure.
In sold_out positions the current shares/valueUsd are null (position fully exited); pctSharesChange is -100.
Form 13F reports LONG 13(f) securities only and is lagged up to 45 days after quarter-end (stale_days is reported); informational, not investment advice.
CUSIP->ticker is best-effort; ticker can be null when unresolved.
Attribution is returned (SEC EDGAR / Form 13F, US public domain) and should be displayed.
Distinct from the sibling Agentstools 13F Filing (/holdings/filing), which normalizes ONE filing rather than diffing two consecutive quarters.
usage.guide: Get the deterministic quarter-over-quarter diff of an institutional manager's Form 13F portfolio in one keyless x402 call, instead of downloading two filings and reconciling them by hand. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/holdings/changes with QUERY params: cik (or a best-effort name) plus an optional quarter=YYYY-MM-DD (default latest); the route loads that quarter's 13F-HR and the immediately preceding quarter's filing, consolidates each into positions, matches by CUSIP, and buckets every security as new/added/reduced/sold_out/unchanged. Synchronous — the 200 body carries a summary block (bucket counts, added_value_usd, reduced_value_usd, net_flow_usd = net buying/selling for the quarter), a changes object with per-position share and dollar deltas (shares, prevShares, deltaShares, valueUsd, prevValueUsd, deltaValueUsd, pctSharesChange, cryptoAsset tag), stale_days, and both filings cited by accession/period/EDGAR URL. Pays $0.05 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {cik:'1067983'} -> Berkshire Hathaway Q1 2026 vs Q4 2025, net_flow -$3.87B (net selling), 16 positions fully sold out incl. VISA/MASTERCARD/UNH.

entries.name: Agentstools 13F Manager Portfolio
entries.description: Normalized Form 13F portfolio for an institutional manager: give a CIK or name and get the consolidated latest-quarter positions (issuer, CUSIP, resolved ticker, shares, value in US dollars, percent of portfolio, voting authority) plus portfolio total, top positions, concentration metrics and spot Bitcoin/Ether ETF exposure, cited to the filing accession and period.

cik.description: SEC EDGAR filer CIK, any zero-padding accepted.

name.description: Manager name (best-effort resolve; supply cik if not found).

quarter.description: Quarter period-end date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD (default latest).

top.description: How many top positions to return (default 20, max 100).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/holdings/manager with QUERY params (no body): give cik (or best-effort name) to select the manager, with optional quarter (ISO YYYY-MM-DD, default latest) and top (how many positions, default 20 / max 100). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.03 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: found (bool), manager {name, cik}, quarter (period-end date), portfolioValueUsd, positions (count), reported_total_usd, concentration {top10Pct, hhi, positions}, cryptoEtfExposure {holds_crypto_etf, totalValueUsd, pctOfPortfolio, byAsset, holdings[]}, top[] each {issuer, cusip, class, putCall, valueUsd, shares, sshPrnamtType, investmentDiscretion, voting {sole, shared, none}, ticker, match, match_score, pctOfPortfolio}, stale_days, filing {accession, form, filedDate, periodOfReport, isAmendment, reportType, index_url, info_table_url}, attribution, disclaimer. Verified live for {cik:'1067983'} -> Berkshire Hathaway Inc 2026-03-31 13F-HR (accession 0001193125-26-226661), portfolioValueUsd 263095703570, 29 positions (top: AAPL 21.99%, AXP 17.43%, KO 11.56%), top10Pct 90.72, cited to accession/period/EDGAR URL.
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.
Select the manager by cik (any zero-padding, 1067983 or 0001067983 both work) or by best-effort name; supply cik if the name doesn't resolve.
Optional quarter=YYYY-MM-DD selects a specific period-end (default = latest filing); top controls how many positions are returned (default 20, max 100).

The positions array is named top (not holdings); this is the per-manager consolidated view. The sibling Agentstools 13F Filing (/holdings/filing) pulls one exact filing's full information table, and Agentstools 13F Holdings by Security (/holdings/security) pivots by held security.
CUSIP->ticker is best-effort: each position carries match (exact|fuzzy|none) and, when fuzzy, match_score; ticker can be null when unresolved.
Form 13F reports LONG 13(f) securities only and is lagged up to 45 days after quarter-end (stale_days is reported); informational, not investment advice.
Attribution is returned (SEC EDGAR / Form 13F, US public domain) and should be displayed.
usage.guide: Get an institutional manager's normalized Form 13F portfolio with a single keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/holdings/manager with QUERY params: pass cik (or a best-effort name) to select the manager, plus optional quarter=YYYY-MM-DD (default latest) and top=N (default 20, max 100). Synchronous — the 200 body carries manager {name,cik}, quarter, portfolioValueUsd (+ reported_total_usd), positions count, a concentration block (top10Pct, hhi), the crypto-ETF exposure slice, and the top[] positions (one per security: issuer, cusip, class, resolved ticker + match quality, shares, valueUsd, pctOfPortfolio, sshPrnamtType, investmentDiscretion, sole/shared/none voting split), together with stale_days, the source filing {accession, form, periodOfReport, EDGAR index_url + info_table_url}, attribution and disclaimer. Pays $0.03 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {cik:'1067983'} -> Berkshire Hathaway Q1 2026 13F-HR, $263B portfolio, 29 positions led by AAPL/AXP/KO.

entries.name: Agentstools Insider Signal
entries.description: Composite deterministic 0-100 insider + congressional signal for one ticker over a date window, fusing SEC Form-4 insider transactions and US House STOCK Act trades into a scored bullish/bearish direction with cited flags (net insider buying, cluster buy, unusual volume, congressional activity, disclosure lag).

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL. Provide either ticker or cik.

cik.description: SEC EDGAR issuer CIK, any zero-padding accepted. Alternative to ticker.

startdt.description: Window start date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD (default 90 days ago).

enddt.description: Window end date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD (default today).

components.description: Additive score contributions (base plus per-factor deltas) that sum toward signal_score.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/insider/signal with query params ?ticker=<SYMBOL>[&cik=<CIK>][&startdt=YYYY-MM-DD][&enddt=YYYY-MM-DD]. Identify the issuer by ticker OR cik; startdt/enddt bound the window (defaults: last 90 days). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.04 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: found, entity {name, cik, ticker}, window {start, end}, signal {signal_score (0-100), direction (bullish/bearish/neutral), window_days, flags {net_insider_buy {net_shares, net_usd, distinct_buyers, distinct_sellers}, cluster_buy {detected, distinct_buyers, threshold}, unusual_volume {detected, net_buy_usd, threshold_usd}, congress_activity {trades, buys, sells, net}, avg_disclosure_lag_days}, components {base + per-factor score deltas}}, sources {insider_filings, insider_transactions, congress_trades, insider_partial, congress_partial, congress_coverage_note}, attribution[], congress_notice, disclaimer. Verified live for {ticker:AAPL, startdt:2026-01-01, enddt:2026-06-30}: Apple Inc. (cik 0000320193), signal_score 18.4 (bearish), net_insider_buy -397,875 shares / -$111.7M across 5 distinct sellers, no cluster buy, 1 congressional sell; from 26 insider filings / 72 transactions and 1 congress trade.
quirks: Supply either `ticker` or `cik`; both/neither default behavior favors ticker resolution. All query params are technically optional (window defaults to the last 90 days) but a ticker or cik is needed for a meaningful result.
signal_score is a deterministic 0-100 composite: `components` breaks down the additive contributions (base 50 plus per-factor deltas for net_buy_usd, distinct buyers/sellers, cluster_buy, congress).

Congress coverage is a bounded scan — `sources.congress_coverage_note` reports the cap (e.g. 25 newest of 240 matching filings parsed); narrow the window or filter to increase coverage. `insider_partial`/`congress_partial` flag truncated results.
Congressional trade amounts are STOCK Act disclosure RANGES, not exact values (see `congress_notice`); data is self-reported public filings and may be delayed/amended (see `disclaimer`).
Every result is cited via `attribution[]` (SEC EDGAR Form 3/4/5 + US House Clerk PTRs, both US public domain).

Sibling ops on this host are distinct: /insider/trades returns the raw Form-4 transaction list and /congress/trades the raw STOCK Act trades, whereas this endpoint fuses both into a single scored signal.
usage.guide: Get a composite insider + congressional trading signal for one ticker in a single keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/insider/signal?ticker=<SYMBOL>&startdt=YYYY-MM-DD&enddt=YYYY-MM-DD (identify by ticker or cik; window defaults to the last 90 days). Synchronous — the 200 body carries a 0-100 signal_score with bullish/bearish direction and cited flags: net insider buying (shares/USD, distinct buyers vs sellers), cluster buy across distinct insiders, unusual volume, congressional activity (buys/sells/net), and average disclosure lag, plus a `components` breakdown and `sources`/`attribution` provenance. Data fuses SEC Form-4 filings and US House STOCK Act PTRs (both US public domain); congressional amounts are disclosed ranges and results are informational only, not investment advice. Congress coverage is bounded (see congress_coverage_note) — narrow the window for full coverage. Pays $0.04 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: ?ticker=AAPL&startdt=2026-01-01&enddt=2026-06-30 -> Apple signal_score 18.4 (bearish), -$111.7M net insider selling across 5 sellers.

entries.name: Agentstools Insider Trades
entries.description: Normalized corporate-insider transactions from SEC Form 3/4/5 filings for a ticker or issuer CIK over a date window: every director, officer and 10%-owner transaction with code, security, shares, price, value, acquired/disposed and disclosure lag, each cited to its accession and form4.xml URL.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL (supply ticker OR cik).

cik.description: SEC EDGAR issuer CIK, any zero-padding accepted (supply ticker OR cik).

startdt.description: Window start date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD (default 90 days ago).

enddt.description: Window end date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD (default today).

tx_codes.description: Optional filter of SEC Form-4 transaction codes to include.

filings.description: One entry per Form 3/4/5 filing in the window.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/insider/trades with QUERY params (no body): ticker (or issuer cik), plus optional startdt/enddt (ISO YYYY-MM-DD), optional person substring filter and tx_codes[] filter. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: found (bool), entity {name, cik, ticker}, window {start, end}, filings_returned (int), transactions_returned (int), partial (bool), filings[] each {owner {name, cik, role, relationship {isDirector, isOfficer, isTenPercentOwner, isOther, officerTitle}}, form, filing {accession, filedDate, form4_url}, transactions[] each {securityTitle, derivative, transactionCode, transactionLabel, acquiredDisposed, openMarket, shares, pricePerShare, transactionValue, transactionDate, directOrIndirect, sharesOwnedFollowing, filedDate, disclosure_lag_days}}, attribution, disclaimer. Verified live for {ticker:'AAPL', startdt:'2026-01-01', enddt:'2026-06-30'} -> Apple Inc. (cik 0000320193): 26 filings, 72 transactions, e.g. officer Jennifer Newstead (SVP, GC and Secretary) Form 4 sale of 16,238 shares @ $296.42 = $4,813,267.96 on 2026-06-15 (disclosure lag 2 days), each cited to its form4.xml on sec.gov.
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.
Supply ticker OR cik (cik accepts any zero-padding); startdt/enddt default to a 90-day window ending today when omitted.

transactionCode is the raw SEC Form-4 code (P=open-market purchase, S=sale, A=grant/award, F=tax-withholding, M=derivative exercise/conversion, X=option exercise, etc.); transactionLabel is the human-readable version.
pricePerShare/transactionValue are null for non-market events (grants, RSU conversions, tax-withholding) where no cash price applies.
derivative:true rows are derivative securities (RSUs, options); acquiredDisposed A=acquired, D=disposed; directOrIndirect D=direct, I=indirect holding.
openMarket flags whether the transaction was an open-market trade vs an internal grant/exercise.
partial:true signals the window was truncated (not all filings returned); attribution and a disclaimer ('Informational only, NOT investment advice...') are returned and should be displayed.
Filings are self-reported public disclosures and may be delayed, amended or incomplete; disclosure_lag_days is the gap between transaction and filing.
Distinct from the sibling Agentstools op /insider/signal (an aggregated insider buy/sell signal) — this op returns the raw per-transaction records.
usage.guide: Get every SEC-disclosed insider transaction for a company in one keyless x402 call, instead of scraping EDGAR Form 3/4/5 filings yourself. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/insider/trades with QUERY params: ticker (or issuer cik), optional startdt/enddt (ISO YYYY-MM-DD, default last 90 days), optional person substring and tx_codes[] filter. Synchronous — the 200 body carries entity {name, cik, ticker}, window, filings_returned/transactions_returned counts, and a filings[] array where each filing has the owner (name, cik, role, and a parsed relationship: isDirector/isOfficer/isTenPercentOwner + officerTitle), the form type, the filing {accession, filedDate, form4_url}, and transactions[] with securityTitle, derivative flag, transactionCode + human label, acquiredDisposed, openMarket, shares, pricePerShare, transactionValue, transactionDate, directOrIndirect, sharesOwnedFollowing and disclosure_lag_days. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {ticker:'AAPL', startdt:'2026-01-01', enddt:'2026-06-30'} -> Apple Inc., 26 filings / 72 transactions incl. an officer's $4.8M open-market sale, each cited to its form4.xml on sec.gov.

entries.name: Agentstools Insurance Bulletins
entries.description: Recent US state Department of Insurance bulletins, circular letters and notices for a given state, normalized to title, source url, year and type with a linkback to the issuing department.

state.description: US state or territory name or 2-letter code, e.g. 'California' or 'CA'. The primary input.

keyword.description: Optional keyword to filter bulletin titles.

year_from.description: Only bulletins from this year onward.

limit.description: Max items to return, default 25.

inputSchema.description: All inputs are query params on a GET (no request body). No field is strictly required by the schema, but `state` is the useful primary input; keyword/year_from/limit are optional filters.

state.description: Normalized state name, e.g. 'New York'.

source.description: The issuing department feed, e.g. {name:'NY Department of Financial Services — Circular Letters', url, host:'www.dfs.ny.gov'}.

returned.description: Number of items actually returned in this page (<= limit, default 25).

sources.description: {errors{}, partial (bool), used[] (states used)} — response is marked partial rather than failing on an upstream problem.

attribution.description: e.g. 'Source: NY Department of Financial Services — Circular Letters (www.dfs.ny.gov)' — must be shown.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/insurance/bulletins?state=<state>[&year_from=<year>][&keyword=<kw>][&limit=1-100] — all inputs are query params, no request body. `state` (name or 2-letter code) is the primary input; keyword/year_from are optional filters; limit defaults to 25 (max 100). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON on the paid 200: { found (bool), state (normalized name), source{name, url, host}, count (total matched), returned (page size, <= limit), items:[{title, url, date (often null), year, type e.g. 'circular_letter', state}] newest first, provenance{source_url, retrieved}, sources{errors{}, partial, used:[state codes]}, attribution:['Source: NY Department of Financial Services — Circular Letters (www.dfs.ny.gov)'], disclaimer }. Verified paid response for state=NY year_from=2025: found=true, count=10, returned=10, items = NY DFS circular letters (Coverage of Immunizations, Disaster Planning, PrEP HIV prior-auth, etc.).
quirks: GET with all inputs as query params (no body); `state` is the primary input (US state/territory name or 2-letter code). Method is GET per the openapi/402 (the bazaar schema also lists HEAD/DELETE as allowed methods, but GET is the read verb).

Coverage is a CURATED SUBSET of reachable states, not all 50 — the disclaimer notes it 'may lag the department site' and it is partial-on-failure (sources.partial rather than a 500). sources.used[] echoes which state feeds were actually queried.

Per-item `date` is frequently null (many circular letters carry only a year); `year` is populated and items are returned newest first. `type` observed as 'circular_letter' for NY (varies by state department taxonomy).
`count` is the total number of bulletins matched while `returned` (<= `limit`, default 25, max 100) is the actual page size — do not treat count as the number of items in the response.
402 body is empty ({}); the x402 challenge (accepts + bazaar input/output schema) is carried in the base64 `payment-required` response header, not the body.

Public regulatory guidance normalized with a linkback to the issuing department; not legal advice. Attribution must be shown. Distinct sibling ops on the same host: /insurance/state-adoption and /insurance/model-law (different operations, indexed separately).
usage.guide: Get recent US state Department of Insurance bulletins/circular letters with one keyless x402 GET. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/insurance/bulletins?state=<state> (name or 2-letter code, the primary input), optionally &year_from=<year> to floor by year, &keyword=<kw> to filter titles, and &limit=1-100 (default 25). No request body. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless. Synchronous — the 200 body carries found, the source feed {name, url, host}, count (total matched), returned (page size), and items[] {title, url, date (often null), year, type, state} newest first, plus provenance, sources (with a partial flag + used[] states), a required attribution and a disclaimer. Use it for insurance regulatory/compliance monitoring to surface a state's recent circular letters and notices. Coverage is a curated subset of reachable states and may lag the department site; count is the total match count while returned/items.length is the page size.

entries.name: Agentstools Treasury Auctions
entries.description: Returns recent US Treasury auction results plus the upcoming-auction calendar for a security type (Bill, Note, Bond, TIPS, FRN, CMB) from TreasuryDirect, normalized per auction (CUSIP, term, dates, offering/accepted amounts, bid-to-cover, high yield, bidder breakdown) with computed demand signals (latest/average bid-to-cover, bid-to-cover trend, average indirect-bidder share).

type.description: Security type to fetch auctions for (required).

term.description: Optional exact security term filter, e.g. '10-Year'.

days.description: Look back this many days for auction results (optional).

upcoming.description: Also attach the forward auction calendar (optional).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/treasury/auctions?type=<Bill|Note|Bond|TIPS|FRN|CMB>[&term=<exact term, e.g. 10-Year>][&days=<1-3660>][&upcoming=<true|false>] — all inputs are query params, no request body; only type is required. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: type, window_days, count, auctions[] (each: cusip, security_type, security_term, auction_date, issue_date, maturity_date, offering_amount, total_accepted, bid_to_cover, high_yield, high_discount_rate, interest_rate, competitive_accepted, indirect_accepted, direct_accepted, primary_dealer_accepted, soma_accepted, maturing_amount, source), signals{latest_bid_to_cover, avg_bid_to_cover, bid_to_cover_trend[]{auction_date,bid_to_cover}, avg_indirect_share}, provenance{source,dataset}, attribution[], and (when upcoming=true) upcoming[]{cusip,security_type,security_term,auction_date,issue_date}.

term, days and upcoming are optional query params (no request body); term is an exact security-term filter like '10-Year'.
days is the lookback window in days (1-3660) for completed auction results; the upcoming calendar is only attached when upcoming=true.
The endpoint computes signals a raw feed does not: latest/average bid-to-cover, a per-auction bid_to_cover_trend series, and the average indirect-bidder share (demand gauge).
