entries.name: Agentstools Treasury Cash
entries.description: US Treasury operating cash balance (the Treasury General Account) from the Daily Treasury Statement — the latest TGA closing balance, the daily history over a window and the day-over-day change flagged as a build or drawdown, cited to Treasury Fiscal Data.

days.description: Look back this many days of the daily cash balance.

unit.description: e.g. USD_millions — balances are in millions of US dollars.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/treasury/cash with optional QUERY params (no body): days (1-3660, default 30) or its alias range, choosing how many days of daily cash-balance history to return. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: series ('operating_cash_balance'), account ('Treasury General Account (TGA)'), unit ('USD_millions'), window_days, latest {record_date, balance}, history[] each {record_date, balance}, computed {daily_change, direction: build|drawdown}, provenance {source, dataset, record_date}, attribution[] (string). Verified live for {days:30}: latest record_date 2026-08-06 balance 961726 (USD millions), 22-row daily history back to 2026-07-08, computed daily_change 32401 direction 'build', provenance source 'fiscaldata' dataset 'operating_cash_balance'.
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.
No params are required; days defaults to 30. days and range are aliases (both 1-3660) selecting the history window.
Balances are in millions of US dollars (unit: USD_millions).
computed.direction is 'build' (balance rose) or 'drawdown' (balance fell) vs the prior reporting day.
history only spans business/reporting days (weekends/holidays absent), so a 30-day window returns ~22 rows.
No data for the window returns 404 and an upstream failure 502 (never 500); attribution ('Source: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Fiscal Data (public domain)') should be shown.
usage.guide: Read the US government's checking-account balance (the Treasury General Account) with a single keyless x402 GET — a widely watched liquidity signal. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/treasury/cash?days=<N> (default 30; range is an alias, both 1-3660). No request body. Synchronous — the 200 body carries series, account, unit (USD_millions), window_days, latest {record_date, balance}, history[] (daily {record_date, balance}), computed {daily_change, direction: build|drawdown}, provenance and attribution. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {days:30} -> latest 2026-08-06 TGA balance 961,726 (USD millions), day-over-day +32,401 ('build'), with the full ~22-day history. Sibling ops on the same host cover the yield curve (/treasury/rates), the monthly statement (/treasury/statement), federal debt (/treasury/debt) and auctions (/treasury/auctions).

entries.name: Agentstools Treasury Debt
entries.description: Authoritative US federal debt from Treasury Fiscal Data (Debt to the Penny) — latest total public debt split into debt held by the public vs. intragovernmental holdings, the full daily history over a chosen window with computed net issuance and shares, plus the latest interest expense on the public debt broken down by security type, every value cited to Treasury Fiscal Data.

days.description: Look back this many days of daily debt history (default: latest window).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/treasury/debt with optional query param ?days=<int 1-3660> (alias ?range=<int>) selecting how many days of daily debt history to return; omit for the default window. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: series ("debt_to_penny"), unit ("USD"), window_days, latest {record_date, total_public_debt, debt_held_by_public, intragovernmental_holdings}, history[] (daily rows, newest-first, same fields as latest), computed {net_issuance_over_window, public_share, intragovernmental_share, from_date, to_date}, provenance {source, dataset, record_date}, interest_expense {record_date, accrued_public_issues {month_expense, fytd_expense}, breakdown[] (per security type: {security, month_expense, fytd_expense}), unit, note}, and attribution[]. Verified live for {days:30}: latest 2026-08-06 total_public_debt 39,890,263,441,627.83 (debt_held_by_public 32,148,910,864,804.21; intragovernmental 7,741,352,576,823.62); computed net_issuance_over_window 495,285,795,988.78, public_share 0.805934, from_date 2026-07-08 to_date 2026-08-06; interest_expense record_date 2026-07-31 (month 78,044,809,442.17; fytd 679,047,498,114.83); attribution ["Source: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Fiscal Data (public domain)"].
quirks: Both `days` and its alias `range` are optional integers clamped to 1-3660; omitting them returns the default window (30 days observed).
`history[]` is returned newest-first; `computed.net_issuance_over_window` is the total-debt change across the window (a net-issuance proxy).

The `interest_expense` block is fused from a separate Treasury series and lags the debt series (its own record_date, e.g. month-end 2026-07-31 vs debt 2026-08-06); it carries current-month and fiscal-year-to-date figures plus a per-security breakdown.
No data for the window returns 404, an upstream data-source failure returns 502 — never a 500.
Data is public-domain U.S. Government work sourced from Treasury Fiscal Data (Debt to the Penny); attribution[] cites the source.
Treasury siblings on this host are different ops: /treasury/rates, /treasury/statement, /treasury/cash, /treasury/auctions.
usage.guide: Get authoritative US federal debt (Treasury Debt to the Penny) in one keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/treasury/debt?days=<N> (alias ?range=<N>), N in 1..3660; omit for the default ~30-day window. Synchronous — the 200 body carries {series, unit, window_days, latest {record_date, total_public_debt, debt_held_by_public, intragovernmental_holdings}, history[] (daily, newest-first), computed {net_issuance_over_window, public_share, intragovernmental_share, from_date, to_date}, provenance, interest_expense {record_date, accrued_public_issues {month_expense, fytd_expense}, breakdown[] by security type, unit, note}, attribution[]}. Use latest for the current headline debt, computed.net_issuance_over_window for supply pressure over the window, and interest_expense for debt-servicing cost. No data for the window returns 404, upstream failure 502. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: ?days=30 -> total_public_debt ~$39.89T on 2026-08-06, ~80.6% held by the public, net issuance ~$495B over 30 days.

entries.name: Agentstools Treasury Rates
entries.description: US Treasury interest rates in one call: the Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve (1m through 30y) fused with the official average interest rates on the outstanding debt by security type, plus the computed 2s10s spread and yield-curve inversion flag.

year.description: Calendar year of the par yield curve to return (query param, optional; defaults to the current year).

average_interest_rates.description: {record_date, unit ('percent'), rates[{security_type (Marketable|Non-marketable|Interest-bearing Debt), security (e.g. Treasury Bills, Treasury Notes, TIPS, Total Interest-bearing Debt), avg_interest_rate (number, percent)}]} — official Treasury average interest rates on the outstanding debt by security type.

par_yield_curve.description: {date, unit ('percent'), year, points{1m,2m,3m,4m,6m,1y,2y,3y,5y,7y,10y,20y,30y}} — the Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve for the requested year (may omit tenors on some dates).

yield_curve_available.description: true when the par yield curve grain resolved; false when its upstream was unreachable and only average rates are returned.

computed.description: {spread_2s10s (10y minus 2y par yield, percentage points), inverted_2s10s (bool, true when 2s10s < 0)}.

attribution.description: Public-domain source lines (U.S. Department of the Treasury, Fiscal Data + Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates) — must be shown.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/treasury/rates[?year=YYYY] — the only input is an optional `year` query param (integer 1990-2100, defaults to the current year); no request body. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.015 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: {average_interest_rates{record_date, unit, rates[{security_type, security, avg_interest_rate}]}, par_yield_curve{date, unit, year, points{1m,2m,3m,4m,6m,1y,2y,3y,5y,7y,10y,20y,30y}}, yield_curve_available (bool), computed{spread_2s10s, inverted_2s10s (bool)}, attribution[]}
quirks: The only input is an optional `year` query param on a GET (no body); a bare GET returns the current year. Documented method enum is GET|HEAD|DELETE but GET is the read.

Two fused grains: `average_interest_rates` (monthly avg interest rate on the outstanding debt by security type, keyed to record_date) and `par_yield_curve` (Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve, keyed to its own trade date) — their dates differ (verified: avg rates record_date 2026-07-31 vs par curve date 2026-08-07).

The par yield curve is a resilient partial grain: if its upstream is unreachable, yield_curve_available goes false and par_yield_curve/computed may be absent while average_interest_rates still returns.
`computed.spread_2s10s` is 10y-minus-2y par yield in percentage points and `inverted_2s10s` flags a negative spread (verified: spread 0.46, inverted false on 2026-08-07).
Public-domain US Treasury Fiscal Data; the attribution[] lines must be shown. Informational only.
Priced at $0.015 USDC via x402 on Base; the paid call used a live-quoted 402 (accepts amount 15000 = $0.015), no price drift.
usage.guide: Get a full snapshot of US Treasury interest rates with a single keyless x402 GET. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/treasury/rates with an optional `year` query param (integer 1990-2100; defaults to the current year) — no request body. Pays $0.015 USDC via x402 on Base. Synchronous — the 200 body fuses two grains: `average_interest_rates` (the official monthly average interest rates the Treasury pays on its outstanding debt by security type — Treasury Bills/Notes/Bonds/TIPS/FRN, marketable vs non-marketable, and totals, each with avg_interest_rate in percent) and `par_yield_curve` (the Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve, points from 1m through 30y for the requested year). It also returns `computed.spread_2s10s` (the 10y-minus-2y spread in percentage points) and `inverted_2s10s`, plus `yield_curve_available` and public-domain `attribution[]`. The par-curve grain is resilient: if its upstream is down, yield_curve_available goes false and only the average rates come back. Use it for fixed-income/macro analysis — reading the shape of the curve, spotting a 2s10s inversion, or checking the government's cost of debt by security type.

entries.name: Agentstools Treasury Statement
entries.description: The US Monthly Treasury Statement as a federal-budget scorecard: receipts, outlays and the deficit/surplus for the latest month and fiscal year to date, with the same figures for the prior fiscal year, plus computed year-over-year deficit change and interest expense as a share of receipts — sourced from US Treasury Fiscal Data.

note.description: deficit is positive; a negative value is a surplus.

deficit_yoy_change.description: Fiscal-YTD deficit change vs prior year, in USD.

interest_pct_of_receipts_fytd.description: Interest expense on public debt as a share of fiscal-YTD receipts.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/treasury/statement with no query params and no body. x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.02. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous).
usage.outputShape: statement { record_date, fiscal_year, month, current_month{receipts,outlays,deficit}, fiscal_ytd{...}, prior_year_month{...}, prior_year_ytd{...}, unit, note }, computed { deficit_yoy_change (USD), deficit_yoy_pct, interest_pct_of_receipts_fytd }, provenance { source ("fiscaldata"), dataset ("mts_table_1"), record_date }, attribution[] (public-domain citation), interest_expense { record_date, accrued_public_issues{month_expense,fytd_expense}, breakdown[]{security,month_expense,fytd_expense}, unit, note }. Deficit is reported as a POSITIVE number; a negative value is a surplus. All figures in USD.
quirks: No inputs at all — a bare GET returns the latest published month; there are no query params or body.
Deficit is reported as a POSITIVE number; a negative value is a surplus (see statement.note).

The interest_expense block carries its OWN record_date (the outstanding-debt interest series), which can be a later month than statement.record_date (the MTS month) — they are fused from two Treasury Fiscal Data feeds.

computed.deficit_yoy_change and deficit_yoy_pct compare fiscal-YTD deficit against the prior fiscal year; interest_pct_of_receipts_fytd is interest expense on the public debt as a share of fiscal-YTD receipts.
Data is public-domain US Treasury Fiscal Data (dataset mts_table_1); no statement available returns 404, an upstream failure 502.
usage.guide: US Monthly Treasury Statement — the federal budget scorecard. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/treasury/statement (no params, no body). x402 v2 on Base USDC, $0.02, no API key. Synchronous — the 200 body carries statement{record_date, fiscal_year, month, current_month{receipts,outlays,deficit}, fiscal_ytd{...}, prior_year_month{...}, prior_year_ytd{...}}, computed{deficit_yoy_change, deficit_yoy_pct, interest_pct_of_receipts_fytd}, an interest_expense breakdown by security type, and provenance/attribution to US Treasury Fiscal Data (public domain). Deficit values are POSITIVE; a negative value is a surplus.

entries.name: Agentstools Prevailing Wage
entries.description: US prevailing-wage determination for an occupation and location — the DOL OFLC four statutory wage levels (Level 1-4) plus the average, hourly and annualized, with the geographic level, wage year and citation, resolving the occupation by SOC/O*NET code or free text and the location by OFLC area, county+state or metro name, with an optional offered-wage compliance flag.

occupation.description: Occupation title as free text (e.g. 'software developer'). Alternative to soc/onet.

soc.description: SOC occupation code, e.g. 15-1252. Alternative to occupation/onet.

onet.description: O*NET-SOC code, e.g. 15-1252.00. Alternative to occupation/soc.

county.description: County name (supply with state) to resolve the OFLC wage area.

state.description: Two-letter US state code (e.g. CA, NY), used with county.

area.description: OFLC area code (e.g. 41940), an alternative to county+state/msa.

msa.description: Metro or nonmetro area name, an alternative to county+state/area.

level.description: Wage level 1 to 4 to focus the determination.

wage_source.description: Wage population; default all_industries. Use acwia for higher-education / non-profit research employers.

offered_wage.description: Offered wage to compliance-check against the prevailing level.

levels.description: Keyed by level '1'-'4', each { hourly, annual }.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/wage/prevailing with query params (no body). Identify the occupation via one of soc | onet | occupation (free text) and the location via one of area | county+state | msa; optional level (1-4), wage_source (all_industries default | acwia), offered_wage + offered_basis (hour|year, default year) for a compliance flag. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON: found (bool), soc (SOC code e.g. '15-1252'), soc_title (e.g. 'Software Developers'), area (OFLC area code e.g. '41940'), area_name (e.g. 'San Jose-Sunnyvale-Santa Clara, CA'), geo_level (int), wage_source ('all_industries'|'acwia'), wage_year (e.g. '2025-26'), levels{ '1'..'4': { hourly, annual } } (the four statutory DOL OFLC level wages, hourly + annualized at 2080h), average{ hourly, annual }, compliance{ meets_level (int), below_prevailing (bool) } when offered_wage is supplied, and attribution ('DOL OFLC Wage Files + BLS OES (public domain)'). NOTE: this is the provider's documented openapi 200 example — the live paid call returned a degraded payload { wage_year, available:false, status:'unavailable', note:'OFLC prevailing-wage index is still building; retry shortly', disclaimer, attribution } (the four-tier wages were NOT populated at index time).
quirks: Fixed price $0.02 (openapi x-payment-info mode:fixed), not dynamic; live 402 accepts amount '20000' USDC (6dp) on Base confirms it.

All inputs are query params on a GET (no request body); OpenAPI marks every param optional but a usable determination needs an occupation identifier (soc | onet | occupation) plus a location identifier (area | county+state | msa).

PAID-BUT-DEGRADED at index time: the paid HTTP 200 returned { available:false, status:'unavailable', note:'OFLC prevailing-wage index is still building; retry shortly' } instead of the four-tier level wages. Route is live and billable, but the substantive determination was not returned for this query when indexed (2026-08-07) — retry expected to yield the full payload. Do NOT re-pay on the strength of this note alone.

Occupation resolves from a SOC code, an O*NET-SOC code or free-text title; location from an OFLC area code, a county+state, or a metro-area (msa) name. Cheaper resolver steps exist: /wage/occupations ($0.005) maps a title -> ranked SOC candidates and /wage/areas ($0.005) maps a location -> ranked OFLC area codes.
wage_source enum all_industries (default) | acwia (ACWIA population for higher-ed and non-profit research employers).
Supply offered_wage (+ optional offered_basis hour|year, default year) to get a compliance{ meets_level, below_prevailing } flag versus the prevailing level.

These are the DOL OFLC published ready level wages (from the BLS OES survey), the legally operative figures for an H-1B LCA or a PERM certification — public labor-market data, not legal/immigration advice; for an official determination file ETA Form 9141 via FLAG. See /wage/sources for provenance and wage year.
usage.guide: US prevailing-wage (DOL OFLC four-tier) determination for immigration-law, HR and offer-compliance agents. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/wage/prevailing with query params: identify the occupation via soc (e.g. 15-1252) OR onet OR occupation (free text like 'software developer'), and the location via area (OFLC code) OR county+state (e.g. county='Santa Clara'&state=CA) OR msa (metro name); optionally add level (1-4), wage_source (all_industries|acwia), and offered_wage(+offered_basis) for a compliance check. No body. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base, keyless, synchronous. Returns the four statutory level wages (hourly + annualized) plus the average, geo_level, wage_year, SOC/area resolution and attribution. If the occupation or area is unknown, resolve it first with /wage/occupations ($0.005) and /wage/areas ($0.005). NOTE: at index time (2026-08-07) the paid 200 returned status:'unavailable' (OFLC index still building) — retry to get the full determination; the output shape above is the provider's openapi example.

entries.name: Agentstools Bank Health Verdict
entries.description: Return a deterministic financial-health verdict for a US FDIC-insured bank from public call-report data — a 0-100 health score (higher is healthier), an A-F letter grade, derived proxy metrics (capital ratios, a Texas-ratio proxy, uninsured-deposit exposure, ROA trend) and per-dimension signals, all grounded to the reporting date, sourced from the FDIC BankFind Suite.

cert.description: FDIC certificate number (preferred). Resolves the institution directly in the FDIC BankFind Suite.

name.description: Bank name (used if no cert). Matched against FDIC BankFind.

state.description: Optional 2-letter US state code to disambiguate a name match.

as_of.description: Reporting date (REPDTE) the figures are grounded to.

derived_metrics.description: Per-metric {value, fraction}: total_rbc_ratio, tier-1 leverage, Texas-ratio proxy, uninsured-deposit exposure, ROA trend, etc.

sources.description: Provenance; partial:true and an errors{} map when an upstream source is down.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/bankhealth/verdict with query params: cert=<FDIC certificate number, integer, preferred>, OR name=<bank name>, plus optional state=<2-letter US code>. No request body. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.03 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: verdict ('found'|'not_found'), health_score (0-100, higher=healthier), letter_grade (A-F), rating, as_of (REPDTE), query {name,cert,state}, institution {name,cert,active,state}, derived_metrics {metric:{value,fraction}} (e.g. total_rbc_ratio 16.25), signals[] {dimension,points} (e.g. capital_adequacy 30), reasons[], sources {partial, errors{}}, attribution[], disclaimer. Documented success example (openapi/402): cert 628 -> verdict 'found', health_score 86, letter_grade 'A', as_of '2026-03-31', institution 'JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.'. AT INDEX TIME the paid 200 for cert=628 returned verdict 'not_found' with sources.partial=true and errors {failures/institutions/financials: 'upstream FDIC returned HTTP 403'} — the route, payment and envelope are proven live but the upstream FDIC BankFind API was returning 403 to the provider, so no live scored verdict was captured.
quirks: Give `cert` (FDIC certificate number) for a deterministic direct match; `name` (optionally with `state`) is a fallback fuzzy match. cert 628 = JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.
health_score polarity is INVERTED vs risk scores: HIGHER means HEALTHIER (0-100), mapped to an A-F letter_grade.

Figures are DERIVED PROXIES from public FDIC call-report data (capital ratios vs well-capitalized thresholds, a Texas-ratio proxy, uninsured-deposit exposure, ROA trend) — explicitly NOT the confidential CAMELS supervisory rating and NOT a resale of a paid bank rating. Not financial/investment/deposit-safety advice.

Degrades gracefully: when an upstream FDIC source is down the response is partial (sources.partial=true + a per-source errors{} map) rather than erroring; nothing found returns verdict 'not_found'. At index time the upstream FDIC BankFind Suite returned HTTP 403 to the provider, yielding a not_found/partial result for cert=628.
Call-report data is quarterly and lags; every figure is grounded to as_of / REPDTE. Include the attribution[] (FDIC BankFind Suite, US-gov public domain) when redistributing.
US FDIC-insured banks only. Inactive/failed charters are flagged and capped low. Credit unions and enforcement-action/peer-benchmark datasets are declared as deferred future coverage.
usage.guide: Vet the financial health of a US FDIC-insured bank in one keyless x402 call — for treasury, counterparty-risk, BaaS/fintech-partner selection or M&A due diligence. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/bankhealth/verdict?cert=<FDIC certificate number> (preferred; e.g. ?cert=628 for JPMorgan Chase), or ?name=<bank name>[&state=<2-letter US code>] if you don't have the cert. Synchronous — the 200 body carries a deterministic verdict: health_score (0-100, HIGHER is HEALTHIER), an A-F letter_grade, derived_metrics (total risk-based capital ratio, tier-1 leverage, a Texas-ratio problem-asset proxy, uninsured-deposit exposure, ROA trend), per-dimension signals[] with points, and everything grounded to the FDIC reporting date (as_of). These are transparent proxies from public FDIC call-report data, NOT CAMELS and NOT financial advice — show the attribution[]. Pays $0.03 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), no API key or account. Note: at index time the upstream FDIC BankFind API was returning HTTP 403 to the provider, so a live call may come back verdict 'not_found' with sources.partial=true until the FDIC source recovers.

entries.name: Agentstools FDA Catalyst Calendar
entries.description: Forward-looking FDA regulatory catalyst calendar for one biotech issuer (by ticker or CIK), deterministically extracted from primary SEC 8-K/6-K filings — upcoming PDUFA target action dates, advisory-committee meetings, Complete Response Letters, priority reviews and PDUFA extensions, each date grounded in a quote from the filing and cited to its accession and EDGAR URL.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol, e.g. SRRK. Provide ticker OR cik to identify the issuer.

cik.description: SEC EDGAR issuer CIK, any zero-padding accepted. Provide ticker OR cik.

event_types.description: Optional comma-separated filter of regulatory event types to include (default all). One or more of: pdufa, adcomm, crl, priority_review, pdufa_extension.

forward_only.description: Only future-dated events (default true). Set false to also include historical dates.

lookback_days.description: How far back (days) to search the issuer's filings, default 270.

found.description: Whether the issuer was resolved and any filings scanned.

raw_date.description: Raw date text as it appeared in the filing.

year_inferred.description: True when the year was inferred (the filing wrote only a month/day).

quote.description: The surrounding sentence window that grounds the date.

partial.description: True if not all filings could be fetched/parsed.

Verified live for {ticker:'SRRK', forward_only:true}: found=true, entity=Scholar Rock Holding Corp (CIK 0001727196), filings_scanned=7, events_returned=1 — one upcoming pdufa event date_iso 2026-09-30 (raw 'September 30, 2026') grounded to 8-K accn 0001193125-26-336715 filed 2026-08-06.
quirks: Identify the issuer by ticker OR cik — both are optional in the schema but you must supply one, else no issuer resolves. cik accepts any zero-padding.

Precision-first extraction: a date is emitted ONLY when a regulatory keyword co-occurs with it in the same sentence window (deterministic regex/structural parser, no LLM) — a filing mentioning PDUFA without a nearby date yields nothing rather than a guess, so events[] can be empty for a real issuer with no dated catalysts in the lookback window.
forward_only defaults true (only future-dated events); set false to also get historical dates (direction field distinguishes upcoming vs historical).
When an issuer has reported several competing future dates for the same event across filings, the older ones are flagged as possibly superseded and the latest-filed date is marked canonical.
year_inferred=true means the filing wrote only a month/day and the year was inferred — treat that date_iso as lower-confidence than a filing that stated the full date.

The 402 quote comes in the `payment-required` HEADER (base64 JSON) and the 402 BODY is empty ({}) — an x402 client that only parses accepts from the body will fail to pay; read the header. (Same Agentstools pattern as its drug/* ops.)

SEC-sourced (public domain) and informational only — regulatory dates are set by the FDA and may be extended, missed or superseded; NOT investment advice. Preserve the attribution string on redisplay.

queryParams.bill_id: Bill id like hr3076-118 (billtype+number-congress). Supply this OR the congress+billType+billNumber triple.
queryParams.congress: Congress number, e.g. 118 (use with billType+billNumber). Optional.
queryParams.billType: Bill type, one of hr|s|hjres|sjres|hconres|sconres|hres|sres (use with congress+billNumber). Optional.

bill.description: Normalized bill: congress, type, number, title, introducedDate, sponsor, cosponsor count, committees, policyArea, originChamber, becameLaw. null when found=false.

lifecycle.description: Ordered stages [{stage, date, (source action text)}] from introduced to became_law/vetoed/failed.

textVersions.description: GovInfo text/PDF links (populated when a free api.data.gov key is configured).

sources.description: { partial, rate_limited, providers[], errors{provider:message} } — best-effort provenance and per-source errors.

quirks: Two ways to identify the bill: bill_id (e.g. hr3076-118) OR the congress+billType+billNumber triple; billType enum is hr|s|hjres|sjres|hconres|sconres|hres|sres. No request body — all input is query params.

IMPORTANT — at index time (paid probe 2026-08-07, bill_id=hr3076-118) the endpoint returned HTTP 200 with its correct documented envelope but found=false / bill=null because the upstream Congress.gov API (api.congress.gov) returned HTTP 403 to the provider (sources.errors.congress='upstream api.congress.gov returned HTTP 403', partial=true). The differentiator is the computed, stateless lifecycle[] (ordered stages introduced->referred->reported->passed House->passed Senate->resolving differences->to president->became law/vetoed/failed), each with date and source action text — derived from the action history, not resold raw.
textVersions (GovInfo text + PDF links) are only attached when a free api.data.gov key is configured on the provider side; otherwise that slice is empty/not_configured, which is not a failure.
Static price ($0.02 = amount 20000 at 6 USDC decimals), captured from the live 402 payment-required header (body is empty {}), not a dynamic quote.

bill_id.description: Bill id like 'hr3076-118' (billType+billNumber-congress). Convenient single-string alternative to congress+billType+billNumber.

congress.description: Congress number (used with billType + billNumber instead of bill_id).

inputSchema.description: All inputs are query params on a GET (no request body). Identify the bill either via bill_id (e.g. 'hr3076-118') OR via congress + billType + billNumber. Scope the window with either since (ISO date) or window_days.

query.description: Echo of the parsed inputs: {congress, billType, billNumber, bill_id, since, window_days}.

found.description: Whether the bill was resolved and lifecycle data retrieved from upstream.

current_stage.description: The latest lifecycle stage reached, e.g. 'became_law', 'passed_senate' (null when not found).

events.description: The lifecycle-event diff within the requested window, each with stage + date.

all_stages.description: Full list of stages observed for the bill (superset of the windowed events).

sources.description: {errors{}, partial (bool), rate_limited (bool), providers[] e.g. ['congress']} — response is marked partial rather than failing on an upstream problem.

attribution.description: Must be shown, e.g. 'Congress.gov API (api.congress.gov), Library of Congress' and 'GovInfo (govinfo.gov), U.S. GPO'.

entries.name: Agentstools Price Discover
entries.description: Finds a US hospital's machine-readable price files (MRFs) from its website domain by reading the federally-mandated root cms-hpt.txt pointer, returning each location's name, human source page, MRF URL and detected file format (json, csv, json.gz or csv.gz).

domain.description: Hospital website domain to discover from, e.g. nemours.org.

mrf_url.description: A machine-readable-file URL to classify directly instead of discovering from a domain.

source.description: The cms-hpt.txt pointer the MRF was discovered from.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/price/discover?domain=<hospital-domain> — pass either domain (discover from a hospital website) or mrf_url (classify a known file URL directly) as a query param; no request body. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.005 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: query{domain}, found (bool), location_count (int), locations[] (each: location_name, source_page_url, mrf_url, detected_format one of json|csv|json.gz|csv.gz, source = the cms-hpt.txt pointer), attribution, disclaimer.
quirks: GET with query params only, no request body. Pass either domain (a hospital website domain like nemours.org) or mrf_url (a known MRF URL to classify directly); both params are technically optional in the schema but one is needed for a useful result.

This is the cheap first step of the hospital price-transparency workflow: feed a returned mrf_url into /price/hospital (Agentstools) to read actual negotiated, gross and cash prices for a procedure code.
Reads the federally-mandated root /cms-hpt.txt pointer, falling back to a known /documents/ path; a multi-hospital system can list several location blocks.
Not-found is returned cleanly as {found:false,...} (never a 500) when a hospital does not expose a readable pointer file.

Output is informational discovery from the hospital's own published files + US-government public data — NOT a quote, bill or guarantee of coverage; every response echoes an attribution and disclaimer string.
Verified live: domain=nemours.org → found=true, location_count=2, both NEMOURS CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL standardcharges.csv MRFs (detected_format csv) discovered from https://nemours.org/cms-hpt.txt.
usage.guide: Locate a US hospital's machine-readable price files with a single keyless x402 GET. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/price/discover?domain=<hospital-domain> (e.g. nemours.org), or pass mrf_url=<known-file-url> to classify a file directly. No request body; pays $0.005 USDC via x402 on Base. Synchronous — the 200 body carries found, location_count and locations[] where each entry gives the location_name, the human source_page_url, the machine-readable-file mrf_url and its detected_format (json|csv|json.gz|csv.gz), plus the cms-hpt.txt source, attribution and a disclaimer. It reads the hospital's federally-mandated root /cms-hpt.txt pointer (falling back to /documents/) and returns not-found cleanly when none exists. Use it as the cheap first step of price-transparency workflows, then feed a returned mrf_url into Agentstools Price Hospital (/price/hospital) to read the actual negotiated, gross and cash prices for a procedure code.

entries.name: Agentstools Hospital Price
entries.description: Fused, cited hospital price for one procedure billing code at one hospital — gross charge, discounted cash price, de-identified min/max and every payer-specific negotiated rate — streamed from the hospital's own CMS machine-readable file (located via domain auto-discovery or an MRF URL) and fused with CMS Care Compare quality when a CCN or resolvable name is supplied. Informational, not a quote. Keyless pay-per-call x402.

backends.inputSchema: GET query params (no request body). Required: code (string — procedure billing code, e.g. '96365' or '27447'). To locate the hospital file supply EITHER domain (string — hospital domain to auto-discover its machine-readable file, e.g. 'nemours.org') OR mrf_url (string — a machine-readable-file URL from /price/discover). Optional: code_type (array of billing-code systems to constrain the match; enum CPT|HCPCS|MS-DRG|DRG|APC|NDC|ICD-10|CDM|local), payer (string — substring to filter returned negotiated rates), ccn (string — 6-digit CMS Certification Number to fuse Care Compare quality).
backends.outputSchema: { query: {code, code_type[], payer, ccn, mrf_url}, found (bool), match_count (int), charges[]: {description, setting (inpatient|outpatient|both), billing_class, gross_charge (num), discounted_cash (num), minimum (num), maximum (num), codes[]: {code, type}, payers[]: {payer_name, plan_name, standard_charge_dollar (num), standard_charge_percentage (num|null), methodology (string), standard_charge_algorithm? (string)}}, quality: {overall_star_rating, state, ...}|null, citation: {mrf_url, hospital_name, last_updated_on, mrf_version, detected_format (csv|json)}, coverage: {truncated (bool), scanned_bytes (int), quality_fused (bool), quality_error}, attribution[], disclaimer }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/price/hospital?code=<billing code>&domain=<hospital domain> (or &mrf_url=<file URL> instead of domain). Required query param: code. No request body. x402 v2 paid endpoint, $0.04 USDC on Base; result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no polling).
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. charges[] carries each matching line from the hospital's machine-readable file normalized to one schema — description, setting, gross_charge, discounted_cash, min/max, the matched codes[], and payers[] (each payer/plan with its dollar amount and/or percentage, methodology and algorithm). found/match_count report whether the code was located; citation names the source file (hospital_name, last_updated_on, mrf_version, detected_format); coverage reports truncated/scanned_bytes and whether CMS quality was fused; quality (or null) holds Care Compare star rating + measures. Verified 2026-08-07 with {code:'96365', code_type:['CPT'], domain:'nemours.org'} -> HTTP 200, found=true, match_count=3 from NEMOURS CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL's CSV MRF (IV Therapy Prophylaxis, gross $1131, cash $1131, min $211.49/max $1040.52, ~28 payer-specific negotiated rates across FLORIDA BLUE/CIGNA/AETNA/TRICARE etc.); quality was null (no ccn supplied and the children's-hospital name did not resolve a Care Compare row — quality_fused=false, price answer still returned).
quirks: Only `code` is strictly required, but to locate the hospital's file you must also pass EITHER `domain` (auto-discovers the MRF) OR `mrf_url` — with neither, there is no file to scan.
All inputs are query params; there is no request body even though it reads like a POST body in the openapi bazaar example.
A code absent from the file returns found:false with no charges — a rate is never invented.
Very large MRFs are streamed with a scan cap: coverage.truncated=true with an honest coverage.scanned_bytes when the cap is hit (the paid Nemours file scanned ~46.7 MB without truncation).

CMS quality fusion is best-effort: pass a 6-digit `ccn` for reliable fusion; without it (or if the name doesn't resolve) quality=null and coverage.quality_fused=false while the price answer still succeeds.
Informational price estimate from the hospital's own published file + US public data — NOT a quote, bill, or guarantee of coverage (see response disclaimer/attribution).
Price $0.04 USDC on Base (eip155:8453); no API key. The x402 quote (accepts) lives in the base64 'payment-required' response header — the 402 body is an empty {}.
usage.guide: Get the negotiated, gross and cash prices a specific hospital publishes for one procedure billing code, fused with CMS quality. Send a GET to https://api.agentstools.dev/price/hospital with query params: `code` (the procedure billing code, e.g. '96365' or '27447', required) and EITHER `domain` (the hospital's domain, e.g. 'nemours.org', to auto-discover its CMS machine-readable file) OR `mrf_url` (a file URL from the sibling /price/discover). Optionally add `code_type` (constrain the billing-code system: CPT, HCPCS, MS-DRG, APC, NDC, ICD-10, CDM, local), `payer` (substring to filter negotiated rates), and `ccn` (6-digit CMS Certification Number to fuse Care Compare quality). No request body. It is a keyless x402 paid endpoint at $0.04 USDC on Base, synchronous — the result is inline in the 200 body, no polling. Read charges[] for each matching line normalized to one schema (description, setting, gross_charge, discounted_cash, min/max, and payers[] with each plan's dollar amount/percentage, methodology and algorithm); found/match_count tell you whether the code was located; citation names the source file (hospital name, last-updated date, version, format) and coverage flags truncation and whether quality was fused. Pass a ccn for reliable quality fusion — without one, quality may be null while the price answer still returns. Informational only, not a quote — verify with the provider and payer. Verified 2026-08-07 with {code:'96365', code_type:['CPT'], domain:'nemours.org'} -> HTTP 200, 3 matches from Nemours Children's Hospital's CSV MRF, $0.04 charged on Base.

entries.name: Agentstools Realestate Prices
entries.description: Read the FHFA House Price Index for a US geography — the latest purchase-only index level plus year-over-year, quarter-over-quarter and 5-year compound growth, a rising/flat/falling momentum flag, and a short history of recent observations.

geo.description: A state code or name, metro CBSA code, county FIPS, ZIP, or address.

type.description: How to read geo (auto reads a 5-digit number as a ZIP). Optional; default auto.

range.description: Most recent N index observations of history to return. Optional.

level.description: state | metro/cbsa (county/ZIP resolve up to state).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/realestate/prices with QUERY params (no body): geo (required — a state code/name, metro CBSA code, county FIPS, ZIP, or address), type (optional enum auto|state|county|cbsa|zip|address, how to read geo), range (optional integer 1-40, how many recent observations of history). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.015 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: geo {input, kind, label, geography, state}, hpi {level, place_id, geography, flavor, frequency, momentum {available (bool), latest_index (number), latest_period {year, period, frequency}, yoy_pct, qoq_pct, cagr_5yr_pct, trend}, history[] {year, period, index}, source, source_code}, attribution[] (strings), disclaimer. Verified live for {geo:'CA', range:12}: State: California, purchase-only quarterly series, latest_index 420.62 (2026 Q1), yoy_pct -0.534, qoq_pct 0.183, cagr_5yr_pct 4.442, trend 'falling', 12 quarters of history, sourced to FHFA House Price Index (public domain).
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.
Only geo is required; type and range are optional. type=auto reads a 5-digit number as a ZIP.
State and metro CBSA levels are served directly; a county FIPS or ZIP resolves UP to its state-level index (county/ZIP HPI files are developmental and not yet included) — the response notes this.
Sibling /realestate/rents is a distinct rent-index op, not this one.
A blank or unknown geo returns 400; a geography with no index returns 404.
US-only, public-domain FHFA source; attribution must be shown. Aggregate market-tier indicator — not an appraisal, per-address valuation, or investment advice (see disclaimer).
usage.guide: Get US home-price momentum for a place with one keyless x402 GET. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/realestate/prices?geo=<state|CBSA|county FIPS|ZIP|address>&range=<1-40>. Only geo is required (add type to force how geo is read, range for how much history). No request body. Synchronous — the 200 body carries geo {input, kind, geography, state}, hpi {level, flavor, frequency, momentum {latest_index, yoy_pct, qoq_pct, cagr_5yr_pct, trend}, history[] {year, period, index}, source}, attribution[] and disclaimer. Pays $0.015 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {geo:'CA', range:12} → California purchase-only HPI, latest index 420.62 (2026 Q1), YoY -0.534%, 5yr CAGR 4.442%, trend falling, cited to FHFA. County/ZIP inputs resolve up to the state index. For rent trends use the sibling /realestate/rents.

entries.name: Agentstools Realestate Rents

Aggregate market tier, US only — not an appraisal or per-address valuation.

geo.description: A state (2-letter code or name), metro CBSA code, county FIPS, ZIP, or a street address.

type.description: How to read geo. In auto a 5-digit number is a ZIP; use cbsa or county to disambiguate.

geo.description: Resolved geography: input, kind (state/cbsa/county/zip/address), label, geography, state.

rents.description: median_gross_rent {value, source, source_code, geography, period, unit} from Census ACS 5-Year; plus HUD Fair Market Rents by bedroom count (efficiency through 4BR, incl. Small Area FMRs keyed by ZIP where available) when the provider has a HUD token configured, else a fair_market_rents_note explaining FMR was omitted.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/realestate/rents with QUERY params (no body): geo (required — a state 2-letter code or name, a metro CBSA code, a county FIPS, a ZIP, or a street address), type (optional — auto|state|county|cbsa|zip|address; how to read geo). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.015 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: geo {input, kind, label, geography, state}; rents {median_gross_rent {value, source, source_code, geography, period, unit}, and HUD fair_market_rents by bedroom count when a HUD token is configured (else fair_market_rents_note)}; attribution[]; disclaimer. Verified live for {geo:'90001', type:'zip'} -> HTTP 200: ZIP/ZCTA 90001 (CA), rents.median_gross_rent value 1471 (source acs, code B25064_001E, ZCTA5 90001, ACS 5-Year 2023, USD/month), fair_market_rents_note 'HUD Fair Market Rents omitted (HUD_API_TOKEN not configured); ACS median gross rent shown.', attribution ['Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-Year'].
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.

geo accepts a state (2-letter code or name), a metro CBSA code, a county FIPS, a ZIP, or a street address; use type to disambiguate (auto reads a 5-digit number as a ZIP; pass type=cbsa or type=county to read a 5-digit number as a metro/county). Multi-word place names must be URL-encoded.

HUD Fair Market Rents are only included when the provider has a HUD token configured; the verified run returned rents.fair_market_rents_note 'HUD Fair Market Rents omitted (HUD_API_TOKEN not configured); ACS median gross rent shown.' — plan for FMR to be absent and only the ACS median gross rent returned.
Aggregate market-tier read only (state/metro/county/ZIP) — NOT an appraisal and NOT a per-address valuation. Coverage is United States only.
Every value carries its own provenance (source, source_code, geography, period, unit) and the response lists attribution[] for each source used.
Errors: blank or unknown geo -> 400; a geography with no rent data -> 404.

Narrower than the composite Agentstools Real Estate Market (/realestate/market), which also fuses FHFA HPI, ACS demographics and derivatives; use /realestate/rents for a focused, cheaper rents-only read.
usage.guide: Fetch focused rental-market indicators for one US geography with a single keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/realestate/rents with QUERY params: geo (required — a state 2-letter code or name like 'CA', a metro CBSA code, a county FIPS, a ZIP like '90001', or a street address), plus optional type=auto|state|county|cbsa|zip|address to disambiguate how geo is read (auto reads a 5-digit number as a ZIP; use type=cbsa or type=county to read one as a metro/county). Small Area FMRs keyed by ZIP where available) WHEN the provider has a HUD token configured; when HUD is not configured it falls back to ACS rent only with a fair_market_rents_note. Aggregate market-tier, US only — not an appraisal or per-address valuation. Pays $0.015 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {geo:'90001', type:'zip'} -> ZIP 90001 (CA) median gross rent $1,471/mo (ACS 5-Year 2023).

entries.name: Agentstools UCC Creditor
entries.description: Reverse UCC lien lookup by secured party: given a lender/creditor name and a US state, returns the business debtors on which that party currently holds active liens — its lien portfolio in that state — cited to the official state open-data portal.

secured_party.description: The secured party / lender / creditor name (fuzzy-matched), e.g. ALLY BANK.

state.description: Two-letter state code of the UCC index to search. Coverage is per-state; Connecticut (CT) at launch.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/ucc/creditor with QUERY params (no body): secured_party (required — a lender/creditor name, fuzzy-matched) and optional state (two-letter code; currently only CT is covered, defaults to CT). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: query {secured_party, state}, debtor_count (int), active_lien_count (int), debtors[] each {debtor, debtor_city, active_lien_count, lien_classes[] (e.g. ucc_secured, municipal_tax), latest_filed}, coverage {states[], license, source_freshness, collateral_available, disclaimer}, citations[] {source, dataset_url, license, accession_numbers[]}, result_truncated (bool), disclaimer, ts (epoch). Verified live for {secured_party:'ALLY BANK', state:'CT'}: 8 debtors / 31 active liens, top debtor 'HLI Solutions, Inc.' (Beachwood) with 18 active ucc_secured liens (latest_filed 2026-07-23), cited to the Connecticut Secretary of the State UCC & lien dataset (data.ct.gov/resource/xfev-8smz.json, Public Domain).
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.
`secured_party` is the only required param; it is fuzzy-matched, so pass the lender name as commonly written (e.g. 'ALLY BANK').
`state` currently only supports CT (Connecticut at launch); coverage is per-state and honestly labeled in coverage.states — it is NOT national.
This is the REVERSE lens (lender -> its debtors / lien portfolio). The forward due-diligence view (business name -> its creditors and encumbrances) is the separate /ucc/debtor op.
Active-lien status is COMPUTED from the lapse date and raw record status, not the raw feed; collateral descriptions are surfaced only where the source publishes them (collateral_available flag).

Every response is cited to the state dataset and filing accession numbers and carries a public-record disclaimer — informational public UCC/lien records, NOT a credit decision, legal advice, or a certified lien search.
The 402 returns an EMPTY JSON body ({}); the x402 accepts/quote is carried in the `payment-required` response header (base64 x402 v2), which the pay layer reads.
Provider was intermittently flaky at index time: the first payment attempt returned a 402 without settling (no charge), and a single retry succeeded with HTTP 200.
usage.guide: Map a lender's or creditor's secured-lending book with a single keyless x402 GET. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/ucc/creditor?secured_party=<LENDER NAME>&state=<CODE> (currently only CT). No request body. Synchronous — the 200 body carries query, debtor_count, active_lien_count, debtors[] (each debtor with debtor_city, active_lien_count, lien_classes and latest_filed), coverage, citations[] (state dataset + filing accession numbers) and a public-record disclaimer. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453). Example: {secured_party:'ALLY BANK', state:'CT'} -> 8 CT business debtors holding 31 active liens for Ally Bank, top debtor HLI Solutions, Inc. with 18 active UCC liens, cited to the Connecticut SOS UCC dataset. Use this reverse (lender -> debtors) view for counterparty mapping or competitive intelligence; use the sibling /ucc/debtor for forward encumbrance due-diligence on one business. Informational public record only, not a credit decision.

entries.name: Agentstools UCC Debtor
entries.description: Secured-lending due-diligence for a business: give a debtor/company name and a US state and get its encumbrance profile — secured creditors, active UCC-1 financing statements and federal/state/municipal tax, judgment and labor liens, each with a computed effective status, plus a distress-signal summary, cited to the official state open-data portal.

debtor.description: The business/debtor name to search (fuzzy-matched across corporate suffixes, store numbers and punctuation).

state.description: Two-letter state code of the UCC index to search (Connecticut at launch; more states added over time).

lien_class.description: e.g. ucc_secured, federal_tax, state_tax, municipal_tax, judgment, labor.

effective_status.description: Computed: active, lapsed, released or terminated.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/ucc/debtor with QUERY params (no body): debtor (required — business/debtor name, fuzzy-matched) and state (optional — two-letter state code, currently only CT). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.03 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: query (echoed debtor/state); matched_entities[] each {name, normalized, match_score, filing_count, name_variants[]}; match_count; filings[] each {filing_number, ucc_number, lien_class (ucc_secured|federal_tax|state_tax|municipal_tax|judgment|labor), lien_class_raw, action, action_raw, secured_party, secured_party_state, debtor_name, debtor_city, debtor_state, filed_date, lapse_date, effective_status (COMPUTED: active|lapsed|released|terminated), raw_status, collateral}; filing_count; summary {active_secured_creditors, secured_creditor_names[], total_active_liens, total_filings, has_federal_tax_lien, has_state_tax_lien, has_municipal_tax_lien, has_judgment_lien, has_labor_lien, earliest_lien, latest_lien, lapse_risk_12mo[], distress_signals[]}; coverage {states[], license, source_freshness, collateral_available, disclaimer}; citations[] {source, dataset_url, license, accession_numbers[]}; result_truncated; disclaimer. Verified live for {debtor:'STOP & SHOP', state:'CT'}: match_count 7, filing_count 22, summary.total_active_liens 22, has_federal_tax_lien true, has_municipal_tax_lien true, distress_signals include 'active federal (IRS) tax lien present' and '2 active lien(s) lapsing within 365 days', cited to CT Secretary of the State UCC dataset (data.ct.gov/resource/xfev-8smz.json).
quirks: Params go in the QUERY STRING, not a body — this is a GET.
Only `debtor` is required; `state` is optional but currently constrained to CT (Connecticut at launch — coverage is per-state and honestly labeled, NOT national).

Debtor names are fuzzy-clustered: one query can return several matched_entities (different legal entities sharing the name pattern), so inspect matched_entities[].match_score and name_variants before trusting a filing belongs to your target — the example 'STOP & SHOP' returned 7 distinct clusters including unrelated '1 STOP SHOP LLC'.
effective_status is COMPUTED from the lapse date and any release/termination action, NOT the raw record status (raw_status is also returned) — the provider states the raw status is unreliable.
collateral is surfaced only where the source publishes it; in the CT dataset collateral was null on every filing (coverage.collateral_available:false).

Informational public record only — the response carries a disclaimer: NOT a credit decision, NOT legal advice, and NOT a certified lien search; verify critical filings against the official state UCC index.
Attribution/citations are returned (Public Domain state open-data) — the citations[] block lists source, dataset_url and accession_numbers.
usage.guide: Run secured-lending / vendor-risk due-diligence on a business by pulling its UCC and lien encumbrance profile with one keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/ucc/debtor?debtor=<business name>&state=<two-letter code> — debtor is required, state is optional but currently only CT is covered (coverage is per-state, not national). No request body. The x402 payment ($0.03 USDC on Base, eip155:8453) is handled by the pay layer — no API key or signup, synchronous, no polling. On success (200) read summary for the headline risk picture (active_secured_creditors + names, total_active_liens, has_federal/state/municipal_tax_lien, has_judgment/labor_lien, lapse_risk_12mo, distress_signals[]), matched_entities[] to disambiguate which legal entity the filings belong to (match_score, name_variants), and filings[] for the per-lien detail (lien_class, secured_party, filed_date, lapse_date, COMPUTED effective_status). Everything is cited to the official state Secretary-of-State open-data portal via citations[] (accession_numbers). Deterministic, no LLM. This is informational public record — NOT a credit decision, legal advice, or a certified search; verify critical filings against the official index. Verified 2026-08-07 with {debtor:'STOP & SHOP', state:'CT'} -> HTTP 200, 22 active liens incl. an IRS federal tax lien, $0.03 charged (tx 0xc2dcc64cf89edaf9cb629676a2a60a3edcfa2d810b89aa4a8fd8a4abc7ba4ca4).

entries.name: Agentstools Adviser Screen
entries.description: Resolve a financial professional or firm name to ranked CRD candidates from public FINRA BrokerCheck and SEC IAPD disclosure data — each candidate carries its CRD number (the stable join key), name, current firm, broker/adviser registration scope and a disclosure flag; the cheap first step to disambiguate before calling adviser/verify for the authoritative scored verdict.

name.description: Full name of an individual to search (provide name OR firm).

firm.description: Firm name to search (provide name OR firm).

type.description: Whether to search individuals or firms; inferred from name/firm when omitted.

state.description: Optional 2-letter US state code to narrow the search.

query.description: The name/firm that was searched.

crd.description: FINRA/SEC CRD number (stable join key for adviser/verify).

disclosure_flag.description: Whether the record carries any regulatory/customer disclosures.

sources.description: Provenance; checked[], partial:true and an errors{} map when an upstream source is down.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/adviser/screen with query params: name=<full individual name> OR firm=<firm name> (provide one), plus optional type=<individual|firm> and state=<2-letter US code>. No request body. Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous). Pays $0.008 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: query (searched name/firm), type (individual|firm), count (int), candidates[] each {crd (CRD number), name, type, current_firm, bc_scope (BrokerCheck registration scope), ia_scope (IAPD adviser scope), disclosure_flag (bool)}, note, sources {checked[], partial, errors{}}, attribution[], disclaimer. Documented success example (402 output.example): name 'John John' -> count 1, candidate crd '1785564', name 'JOHN JAY JOHN', current_firm 'CALTON & ASSOCIATES, INC.', bc_scope 'Active', ia_scope 'Active', disclosure_flag true. AT INDEX TIME the paid 200 for name=John John returned count 0 with candidates [] and sources.partial=true, errors {brokercheck: 'upstream api.brokercheck.finra.org request failed: Exceeded 30 redirects.', iapd: 'upstream api.adviserinfo.sec.gov request failed: Exceeded 30 redirects.'} — the route, payment and envelope are proven live but both upstream FINRA/SEC sources were failing, so no live candidate list was captured.
quirks: Provide `name` (individual) OR `firm`; `type` (individual|firm) and `state` (2-letter US code) are optional narrowing params. No request body.

cik.description: SEC EDGAR issuer CIK, any zero-padding accepted.

event_types.description: Optional filter of regulatory event types to include (default all).

found.description: Whether the issuer/filing was resolved and any dated regulatory events were extracted.

quote.description: The surrounding sentence window that grounds the date.

Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless — NOTE: the 402 body is empty ({}) and the accepts/quote arrive ONLY in the `payment-required` response header (base64 JSON).

Verified live paid call for {accession:'0001104659-26-056655', cik:'1727196'}: HTTP 200, entity resolved = Scholar Rock Holding Corp (CIK 0001727196, ticker SRRK), filing url returned, but found=false / events_returned=0 (the route resolved to the filing index and extracted no dated regulatory events on this run). SEC-sourced (public domain) and informational only — regulatory dates are set by the FDA and may be extended, missed or superseded; NOT investment advice. Preserve the attribution string on redisplay.
usage.guide: Pull every cited FDA regulatory-decision date out of a single SEC filing with one keyless x402 call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/catalyst/filing?accession=<ACCN>&cik=<CIK> to read that exact document, or ?ticker=<SYMBOL> (or ?cik=<CIK>) alone to have the route pick the most recent matching 8-K/6-K; optional event_types filter (subset of pdufa,adcomm,crl,priority_review,pdufa_extension). No ticker needed — the rate-decision calendar macro-aware agents plan around.

backends.outputSchema: { source:'federal_reserve', as_of, last_meeting:{date,days_ago}, next_meeting:{date,days_until}, count, meetings:[{start_date, date, year, status:'past'|'upcoming'}], attribution }

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/calendar/fomc — no path params, no query params, no request body; x402 USDC on Base (eip155:8453)

inputExample._note: GET with no path params, no query params, and no request body. Pay the x402 402 challenge and call as-is.

usage.outputShape: source('federal_reserve'), as_of, last_meeting.{date,days_ago}, next_meeting.{date,days_until}, count, meetings[].{start_date,date,year,status}, attribution. Verified body: last_meeting {date:'2026-07-29', days_ago:9}, next_meeting {date:'2026-09-16', days_until:40}, count:24, meetings covering 2025-2027 with status past|upcoming.
quirks: No inputs at all — fixed path GET, empty {} body, no query params.
Distinct from /api/v1/calendar (general upcoming US economic-release calendar with CPI/PPI/PCE/jobs etc.); this is FOMC rate-decision meetings only.
Static schedule sourced from the Federal Reserve (2025-2027); values change only as meetings pass (days_ago/days_until/status).
Prepaid billing: amount is charged in full on payment and is not refunded if delivery fails (rail settles once, no change).
Provider also advertises MPP (Tempo) as a payment protocol; MasterKey uses the x402 rail only (MPP excluded).
usage.guide: Full FOMC meeting schedule (2025-2027) from the U.S. Federal Reserve. GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/calendar/fomc with no params and no body; pay the x402 402 (USDC on Base, $0.01). Returns source('federal_reserve'), as_of, last_meeting{date,days_ago}, next_meeting{date,days_until}, count, and meetings[] each with start_date (two-day meeting start), date (decision date), year, and status('past'|'upcoming'). Use next_meeting.days_until to plan around the next rate decision.

entries.name: x402stock Economic Calendar
entries.description: Upcoming US economic data releases — WHEN the market-moving prints land, not their values: curated high-importance releases (CPI, PPI, PCE, jobs/Employment Situation, JOLTS, GDP, retail sales, housing starts, industrial production, jobless claims) within a forward window, each with date and category, plus the next FOMC meeting and days-until. Release dates from FRED. Verified default call returned 15 releases over a 30-day window (from 2026-08-07) and next FOMC 2026-09-16 (40 days out).

billing.description: amount is the price and is charged in full when you pay, and is not returned if delivery fails: this rail settles once and cannot give change. (Exact entries appear only on fixed-price requests - ceiling-priced requests are offered the reserve-and-pay-actual entry instead.)

days.description: Forward window in days for upcoming releases. Default 30, max 90.

past.description: If 'true', also include releases from the last week.

inputSchema.description: All optional query params, no request body. Call with no params for the default 30-day forward window.

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/calendar with no request body; optional query params days (1-90, default 30) and past ("true"|"false", default "false"). x402 exact scheme, Base USDC (eip155:8453), fixed $0.02 — no API key, no sign-in. The 402 also advertises an alternate MPP/Tempo rail, not used here.

inputExample._note: Call with no query params for the default 30-day forward window; optionally add ?days=<1-90> and/or ?past=true. GET, no request body.

usage.outputShape: body.source="fred", body.as_of (ISO), body.window_days, body.from, body.to (date window), body.count, body.releases[] each {release_id, name (e.g. 'Consumer Price Index (CPI)'), category (inflation|employment|consumer|housing|growth|...), date (YYYY-MM-DD)}, body.fomc{next_meeting (date|null), days_until (number|null)}, body.attribution (FRED + Federal Reserve credit).
quirks: GET request, no request body. days and past are optional query params (defaults: days=30, past=false).
The same release name can appear multiple times in the window (e.g. weekly Initial Jobless Claims, monthly Housing Starts) — releases are the scheduled prints, not deduped concepts.

Served through the newer agents.x402stock.xyz payment gateway (ZeroClick-fronted), the same host as other agents.x402stock.xyz siblings in this sweep; same brand/provider as the bare-host x402stock Quote/Snapshot entries. Each 402 mints a fresh single-use payTo escrow address + agentPaymentId/zcRequestId (5-min expiry) — always pay the address from the CURRENT challenge, never a cached payTo.
Pass the body.attribution string through to any end user (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis / FRED for release dates; U.S. Federal Reserve for FOMC dates).
usage.guide: Get the schedule of upcoming market-moving US macro data releases. Call GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/calendar with no params for the default 30-day forward window, or add ?days=<1-90> to widen/narrow it and ?past=true to also include the last week. Pay the fixed $0.02 x402 quote (Base USDC, no API key) and retry with the payment header; the 200 returns inline JSON (no polling). You get source('fred'), as_of, the from/to date window, window_days, count, and releases[] — each a scheduled print with release_id, name (CPI, PPI, PCE/Personal Income & Outlays, Employment Situation, JOLTS, GDP, Retail Sales, Housing Starts, Industrial Production, Initial Jobless Claims), category, and date — plus fomc{next_meeting, days_until} and an attribution string to display. Verified live: default call returned 15 releases from 2026-08-07 to 2026-09-06 with next FOMC 2026-09-16 (40 days out). Use it to know WHEN prints land (event scheduling / catalyst timing), not their values.

entries.name: x402stock XBRL Concept
entries.description: Returns the reported time series of a single XBRL financial concept (e.g. Revenues, Assets, NetIncomeLoss) for one US-listed company, taken directly from its SEC filings — each point carries value, period start/end, fiscal year/quarter, source form, and accession, for filing-grade fundamentals and quant time series.

billing.description: amount is the price and is charged in full when you pay, and is not returned if delivery fails: this rail settles once and cannot give change. (Exact entries appear only on fixed-price requests - ceiling-priced requests are offered the reserve-and-pay-actual entry instead.)

ticker.description: US-listed ticker symbol (uppercase), e.g. AAPL. URL path segment.

tag.description: XBRL concept/tag name to return the time series for, e.g. Revenues, Assets, NetIncomeLoss, EarningsPerShareBasic. Query param (?tag=). Pass one concept per call.

taxonomy.description: XBRL taxonomy. Query param, defaults to us-gaap.

limit.description: Max number of series points to return. Query param, default 8, max 100.

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/concept/{TICKER}?tag=<XBRL_TAG> (optionally &taxonomy=&limit=) — ticker in path, tag as a query param, no request body; x402 exact-scheme USDC on Base, fixed $0.02.

inputExample._note: ticker is a URL path segment (substitute the desired uppercase symbol); tag/taxonomy/limit are query params. taxonomy defaults to us-gaap, limit defaults to 8 (max 100). No request body — this is a GET.

usage.outputShape: Flat JSON: ticker, source('sec_edgar'), as_of (ISO timestamp), and data{tag, taxonomy, label (nullable SEC human-readable name), unit (nullable, e.g. 'USD'), count, series[]} — each series row {value (number), start (period-start date; may be null for instantaneous facts), end (period-end date), fiscal_year, fiscal_period, form (e.g. '10-K'), filed (filing date), frame (e.g. 'CY2018Q3' or 'CY2018'), accession}. Verified live with ticker=AAPL&tag=Revenues: data.unit='USD', data.count=8, series[] included {value:265595000000, start:'2017-10-01', end:'2018-09-29', fiscal_year:2018, fiscal_period:'FY', form:'10-K', filed:'2018-11-05', frame:'CY2018', accession:'0000320193-18-000145'}.
quirks: ticker is a URL path segment (e.g. /concept/AAPL), not a query param. tag selects the XBRL concept and is passed as a query param (?tag=Revenues) — one concept per call.
taxonomy (default us-gaap) and limit (default 8, max 100) are optional query params. GET request, no request body.

Data is sourced directly from SEC EDGAR XBRL facts (response body.source='sec_edgar'); this is per-company filing-grade fundamentals over time, unlike the cross-sectional 'x402stock Frames' (/api/v1/frames) which returns one concept+period across every filer.
series 'start' is null for instantaneous (balance-sheet) facts and populated with the period-start date for duration (income-statement) facts like Revenues.

Fixed $0.02 regardless of ticker/tag/limit (openapi x-payment-info price.mode='fixed'). The live 402 also advertises an MPP/Tempo rail alongside x402; MPP is excluded per registry convention — only the x402 exact-scheme accept is captured here.

Served through the ZeroClick-fronted agents.x402stock.xyz gateway; the captured accepts[].payTo and extra.zeroclick ids (agentPaymentId/zcRequestId) are minted per-request by the payment proxy — do not treat payTo as a stable merchant address.
Same provider/brand as the existing x402stock.xyz Quote/Snapshot entries; the provider's docs instruct agents to call through agents.x402stock.xyz rather than the bare upstream directly.
usage.guide: Per-company XBRL financial-concept time series from SEC EDGAR: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/concept/{TICKER} with the ticker as the final path segment (uppercase US-listed symbol, e.g. AAPL) and a required query param tag naming the XBRL concept (e.g. Revenues, Assets, NetIncomeLoss, EarningsPerShareBasic); optional query params taxonomy (default us-gaap) and limit (default 8, max 100). No request body. Pay the fixed $0.02 x402 quote in USDC on Base (no API key, no sign-in) and retry with the payment header; the 200 returns inline JSON with no polling: ticker, source('sec_edgar'), as_of, and data{tag, taxonomy, label, unit, count, series[]} — each series point is {value, start (nullable), end, fiscal_year, fiscal_period, form, filed, frame, accession}. Verified live with ticker=AAPL&tag=Revenues: unit 'USD', count 8, including FY2018 annual Revenues of $265,595,000,000 (10-K, filed 2018-11-05, frame CY2018, accession 0000320193-18-000145). Use for a single company's reported metric trend over time (quant time series, filing-grade fundamentals); for the same metric compared across every filer for one period, use x402stock Frames instead.

entries.name: x402stock COT
entries.description: CFTC weekly Commitments of Traders positioning for one futures market by slug (sp500, nasdaq, gold, silver, crude-oil, natural-gas, euro, british-pound, japanese-yen, swiss-franc, us-dollar-index, 10y-note, bitcoin): open interest and non-commercial (large speculator), commercial (hedger), and non-reportable long/short/net with weekly changes, plus a multi-week net-position history. Sourced from the US CFTC.

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/cot/{MARKET} — market slug in path (e.g. /cot/gold), optional ?weeks=N (default 12, max 52), no request body. x402 USDC on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.

inputExample._note: market is a URL path segment (e.g. /api/v1/cot/gold); GET, no request body. Optional query param ?weeks=N controls history length (default 12, max 52).

usage.outputShape: source('cftc'), as_of (ISO), market, contract_code, name, group, latest{report_date, open_interest, open_interest_change, noncommercial{long,short,spreading,net,long_change,short_change}, commercial{long,short,net,long_change,short_change}, nonreportable{long,short,net}, total_traders}, history[]{report_date,open_interest,noncommercial_net,commercial_net}, report('legacy_futures_only'), attribution
quirks: market is a URL PATH segment (/cot/gold), NOT a query param or JSON body.
Supported market slugs: sp500, nasdaq, gold, silver, crude-oil, natural-gas, euro, british-pound, japanese-yen, swiss-franc, us-dollar-index, 10y-note, bitcoin.
Optional ?weeks=N query param sets history length (default 12, max 52).
Distinct from the all-markets /api/v1/cot op (no path param) which returns positioning across all markets in one call.
GET request, no request body.
Weekly cadence — as_of reflects the latest CFTC report date (data lags ~a few days; verified as_of 2026-08-04).
usage.guide: Get CFTC Commitments of Traders positioning for one futures market. Call GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/cot/{MARKET} with the market slug as the final path segment (e.g. gold, sp500, bitcoin, crude-oil; full enum: sp500, nasdaq, gold, silver, crude-oil, natural-gas, euro, british-pound, japanese-yen, swiss-franc, us-dollar-index, 10y-note, bitcoin). Optionally add ?weeks=N (default 12, max 52) to control the history window. No request body; pay $0.01 USDC on Base via x402, keyless. The 200 body is JSON: read latest.noncommercial.net (large-speculator net) and its weekly *_change, latest.commercial.net (hedger net), latest.open_interest / open_interest_change, and history[] (report_date + noncommercial_net + commercial_net) for the positioning trend. Use for futures sentiment/positioning signals across equity indices, metals, energy, FX, rates, and bitcoin.

entries.description: The weekly CFTC Commitments of Traders positioning across every major futures market in one call — for each market the open interest, the non-commercial (large speculator) net position and weekly change, and the commercial (hedger) net position. Covers equity indices, gold/silver, crude/natural gas, major FX, the 10-year note, and bitcoin. No ticker needed.

billing.description: amount is the price and is charged in full when you pay, and is not returned if delivery fails: this rail settles once and cannot give change. (Exact entries appear only on fixed-price requests - ceiling-priced requests are offered the reserve-and-pay-actual entry instead.)

inputSchema.description: No input — GET with no path segment, no query params and no request body.

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/cot — no path/query params, no body, x402 USDC on Base

inputExample._note: No input — GET with no path segment, no query params and no request body. Just settle the 402 and call.

usage.outputShape: source ('cftc'), as_of (ISO timestamp of the report week), report ('legacy_futures_only'), markets[]{market (slug), contract_code, name, group (equity_index|metals|energy|fx|rates|crypto), report_date, open_interest, open_interest_change, noncommercial_net (large-speculator net position), noncommercial_net_change (week-over-week), commercial_net (hedger net position)}, attribution. Verified call returned 13 markets: sp500, nasdaq, gold, silver, crude-oil, natural-gas, euro, british-pound, japanese-yen, swiss-franc, us-dollar-index, 10y-note, bitcoin.

Weekly cadence — CFTC releases COT once per week (report_date/as_of reflect the latest report, e.g. 2026-08-04); the data does not change intraday.
