Provider also advertises an MPP (tempo) payment rail on the same 402 challenge — excluded here; the served backend is x402 exact / Base USDC only.

extra.zeroclick agentPaymentId/zcRequestId in accepts are captured from one live 402 challenge and are per-request ephemeral identifiers — the x402 client should use the ids from its own fresh 402, not these.
usage.guide: Weekly CFTC Commitments of Traders positioning across every major futures market in one call. GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/cot — no params, no body; settle the x402 402 (USDC on Base, $0.02). Returns source, as_of, report, and a markets[] array where each entry carries the market slug, contract_code, human name, group (equity_index|metals|energy|fx|rates|crypto), report_date, open_interest (+ weekly change), noncommercial_net (large-speculator net position) with its weekly change, and commercial_net (hedger net position). Use it to read speculative vs hedger positioning and week-over-week shifts across S&P 500, Nasdaq, gold, silver, WTI crude, natural gas, EUR/GBP/JPY/CHF, the US Dollar Index, the 10-year Treasury note, and bitcoin — no ticker needed. Data updates weekly with the CFTC report.

entries.name: x402stock Dossier
entries.description: A US-listed company's recent SEC disclosure picture in one call by ticker: the recent filings index, Form 4 insider transactions with a net buy/sell signal, material 8-K events broken out by item code, and Form 3 initial holdings — sourced from SEC EDGAR with the CIK resolved once and shared across sections.

billing.description: amount is the price and is charged in full when you pay, and is not returned if delivery fails: this rail settles once and cannot give change. (Exact entries appear only on fixed-price requests - ceiling-priced requests are offered the reserve-and-pay-actual entry instead.)

ticker.description: US-listed ticker symbol (uppercase), a URL path segment (e.g. AAPL). No query params, no request body.

inputSchema.description: GET with the ticker as the final path segment. No query params and no request body (bazaar input schema: method GET, empty queryParams, pathParams.ticker).

sections.description: Per-section status map (e.g. {filings:'ok', insider_trades:'ok', material_events:'ok', form_3:'ok'}); sections degrade independently.

filings.description: { ticker, source, as_of, data:{ cik, company, count, filings:[{form,accession,filing_date,report_date,description,items[],primary_document,url}] } }

insider_trades.description: { ticker, source, as_of, data:{ filings_parsed, transaction_count, summary:{buys,sells,shares_bought,shares_sold,net_shares,signal}, transactions:[{owner_name,is_director,is_officer,officer_title,is_ten_percent_owner,filing_date,accession,url,security,transaction_date,code,code_label,shares,price_per_share,acquired_disposed,shares_owned_after,is_derivative}] } }

form_3.description: { ticker, source, as_of, data:{ filings_parsed, holding_count, holdings:[{owner_name,is_director,is_officer,officer_title,is_ten_percent_owner,filing_date,accession,url,security,shares,direct_or_indirect,nature_of_ownership,is_derivative,exercise_price,exercise_date,expiration_date,underlying_security,underlying_shares}] } }

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/dossier/:ticker with the uppercase ticker as the final path segment (e.g. /dossier/AAPL). No query params, no request body. x402 exact scheme, Base USDC (eip155:8453).

inputExample._note: ticker is a URL path segment, not a query param or JSON body; GET with no request body

usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON on the paid 200: { ticker:'AAPL', source:'x402stock', as_of:<ISO timestamp>, sections:{filings:'ok',insider_trades:'ok',material_events:'ok',form_3:'ok'}, filings:{data:{cik,company,count,filings:[{form,accession,filing_date,report_date,description,items[],primary_document,url}]}}, insider_trades:{data:{filings_parsed,transaction_count,summary:{buys,sells,shares_bought,shares_sold,net_shares,signal},transactions:[...]}}, material_events:{data:{count,events:[{form,accession,filing_date,report_date,url,items:[{code,label}]}]}}, form_3:{data:{filings_parsed,holding_count,holdings:[...]}} }. Verified live 2026-08-07 with ticker=AAPL -> HTTP 200 (Apple Inc., cik 0000320193, 20 filings, insider summary signal 'net_selling' net_shares -387752, 20 material events), $0.05 charged on Base.
quirks: Ticker is a path segment in the URL (e.g. /dossier/AAPL), not a query param or body. Substitute the desired uppercase US-listed symbol; the URL is templated as :ticker.
GET request, no request body (bazaar input schema allows GET/HEAD/DELETE; use GET).

One combined call resolves the CIK once and returns four SEC sections at a lower combined price than four separate calls; `sections` reports each section's status and sections degrade independently (a section may be null/error while others are 'ok').
insider_trades.data.summary.signal is a derived net buy/sell classification (e.g. 'net_selling') computed from Form 4 transactions.

Called through the agents.x402stock.xyz ZeroClick payment proxy — the x402 `payTo` address is minted fresh per request (do not treat it as a stable merchant address). Fixed price $0.05 (50000 atomic USDC), confirmed by the live 402 amount matching the charged cost.
Data is from SEC EDGAR; the internal service slug in the 402 zeroclick extension is 'sec-filings'.
usage.guide: Call GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/dossier/:ticker with the uppercase US ticker as the final path segment (e.g. AAPL, TSLA). No query params, no request body; pay the fixed $0.05 x402 quote (Base USDC, no API key) and retry with the payment header. The 200 returns a synchronous JSON SEC-disclosure dossier: read `filings.data.filings[]` for the recent filings index, `insider_trades.data.summary` (net_shares/signal) and `insider_trades.data.transactions[]` for Form 4 insider activity, `material_events.data.events[]` (with per-event 8-K item codes/labels) for material events, and `form_3.data.holdings[]` for initial holdings. Check `sections` for per-section status since sections degrade independently. No polling; no auth beyond the x402 payment.

entries.name: x402stock Energy Benchmark by Product
entries.description: Price history for one energy benchmark — WTI crude, Brent crude, Henry Hub natural gas, or US regular retail gasoline — with the latest value, prior reading, change, and recent daily history, sourced from the US EIA.

pathParams.product: one of wti | brent | natural-gas | gasoline

queryParams.limit: integer, default 30, max 365 — number of history points

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/energy/{product} where {product} is wti|brent|natural-gas|gasoline (e.g. /energy/wti), optional ?limit= query param, no body, x402 USDC on Base

inputExample._note: product is a URL path segment (wti | brent | natural-gas | gasoline), not a JSON body; this is a GET with no request body. Optionally append ?limit=N (default 30, max 365).

usage.outputShape: source('eia'), as_of (ISO), product, series_id, name, unit (e.g. usd_per_barrel), eia_units (e.g. $/BBL), frequency (e.g. daily), latest{date,value}, prior{date,value}, change, change_percent, history[]{date,value}, attribution
quirks: product is a path segment in the URL (e.g. /energy/wti), not a query param or body. Supported values: wti (WTI crude, $/bbl), brent (Brent crude, $/bbl), natural-gas (Henry Hub, $/MMBtu), gasoline (US regular retail, $/gal).
GET request, no request body.
Optional ?limit= query param controls how many recent history points are returned (default 30, max 365).
Units differ per product: WTI/Brent are $/barrel, natural-gas is $/MMBtu, gasoline is $/gallon — read unit/eia_units to interpret values.
Underlying source is the US Energy Information Administration (EIA); values are daily and point-in-time.
Provider also advertises an MPP (tempo) payment rail on this endpoint — excluded here; the served backend is x402 exact / Base USDC only.
usage.guide: Get price history for one energy benchmark in one call. GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/energy/{product} with product as the final path segment — wti (WTI crude, $/bbl), brent (Brent crude, $/bbl), natural-gas (Henry Hub, $/MMBtu), or gasoline (US regular retail, $/gal). Optionally add ?limit=N (default 30, max 365) to control history length. No request body; pay $0.01 USDC on Base via x402. Response is JSON: read latest{date,value} for the current price, prior{date,value} plus change/change_percent for the move, and history[]{date,value} for the recent series. unit/eia_units tell you the price unit; source is the US EIA.

entries.name: x402stock Energy Benchmarks (All)

billing.description: amount is the price and is charged in full when you pay, and is not returned if delivery fails: this rail settles once and cannot give change.

inputSchema.description: No parameters — GET with an empty query and no request body returns every energy benchmark.

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/energy — no query params, no request body, x402 USDC exact on Base (agents.x402stock.xyz is x402stock's own agent-facing payment gateway; it mirrors the upstream x402stock.xyz paths 1:1 and proxies through after payment).
usage.outputShape: source ('eia'), as_of, series ('energy_prices'), products[].{product, series_id, name, unit, eia_units, frequency, latest{date,value}, prior{date,value}, change, change_percent}, attribution
quirks: Takes NO input — plain GET with an empty query and no body returns all four benchmarks (wti, brent, natural-gas, gasoline). This is the aggregate feed; for one benchmark with history use the sibling /api/v1/energy/{product}, which is a separate service.
Flat $0.02 per request (x402 exact, Base USDC), independent of how many products are returned.

Data is sourced from the U.S. EIA. WTI/Brent are in usd_per_barrel, natural-gas in usd_per_mmbtu, gasoline in usd_per_gallon; gasoline is a weekly series while the oil/gas series are daily, so their 'prior' dates differ.

agents.x402stock.xyz is a payment-gateway (ZeroClick) proxy in front of x402stock.xyz, not a separate provider — same brand/dataset (serviceName 'x402stock' in the 402, source 'eia' in the body). The captured payTo (0xc433838e597191b3a829b304d56615b9e68d890a) is the gateway's recipient at index time and may rotate per request.
The live 402 also advertises an MPP/Tempo payment rail (protocols.mpp, method 'tempo') alongside x402 — only the x402 (Base USDC, exact) offer is indexed here, per registry policy of excluding MPP.
The 402's zeroclick block also mentions an optional plan/identity-credential (Bearer) path for buying a plan; pay-as-you-go needs no registration — settling the x402 challenge directly is sufficient.

entries.name: x402stock Exchange Rates

Accounting-grade / reference conversion (incl. exotic currencies) rather than live market FX. Optional ?currency= filter. entries.description: Current and resolved US drug shortages from openFDA, newest update first — one call for the whole market or narrowed to a single manufacturer via ?company=. Each entry carries the generic name, manufacturer, status (Current/Resolved), therapeutic category, dosage form, presentation (with NDC), posting/update dates, update type, and reason. A supply-side catalyst signal for generic drugmakers. Verified market-wide call: total_matched 1651, 20 items returned (e.g. Etomidate Injection, Mylan Institutional / Viatris, status Current).

billing.description: amount is the price and is charged in full when you pay, and is not returned if delivery fails: this rail settles once and cannot give change. (Exact entries appear only on fixed-price requests - ceiling-priced requests are offered the reserve-and-pay-actual entry instead.)

company.description: Optional manufacturer/company name to narrow to one maker (e.g. 'Pfizer'). Omit for a market-wide shortage feed.

limit.description: Max shortage items returned (default 20, max 100). total_matched is the true openFDA match count regardless of limit.

inputSchema.description: All optional query params, no request body. Call with no params for the full market-wide feed.

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/fda/shortages[?company=<name>][&limit=1-100] — both query params optional; omit company for a market-wide feed, add company (free-text, 2-120 chars) to narrow to one manufacturer. limit defaults to 20 (max 100). No request body. x402 exact scheme, Base USDC (eip155:8453) — this endpoint's 402 also advertises an alternate MPP/Tempo rail, not used here.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous flat JSON on the paid 200: { source:'fda' (const), as_of:<ISO timestamp>, company:<string|null> (null for a market-wide call), total_matched:<true openFDA match count>, count:<items returned, capped by limit>, shortages:[{ generic_name, company_name, status ('Current'|'Resolved'), therapeutic_category:[<string>], dosage_form, presentation (drug + strength + NDC), posted_date, updated_date, update_type (e.g. 'Reverified'), reason (nullable, e.g. 'Estimated recovery: Q4 2026') }], attribution:'Source: openFDA, U.S. Food and Drug Administration' }. Verified market-wide: total_matched 1651, count 20.
quirks: Both params are OPTIONAL — calling with no params returns the full market-wide shortage feed (verified: total_matched 1651, 20 items). company (2-120 chars) is a fuzzy match against the manufacturer/company name.
`limit` defaults to 20 (NOT 10) and caps at 100; count/shortages.length is capped by limit, but total_matched is the true openFDA match count regardless.

Per-item `reason` is often null (e.g. reverified 'Current' entries); when present it can carry an estimated recovery quarter (e.g. 'Estimated recovery: Q4 2026'). therapeutic_category is an array that can hold many categories for one drug.

This is the drug-SHORTAGES feed (/fda/shortages) — distinct from the sibling 'x402stock FDA Catalysts' (/fda), which returns per-company recalls/approvals/clearances across 5 openFDA datasets. Different path, different dataset.

Served through the newer `agents.x402stock.xyz` payment gateway — a different host from the existing 'x402stock Quote'/'x402stock Snapshot' entries (bare x402stock.xyz), but the same brand/provider (serviceName:'x402stock', source:'fda' in the body).

Like sibling agents.x402stock.xyz endpoints, the 402's accepts[].payTo and extra.zeroclick ids (agentPaymentId/zcRequestId) are minted per-request by the payment proxy — do not treat payTo as a stable merchant address; always pay whatever the live 402 quotes.
Fixed price ($0.02): the live 402 quoted 20000 atomic units (eip155:8453 USDC) and the paid amount matched exactly; the challenge also carries zeroclick.info.payment.amountUsd '0.020000'.
Dual payment rails advertised on the same 402: x402 (Base USDC, scheme exact — what was paid) and MPP/Tempo (also USDC) via a separate challenge; MasterKey uses only the x402 accept.
usage.guide: Call GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/fda/shortages with no params for a market-wide US drug-shortage feed, or add ?company=<manufacturer name> (free-text, 2-120 chars, e.g. 'Pfizer' or 'Mylan') to narrow to one maker, plus optional &limit=1-100 (default 20). Pay the fixed $0.02 x402 quote (Base USDC, no API key) and retry with the payment header. The 200 returns a synchronous JSON snapshot from openFDA: source, as_of, company (null when market-wide), total_matched (true match count), count, and shortages[] — each with generic_name, company_name, status (Current/Resolved), therapeutic_category[], dosage_form, presentation (drug + strength + NDC), posted_date/updated_date, update_type, and a nullable reason (sometimes an estimated recovery quarter) — plus an openFDA attribution string to pass through. No polling. Use it as a supply-side catalyst signal for generic drugmakers or to monitor drug-supply risk by manufacturer.

entries.name: x402stock FRED
entries.description: Pull a key market-signal macro series from the U.S. Federal Reserve (FRED) by slug — VIX, yield-curve spreads (10y-2y, 10y-3m), credit spreads (high-yield, IG), 10y breakeven/real yield, jobless claims, consumer sentiment, 30y mortgage rate, financial conditions, and recession probability — or any raw FRED series ID (e.g. DGS10). Each call returns the latest value, prior, absolute + percent change, year-over-year, and ~24 points of recent history in one synchronous x402 call. Verified call :series=vix returned series_id VIXCLS ('CBOE Volatility Index (VIX)', unit index, daily) latest {2026-08-06, 15.15}, prior {2026-08-05, 15.81}, change -0.66, change_percent -4.17, yoy_percent null, plus a 24-point daily history.

billing.description: amount is the price and is charged in full when you pay, and is not returned if delivery fails: this rail settles once and cannot give change. (Exact entries appear only on fixed-price requests - ceiling-priced requests are offered the reserve-and-pay-actual entry instead.)

series.description: FRED series, as a path segment. Either a friendly slug — vix, yield-curve-10y-2y, yield-curve-10y-3m, high-yield-spread, ig-spread, breakeven-10y, real-yield-10y, jobless-claims, consumer-sentiment, mortgage-30y, financial-conditions, recession-probability — or a raw FRED series ID such as DGS10 (10-year Treasury) or VIXCLS.

inputSchema.description: Single path parameter (:series). No query params, no request body.

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/fred/:series — the FRED series goes in the PATH (a friendly slug like 'vix' or a raw FRED series ID like 'DGS10'). No query params, no request body. x402 exact scheme, Base USDC (eip155:8453). The 402 also advertises an alternate MPP/Tempo rail (currency 0x20C0...b9537d11c60E8b50, method 'tempo') — not used here.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous flat JSON on the paid 200: { source:'fred' (const), as_of:<ISO timestamp>, series_id:'VIXCLS', title:'CBOE Volatility Index (VIX)', unit:'index', frequency:'daily', latest:{date,value}|null, prior:{date,value}|null, change:number|null, change_percent:number|null, yoy_percent:number|null, history:[{date,value}] (recent points, ~24 for the daily vix series, newest first) }. Verified for :series=vix: latest {2026-08-06, 15.15}, prior {2026-08-05, 15.81}, change -0.66, change_percent -4.17, yoy_percent null.
quirks: :series accepts BOTH a curated friendly slug (vix, yield-curve-10y-2y, yield-curve-10y-3m, high-yield-spread, ig-spread, breakeven-10y, real-yield-10y, jobless-claims, consumer-sentiment, mortgage-30y, financial-conditions, recession-probability) AND a raw FRED series ID (e.g. DGS10, VIXCLS) — the OpenAPI path example is 'DGS10' while the summary lists the slugs; the verified slug 'vix' resolved to series_id 'VIXCLS'.
One templated service, not one-per-series: the path segment is the only input. Substitute the series you want at call time.

yoy_percent can be null (was null for the daily vix series); change/change_percent/latest/prior are also nullable. history length and frequency vary by series (daily for vix; weekly/monthly for others).

Served through the newer agents.x402stock.xyz payment gateway — same brand/provider as the bare x402stock.xyz entries; per its own openapi it is a transparent proxy in front of x402stock's upstream API.

The 402's accepts[].payTo and extra.zeroclick ids (agentPaymentId/zcRequestId) are minted per-request by the payment proxy — do not treat payTo as a stable merchant address; always re-quote from a fresh 402 at call time.
Fixed price ($0.01, per OpenAPI x-payment-info.price.mode:'fixed'); the live 402 (amount '10000' atomic USDC) and the paid amount matched exactly — not a ceiling/dynamic quote.
Distinct from the existing 'FRED Macro' registry entry, which is a different provider (Heurist Mesh FredMacroAgent on mesh.heurist.xyz, POST-based) serving the same public FRED data — not merged.
usage.guide: Get a key U.S. macro / market-signal series straight from FRED, no ticker or API key needed. Call GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/fred/:series with the series in the path — use a friendly slug (vix, yield-curve-10y-2y, yield-curve-10y-3m, high-yield-spread, ig-spread, breakeven-10y, real-yield-10y, jobless-claims, consumer-sentiment, mortgage-30y, financial-conditions, recession-probability) or a raw FRED series ID like DGS10. Pay the fixed $0.01 x402 quote (Base USDC, exact scheme) and retry with the payment header; the result is inline in the 200 (no polling). You get source, as_of, series_id, title, unit, frequency, the latest and prior {date,value}, absolute + percent change, year-over-year percent (may be null), and a recent history array — ideal for a fast macro/rates/volatility snapshot in stock or crypto research.

Payment for the API call is USDC on Base even though the underlying token it describes is a Solana SPL token (contract_address is a Solana mint, e.g. 'Pren1FvFX6J3E4kXhJuCiAD5aDmGEb7qJRncwA8Lkhw') — two different chains for two different purposes.

entries.name: x402stock Factor Score
entries.description: Transparent quant factor score for a US stock by ticker: Value (P/E, P/S, P/B), Quality (ROE, margins, leverage), Growth (YoY revenue & earnings) and Momentum (trailing return), each 0-100 from filing-grade fundamentals, plus an equal-weighted composite — every underlying metric returned with a label.

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/score/factors/:ticker with the :ticker path segment substituted by an uppercase US-listed symbol (e.g. AAPL) — no query params, no request body. First call returns HTTP 402 with a signed x402/MPP challenge; settling the x402 challenge (scheme exact, Base USDC) returns HTTP 200 with the score inline (synchronous, no polling). Called through x402stock's agents.x402stock.xyz agent-facing payment proxy in front of its upstream API; same provider/brand as the existing x402stock Quote/Snapshot entries.

inputExample._note: :ticker is the only input — substitute an uppercase US-listed ticker symbol (e.g. AAPL, MSFT, TSLA). No query params or request body.

usage.outputShape: Flat JSON: ticker, source('x402stock'), as_of (ISO timestamp), sections.{financials,price,price_history,profile} ('ok' health flags), composite.{value(0-100),max(100),label,confidence}, factors.{value,quality,growth,momentum} — each with score(0-100, nullable), label (e.g. weak/above_average/strong) and a metrics object (value: pe,ps,pb; quality: roe,gross_margin,net_margin,debt_to_equity; growth: revenue_growth_yoy,earnings_growth_yoy; momentum: trailing_return,above_mean), methodology (string), inputs.{market_cap,price,fiscal_year,revenue,net_income,equity}, disclaimer. Verified live call for AAPL returned composite.value 61.7 (above_average), value 26.7 (weak), quality 81.3 (strong), growth 64 (above_average), momentum 75 (strong).
quirks: :ticker is a required path segment (not a query param); a bare /score/factors with no ticker will not resolve. Substitute an uppercase US-listed symbol.

Per-factor score is nullable (anyOf number|null) — a factor whose underlying fundamentals are unavailable can come back null, and composite is the mean of only the AVAILABLE factors (composite.confidence reflects coverage).

Scores are absolute-threshold based, NOT cross-sectional percentiles (per the response's methodology field): each factor is 0-100 from fixed thresholds, so a 'weak' Value simply means expensive multiples, not a rank vs peers.
Inputs are delayed/periodic filing-grade fundamentals (the response carries fiscal_year and a disclaimer) — factual quantitative analysis, explicitly not investment advice.

The x402 payTo address and extra.zeroclick agentPaymentId/zcRequestId nonces rotate on every fresh 402 (per-challenge billing metadata) — always settle whatever the live 402 quotes rather than hardcoding this recorded payTo.

Response also advertises an MPP (Tempo USDC) settlement path alongside x402 (Base USDC); only the x402 rail was exercised for this index. Fixed price $0.15 (meterSlug score_factors) per the live 402 and provider OpenAPI x-payment-info.

The x402 payTo is minted fresh per request by the agents.x402stock.xyz pay-per-use proxy (captured 0xefae579e...c3a7311b) — don't treat it as a stable merchant address; always pay whatever the live 402 quotes.

The live 402 also advertises an MPP/Tempo rail (www-authenticate: Payment method="tempo", currency 0x20C0...E8b50) alongside x402 — only the x402 (Base USDC, exact scheme) accept is captured here, per registry policy of excluding MPP.
usage.guide: Get a one-shot macroeconomic snapshot for any country with GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/world-bank/country/:iso, substituting :iso with a 2- or 3-letter ISO country code (e.g. US, CN, IN, DE). No query params or request body. Pay the fixed $0.02 x402 quote (Base USDC, no API key, no sign-in) and retry with the payment header. The 200 returns a synchronous JSON profile with the country identity and an `indicators` array of the latest values for 10 headline World Bank World Development Indicators: GDP, GDP growth, GDP per capita, inflation, unemployment, population, government debt (% GDP), current account (% GDP), exports (% GDP), and FDI (% GDP) — each with its WDI code, human-readable name, and { year, value } (or null if unavailable). Covers international macro that the US-only FRED/BLS endpoints don't. Annual data, not real-time; no polling.

entries.name: x402stock xStock by Ticker
entries.description: Track one tokenized US equity (xStock) by symbol (e.g. AAPLx) or underlying ticker (e.g. AAPL): its on-chain Raydium CLMM pool price decoded from the public Solana ledger, the per-share price after the Token-2022 scaled-UI multiplier, the real underlying's live quote, and the premium/discount percent between them.

billing.description: amount is the price and is charged in full when you pay, and is not returned if delivery fails: this rail settles once and cannot give change. (Exact entries appear only on fixed-price requests - ceiling-priced requests are offered the reserve-and-pay-actual entry instead.)

ticker.description: xStock symbol (e.g. AAPLx) or underlying US-equity ticker (e.g. AAPL). List every tracked symbol via the bare /api/v1/xstocks endpoint.

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/xstocks/{ticker} where {ticker} is the final path segment (e.g. /AAPL or /AAPLx) — no query params, no request body. First call returns HTTP 402 with a signed x402 challenge (this host also advertises an MPP/Tempo option); settle the x402 challenge (scheme exact, Base USDC, eip155:8453) and retry to get HTTP 200 with the data inline. agents.x402stock.xyz is x402stock's identity/payment/proxy front door for the upstream x402stock.xyz API.

inputExample._note: ticker is the final URL path segment, not a query param or body; this is a GET with no request body. Accepts either the xStock symbol (AAPLx) or the underlying ticker (AAPL).

usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON on the paid 200: { source:'x402stock', as_of:<ISO>, venue:'solana', protocol:'raydium-clmm', program:<pool-program pubkey>, note:<method note>, us_market_open:<bool|null>, sections:{onchain,underlying}, item:{ symbol (e.g. AAPLx), underlying (e.g. AAPL), pool, mint, xstock_price_usd, pool_price_raw_unit, multiplier (Token-2022 scaled-UI), liquidity, tick_current, underlying_price_usd, underlying_change_percent, underlying_market_status, premium_percent } }. Verified AAPL call returned xstock_price_usd 313.265706, underlying_price_usd 313.08, premium_percent 0.0593.
quirks: Path-param service: {ticker} is a single URL path segment; substitute the desired symbol per call (do NOT create one service per ticker). The bare /api/v1/xstocks endpoint (indexed separately as 'x402stock xStocks', $0.04) lists every tracked symbol.
Accepts both the xStock symbol (AAPLx) and the plain underlying ticker (AAPL) — the response `item.symbol` is the xStock symbol and `item.underlying` the real ticker.
Fixed price $0.02 (meterSlug 'xstocks_ticker', 20000 atomic USDC units) — not a dynamic/ceiling quote; confirmed by the openapi x-payment-info (mode:'fixed') and the live 402.

The x402 payTo address is minted fresh per request by the ZeroClick proxy (differs between probes seconds apart) — do not treat it as a stable merchant address; always settle against the payTo in the live 402.

On-chain prices are decoded from Raydium CLMM pool state (sqrt_price_x64) on Solana — NOT from Backed/xStocks, Chainlink, or Pyth. The AMM price is arb-anchored to the underlying only while US markets are open (us_market_open); off-hours it is standing 24/7 price discovery.
Underlying fields can be null when sections.underlying is 'unavailable'.
usage.guide: Call GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/xstocks/{TICKER} with the symbol as the final path segment (e.g. /AAPL, /TSLAx). No request body; pay the fixed $0.02 x402 quote (Base USDC, no API key/signup) and retry with the payment header. The 200 returns synchronous JSON: read item.xstock_price_usd for the tokenized on-chain price, item.underlying_price_usd for the real underlying quote, and item.premium_percent for the premium/discount between them — use it to spot arbitrage/mispricing on a single tokenized equity, or item.liquidity/item.tick_current for that xStock's Raydium pool health. Use the bare /api/v1/xstocks endpoint instead when you want all tracked xStocks at once.

entries.name: Greeneris US SEC Fundamentals
entries.description: As-filed XBRL financial fundamentals for any SEC-registered US company, straight from the SEC EDGAR companyconcept API — look up a single XBRL concept (e.g. Revenues, Assets, NetIncomeLoss) by CIK and get the most recent as-filed facts with period, value, fiscal year/period, form type and filing date, grouped by unit. Keyless pay-per-call over x402. $0.01.

cik.description: SEC Central Index Key, 1-10 digits (e.g. 320193 = Apple Inc.)

tag.description: XBRL concept, e.g. Revenues, Assets, NetIncomeLoss, EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding

taxonomy.description: XBRL taxonomy (default us-gaap; use dei for entity/document concepts)

limit.description: Most recent facts to return per unit, 1-40 (default 8)

outputSchema.description: { ok, data: { cik (number), entity, taxonomy, tag, label, units: { <UNIT e.g. USD|shares>: [{ start, end, value (number), fy (number), fp, form, filed }] }, source } }

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/us/sec-fundamentals?cik=<CIK>&tag=<XBRLConcept>&taxonomy=<us-gaap|dei>&limit=<1-40>. One x402 payment (Base USDC), no API key, no account. Result inline in the 200 body under data.units.
usage.outputShape: JSON: { ok, data: { cik, entity, taxonomy, tag, label, units: { USD: [{ start, end, value, fy, fp ('FY'|'Q1'..), form ('10-K'|'10-Q'..), filed }], shares?: [...] }, source } }. Example: cik 320193 -> entity 'Apple Inc.', tag Revenues, units.USD[0] = { start:'2017-10-01', end:'2018-09-29', value:265595000000, fy:2018, fp:'FY', form:'10-K', filed:'2018-11-05' }.
quirks: cik and tag are BOTH required — calling with no params returns HTTP 402 with an empty {} body (that empty body is NOT a documented input).
cik is the SEC Central Index Key (1-10 digits), e.g. 320193 = Apple Inc.; the CIK is not the ticker — look it up via SEC EDGAR if you only have a ticker.
tag is a single XBRL concept name (case-sensitive), e.g. Revenues, Assets, NetIncomeLoss, EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding — one concept per call.
taxonomy defaults to us-gaap; use dei for document/entity-level concepts (e.g. EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding).
limit is passed as a string, 1-40 (default 8), and caps the most-recent facts returned per unit.
Facts are grouped by unit (USD, shares, USD-per-shares, etc.); each fact carries the reporting period (start/end), fiscal year (fy) + period (fp), source form (10-K/10-Q) and filing date (filed).
Source is the SEC EDGAR XBRL companyconcept API (US federal data, public domain); served with a 12h cache, updated as filings are accepted.
US SEC-registered companies only; part of the provider's eu-verify data family (fi/company, us-debt, us-treasury-rates, etc.).
usage.guide: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/us/sec-fundamentals?cik=<CIK>&tag=<XBRLConcept>. Pass cik as the SEC Central Index Key (e.g. 320193 for Apple Inc. — not the ticker) and tag as a single XBRL concept name (Revenues, Assets, NetIncomeLoss, EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, ...). Optionally set taxonomy (us-gaap default, or dei for entity/document concepts) and limit (1-40, default 8) for how many most-recent facts per unit. Pure x402 (Base USDC, no API key). Read data.units[<UNIT>][] for the as-filed facts, each with period, value, fiscal year/period, form and filing date.

entries.name: Strale Credit Score Band
entries.description: Interprets and converts a credit score across scoring systems (FICO, VantageScore, Experian, Equifax), mapping it to a universal risk band with a percentile estimate and next-band threshold.

system.description: Scoring system: fico, vantagescore, experian, equifax (default: fico)

usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/credit-score-band?score=720&system=fico (required query param: score = credit score value; optional query param: system = fico|vantagescore|experian|equifax, default fico); x402 USDC on Base
usage.outputShape: { score, system, system_name, band, universal_risk_level, percentile_estimate, typical_characteristics, next_band_name, next_band_threshold, points_to_next, score_range:{min,max} }; provenance/payment under body._meta (capability, provenance.source='strale-credit-reference', payment.settlement_id/price_usd). Verified: score=720 system=fico -> band 'Good', universal_risk_level 'moderate', percentile_estimate '40-59th', next_band_name 'Very Good', next_band_threshold 740, points_to_next 20, score_range {min:300,max:850}.
quirks: `score` is a required query param (number); `system` is an optional query param, one of fico|vantagescore|experian|equifax (default fico).
Interpretation only — this is a reference mapping (source 'strale-credit-reference'), not a bureau pull of a real person's credit; no PII/identity input.
score_range reflects the selected system's valid range (e.g. FICO 300-850).
Provenance and settlement metadata are returned under body._meta.
usage.guide: Interpret/convert a credit score across scoring systems. Make a GET request to https://api.strale.io/x402/credit-score-band with required query param `score` (the numeric credit score) and optional `system` (fico, vantagescore, experian, or equifax; defaults to fico), e.g. ?score=720&system=fico. Pay the fixed $0.0216 x402 quote (USDC on Base, no API key) and retry with the payment header. The 200 returns plain JSON: read body.band for the risk band, body.universal_risk_level and body.percentile_estimate for the risk interpretation, and body.next_band_name/next_band_threshold/points_to_next for progress to the next band. Payment/provenance are under body._meta.

entries.name: Strale Currency Convert
entries.description: Convert an amount between two fiat currencies using ECB reference exchange rates, returning the converted amount and rate — pay-per-call over x402 (USDC on Base), no API key.

inputSchema.amount: number (query param, required) — the quantity of the FROM currency to convert
inputSchema.from: string (query param, required) — source currency ISO 4217 code (e.g. USD)
inputSchema.to: string (query param, required) — target currency ISO 4217 code (e.g. EUR)

usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/currency-convert?amount=100&from=USD&to=EUR (three required query params: amount=number, from=ISO4217, to=ISO4217; no body). Pay the fixed x402 quote (~$0.0216 USDC on Base) and retry with the payment header. Result JSON is inline in the 200.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous flat JSON from the paid 200: { amount:100, from:'USD', to:'EUR', converted_amount:86.69, rate:0.866927, date:'2026-08-07', _meta:{ capability, latency_ms, provenance:{source:'ecb.europa.eu', fetched_at}, payment:{method,settlement_id,price_usd} } }. converted_amount = amount * rate; rate = 1 FROM in TO.
quirks: All three params (amount, from, to) are query params and required — never a body; the 402 outputSchema.input marks method GET with queryParams {amount,from,to} all required.

Rates are ECB reference rates (source: ecb.europa.eu), published once per working day (~16:00 CET) — not a live/intraday tradable FX feed; `date` reflects the ECB business day and may lag on weekends/holidays.
Fixed price ($0.0216 = 21600 atomic USDC in the live 402 accept), not a dynamic per-request quote.
Single accept: Base (network 'base') USDC only — no Solana leg advertised.
Payment/provenance metadata is returned under body._meta (settlement_id = the x402 tx hash).
usage.guide: Convert a fiat amount between two currencies at ECB reference rates in one paid call. Issue a plain GET to https://api.strale.io/x402/currency-convert with three required query params — amount (number), from (ISO 4217, e.g. USD), to (ISO 4217, e.g. EUR) — and no body, then pay the fixed x402 quote (~$0.0216 USDC on Base, no API key) and retry with the payment header. On the 200, read body.converted_amount for the result and body.rate for the applied rate (1 FROM in TO); body.date is the ECB reference date. Synchronous — no polling. Note: ECB reference rates update once per working day, so this is not an intraday tradable quote.

entries.name: Strale Exchange Rate
entries.description: Current exchange rate between two ISO 4217 currencies using European Central Bank (ECB) reference data. Returns the rate, the inverse rate, and the reference date.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/exchange-rate?from=USD&to=EUR (required query params: from = source ISO 4217 currency, to = target ISO 4217 currency); x402 USDC on Base
usage.outputShape: { from, to, rate (number: 1 unit of `from` in `to`), inverse_rate (number), date (YYYY-MM-DD ECB reference date) }; provenance/payment under body._meta (capability, latency_ms, provenance.source='ecb.europa.eu', payment.settlement_id/price_usd). Verified: from=USD to=EUR -> rate 0.866927, inverse_rate 1.1535, date 2026-08-07.
quirks: Both `from` and `to` are required ISO 4217 currency codes passed as query params.
Rates are ECB reference rates (once-daily reference, not live intraday market FX).
`rate` is 1 unit of `from` expressed in `to`; `inverse_rate` is the reciprocal.
Provenance and settlement metadata are returned under body._meta.
usage.guide: Get the current ECB reference exchange rate between two currencies. Make a GET request to https://api.strale.io/x402/exchange-rate with required query params `from` and `to` set to ISO 4217 codes (e.g. ?from=USD&to=EUR). Pay the fixed $0.0216 x402 quote (USDC on Base, no API key) and retry with the payment header. The 200 returns plain JSON: read body.rate for 1 `from` in `to`, body.inverse_rate for the reciprocal, and body.date for the ECB reference date. Payment/provenance are under body._meta.
